title: flag.ExitOnError bypasses error handling in CLI flag parsing
description:
At internal/cli/app.go:79, the FlagSet uses flag.ExitOnError:

    fs := flag.NewFlagSet("infomunge", flag.ExitOnError)

This causes os.Exit(2) on flag parsing errors, bypassing the normal error handling flow in main(). This makes it impossible to test flag parsing error paths and prevents graceful error reporting.

Fix: change to flag.ContinueOnError and handle the error from fs.Parse() explicitly:

    fs := flag.NewFlagSet("infomunge", flag.ContinueOnError)
    if err := fs.Parse(args); err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }

title: Separate declaration parsing from declaration evaluation
description:
Problem:
Header and module declaration parsing currently parses syntax and evaluates declarations in the runner. Variable parsing calls the preprocessor and evaluator immediately; function parsing parses Go AST bodies; type/property parsing returns evaluator types; module parsing updates both a typed namespace and raw eval context.

Why it matters:
This couples header syntax, module loading, preprocessing, evaluator internals, and scope mutation. It makes it hard to validate declarations independently, reuse parsing in tooling, or reason about import cycles and declaration ordering without executing expressions.

Evidence:
- `internal/runner/declarations.go` imports evaluator, preprocessor, sourcemap, and go/parser.
- `parseVarDeclFromLinesWithGoContext` preprocesses and evaluates variable expressions.
- `buildFunLambda` preprocesses and parses the function body AST directly.
- `internal/runner/module_parser.go` mutates `rawNs` while constructing `Namespace` entries.

Suggested direction:
Introduce a declaration AST/IR for headers and modules. Parsing should produce version/output/input/import/var/fun/type declarations with source spans. A later binder/evaluator phase should resolve imports and evaluate declarations into a scope.

Acceptance:
- Header/module declaration parsing can be unit-tested without evaluator side effects.
- Module and script headers share the same declaration IR.
- Existing import/var/fun/type behavior remains covered by runner/module cucumber or Go tests.

title: Replace preprocessor mapping invariant panic with recoverable error path
description:
The preprocessor rewriter uses a hard panic in invariant checking, which can terminate the process if any internal mapping drift occurs.

Evidence:
- `internal/preprocessor/preprocessor.go:111`
  - `panic(fmt.Sprintf("mapping invariant violated ..."))`

Why this is significant:
- Even if this is intended as a programming-error detector, panics at this layer can take down CLI/server requests instead of surfacing an actionable parse/runtime error.
- A single malformed internal state should not crash the entire process in production paths.

Proposed fix:
- Replace the panic path with structured error propagation (or guard with recover in the top-level preprocessing/evaluation boundary).
- Preserve invariant details in error context for debugging.
- Add a regression test that validates invariant failures are reported as errors, not panics.

title: Align match matches and scan with DataWeave regex semantics
description:
The supported `match`, `matches`, and `scan` operations use Go substring-search behavior and omit the full match from returned capture arrays, producing results that disagree with their documented DataWeave model.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision, compared with DataWeave CLI 2.11.0:
- `matches("hello world", "l")` returns `true`; expected `false` because the whole input does not match.
- `"ba" matches /a$/` returns `true`; expected `false`.
- `match("foo123bar", /([a-z]+)([0-9]+)/)` returns `["foo","123"]`; expected `[]` because the whole input does not match.
- `match("foo123", /([a-z]+)([0-9]+)/)` returns `["foo","123"]`; expected `["foo123","foo","123"]`.
- `scan("abc123def", /[0-9]+/)` returns `["123"]`; expected `[["123"]]`.
- `scan("foo1 bar2", /([a-z]+)([0-9])/)` returns `[["foo","1"],["bar","2"]]`; expected `[["foo1","foo","1"],["bar2","bar","2"]]`.

Likely source:
- `callBuiltinMatches` calls `regexp.MatchString`, which succeeds on substrings despite the code comment saying the entire string is checked.
- `callBuiltinMatch` also uses substring search and returns `matches[1:]`, dropping the full match.
- `callBuiltinScan` drops element zero and changes the result shape when there are no capture groups.
- Existing cucumber scenarios currently codify substring behavior such as `matches("hello world", "l") == true`, despite the original builtin task and DataWeave semantics requiring a whole-string match.

Acceptance criteria:
- `matches` and `match` require a whole-input match without changing explicit regex flag behavior.
- `match` returns the full match at index zero followed by capture groups, and returns an empty array when the input does not match.
- `scan` always returns an array of match arrays, each containing the full match followed by capture groups.
- Infix and function-call forms behave identically.
- Update contradictory cucumber expectations and add focused evaluator tests for partial/full matches, anchors, zero capture groups, and multiple captures.

title: Retire remaining legacy runner wrappers after ExecuteString migration
description: Problem: ExecuteString is now the structured execution path, but internal/runner/runner.go still exposes several compatibility wrappers and side-effect APIs such as RunFromString, RunFromStringWithContextAndOptionsAndGoContext, RunString, RunStringWithGoContext, and PrintExecutionResult. runFromStringWithConfig also repeats Lazy validation before calling ExecuteString, which performs the same check again. Risk: new callers can still choose value-only or stdout-printing paths and bypass the clearer adapter boundary, while duplicated option defaults and validation add drift risk. Suggested direction: move stdout printing to CLI-facing adapters, keep a minimal documented compatibility layer only where external callers need it, and migrate internal tests and helpers to ExecuteString plus FormatExecutionResult. Acceptance: runner has one primary structured execution API, duplicate Lazy/BaseDir handling is removed, and compatibility wrappers are either gone, deprecated, or trivially delegated with focused coverage.

title: Complete insertion-order propagation across formats and object transforms
description: The ordered-object implementation is only used by JSON, YAML, CSV, and a subset of evaluator producers. Other structured readers and copy/merge transforms fall back to untracked maps, so ObjectKeys sorts their fields alphabetically and silently changes source order. Reproductions: - keysOf(read("b=2\na=1", "text/x-java-properties")) returns ["a","b"] instead of source order ["b","a"]. - keysOf(read("21", "application/xml").root) returns ["a","b"]. - URL-encoded b=2&a=1 also returns ["a","b"]. - keysOf({b:2,a:1} - "missing"), keysOf({b:2,a:1} -- []), and an update expression over {b:2,a:1} all return ["a","b"]. - {b:2,a:1} ~ {c:3} returns key order ["a","b","c"] instead of preserving left order then new right keys. Evidence: Many structured readers still construct Object with make or literals, including XML, properties, URL-encoded, multipart, flatfile, XLSX, and protobuf. Object subtraction, remove, update expressions, deepCopy, attribute merges, and object update similarly copy through raw map iteration. Acceptance criteria: - Define small shared clone/merge/set helpers that preserve tracked order and use them instead of repeated raw map-copy loops. - Preserve source/header/wire order in every structured reader where the format exposes an order. - Preserve existing key positions on replacement, append genuinely new keys deterministically, and omit removed keys without reordering survivors. - Extend the structured-reader order table beyond JSON, YAML, and CSV and add cucumber regressions for the minimized evaluator operations. - Keep structural equality order-insensitive and keep the documented alphabetical fallback only for intentionally untracked external maps.

title: Make the documented lazy pipeline example executable
description:
The pipeline example in docs/lazy-evaluation.md uses |> to combine __lazyMap and __lazyFilter, but InfoMunge does not parse that syntax.

Documented shape:
var stream = __toStream([1,2,3,4,5])
var result = stream |> __lazyMap((x) -> x * x) |> __lazyFilter((x) -> x > 10)
---
force_eval(result)

InfoMunge fails at the first greater-than character with expected operand. The equivalent nested expression force_eval(__lazyFilter(__lazyMap(__toStream([1,2,3,4,5]), (x) -> x * x), (x) -> x > 10)) succeeds with [16,25]. Source review also shows replacePipeToFunctionOperator recognizes only a spaced vertical bar followed by a bare identifier and explicitly declines function calls, so it cannot support the documented chain.

Acceptance criteria:
- Either implement a clearly specified pipeline syntax that supports the documented lazy function composition, or rewrite the example to supported nested calls.
- Make the entire documentation example a valid standalone InfoMunge script with header declarations before the body separator.
- Add an executable documentation or Cucumber regression test for the example and expected [16,25] result.

title: Resolve user-defined functions before same-named builtins
description:
Problem

A local or imported user function cannot override a same-named builtin. Calls dispatch to special and regular builtin registries before checking the lexical scope, so valid declarations are silently ignored.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision, compared with DataWeave CLI 2.11.0:

`fun upper(x) = "custom:" ++ x` followed by `upper("abc")` returns `"ABC"`; expected `"custom:abc"`.

`fun sizeOf(x) = 99` followed by `sizeOf([1,2,3])` returns `3`; expected `99`.

Likely source

`evalCallExprWithVisitor` in `internal/evaluator/visitor.go` checks `GetBuiltinSpecial` and `GetBuiltinFunction` before it checks `visitor.scope.Vars` for a Lambda.

Impact

This is a silent wrong-result bug and makes normal lexical shadowing depend on whether a future release adds a builtin with the same name. Imported custom module functions are affected as well.

Acceptance criteria

- Local and imported user functions win normal unqualified name resolution over same-named builtins, matching DataWeave behavior.
- Builtins remain available when no user binding shadows them.
- Core module wrappers that intentionally share builtin names keep working without recursive self-calls, using an explicit native resolution mechanism or equivalent design.
- Exact user-function arity and lexical-scope behavior remain unchanged.
- Add cucumber regressions for at least one string builtin name and one collection builtin name, plus module coverage.

title: Add null-helper behavior to dw::core::Strings exports
description:
Problem

All four current dw::core::Strings exports have DataWeave null helper overloads, but the InfoMunge wrappers dispatch directly to strict native handlers. Optional string transformations therefore fail instead of preserving null.

Confirmed against DataWeave CLI 2.11.0

appendIfMissing(null, "x"), prependIfMissing(null, "x"), charCodeAt(null, 0), and fromCharCode(null) each return null. InfoMunge rejects the null argument; appendIfMissing reports that argument 1 must be a string.

Likely source

modules/dw/core/Strings.im forwards every call through __native, while the matching handlers in builtins_string_basic.go immediately assert string or integer arguments and have no null policy.

Acceptance criteria

- Every exported Strings module function returns null for the DataWeave-supported null position.
- Non-null argument validation and unicode behavior remain unchanged.
- Add module-level cucumber coverage for all four null overloads.
- Keep public direct builtin behavior explicit if it intentionally differs from imported module helper behavior.

title: Preserve exact integer values across numeric builtins
description:
Adversarial expression review found that arithmetic operators now protect integer precision, but many numeric builtins immediately convert exact int values to float64 and silently return plausible wrong values above 2^53.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision (DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 as oracle):
- sum([9007199254740993, 1]) returns 9.007199254740992e+15; DataWeave returns 9007199254740994.
- avg([9007199254740993, 9007199254740993]) returns 9.007199254740992e+15; DataWeave returns 9007199254740993.
- max([9007199254740992, 9007199254740993]) returns 9.007199254740992e+15; DataWeave returns 9007199254740993.
- abs(9007199254740993) returns 9.007199254740992e+15 instead of preserving 9007199254740993.
- mod(9007199254740993, 2) returns 0; DataWeave returns 1.
- isEven(9223372036854775808.0) returns false and isOdd returns true; DataWeave returns true and false.

Likely source: internal/evaluator/builtins_math.go routes ceil, floor, round, abs, min, max, pow, sum, avg, mod, and integer predicates through toNumber, ToFloat, or explicit float64/int64 conversions. This bypasses the exact rational and checked integer helpers used by evaluator arithmetic.

Acceptance criteria:
- Numeric builtins preserve exact integer inputs and results whenever representable by the runtime numeric model.
- A builtin must return a clear precision/range error rather than a rounded, wrapped, or misclassified value when exact evaluation is not supported.
- Audit all conversions in builtins_math.go, including aggregate, unary, modulo, range/random bounds, and integer-predicate paths.
- Add focused evaluator tests and cucumber regressions for the minimized cases, including values immediately above 2^53 and at int64 boundaries.

title: Finish nested collection source ownership inside explicit lambda bodies
description: A fresh differential review found that the fixes in bd-2tp2 and bd-2570 only keep a following collection operator inside an explicit lambda body for narrow source shapes such as a direct array literal. Minimized silent wrong-result repro: `[1,2] map (x) -> flatten([[x, x + 1]]) reduce (v,a) -> v + a`. InfoMunge returns `[2,3,1,2]`, while DataWeave 2.11.0 returns `[3,5]`. The transform trace rewrites reduce outside the outer map: `__reduce(__map(... flatten(...)), ...)`. Additional computed-source repros include `[1,2] map (x) -> {a:x,b:x+1} pluck $`, which returns the original objects instead of `[[1,2],[2,3]]`, and function-call, concatenated-array, conditional, and object sources followed by map, filter, reduce, groupBy, pluck, or mapObject. Preserve nested collection ownership for computed collection-producing expressions in explicit arrow bodies, while retaining the intentionally documented outer-chaining cases. Add focused transform traces, Cucumber wrong-result regressions, and differential generation for these source shapes.

title: Reject ambiguous or invalid XML output instead of dropping data or emitting malformed markup
description: The custom XML renderer does not validate the root shape or XML names. At the root, toXMLWithOptionsRecursive selects only the first non-special object key, so output application/xml for {a: 1, b: 2} succeeds with only the a element and silently discards b. Keys are interpolated into markup after only replacing hash with colon, so a key containing a space emits malformed XML such as an opening bad key tag without returning an error. Similar invalid attribute names are possible. Acceptance: define and document whether multiple roots are rejected or serialized as an explicit fragment, but never silently discard values; validate element and attribute QName syntax after namespace resolution; return typed validation errors for unrepresentable objects; add focused format tests and cucumber regressions for multiple roots, invalid names, namespaces, and valid ordered output.

title: unique() conflates different types with same string representation
description:
The `unique()` function in `internal/evaluator/builtins_collection.go:82-96` uses `fmt.Sprintf("%v", item)` as a deduplication key. This causes false collisions between values of different types that have the same string representation:

- `unique([1, "1"])` would drop `"1"` because both int `1` and string `"1"` format to `"1"` via `%v`
- `unique([true, "true"])` would similarly collide
- `unique([nil, "<nil>"])` would collide

Meanwhile, `distinct()` at line 100-126 correctly uses `fmt.Sprintf("%T:%v", item, item)` which includes the type, preventing these collisions.

Either `unique` should include type info like `distinct` does, or the semantic difference between `unique` and `distinct` should be explicitly documented and tested with cross-type scenarios.

Files:
- `internal/evaluator/builtins_collection.go:82-96` (unique — type-agnostic)
- `internal/evaluator/builtins_collection.go:100-126` (distinct — type-aware)

title: Bind the index parameter in lazyReduce lambdas
description:
The lazy reduce builtin explicitly accepts a two- or three-parameter lambda, and the Cucumber suite includes a three-parameter acceptance scenario, but the implementation binds only accumulator and value. Any use of the accepted index parameter fails at evaluation time.

Minimized reproduction on the current revision:
- `__lazyReduce(__toStream([10,20,30]), (acc, x, idx) -> acc + idx, 0)`
- Expected zero-based index accumulation: `3`
- Actual: `unresolved reference: idx`

The eager equivalent `[10,20,30] reduce (acc = 0, x, idx) -> acc + idx` correctly returns `3`.

Source evidence:
- `callBuiltinLazyReduce` accepts lambda counts from 2 through 3.
- `applyLambdaReduce` in `internal/evaluator/lazy.go` binds parameter 0 and parameter 1 only.
- The stream loop does not track an element index.
- The existing three-parameter feature scenario ignores its third argument, so it cannot catch the defect.

Acceptance criteria:
- lazyReduce binds a zero-based index to parameter 3 when present.
- Two-parameter lazy reducers remain unchanged.
- Index progression is correct through the complete stream and errors still propagate through lazy resolution.
- Update the existing three-parameter Cucumber scenario so its result depends on the index, and add a focused evaluator regression.

title: Harden readUrl private-network validation against DNS rebinding
description: readUrl validates hostname resolution before the HTTP request, but the actual transport may resolve again to a different address. DNS lookup errors also currently fail open. Move private-address enforcement into the HTTP transport DialContext or otherwise bind validation to the actual remote IP, fail closed on resolution errors where appropriate, and add cucumber coverage for blocked private targets and redirects.

title: Short-circuit some and every predicate evaluation
description:
The some and every builtins continue evaluating predicates after their result is already determined. Later failures or side effects therefore escape from logically unreachable elements.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision:
- some([1, 0], (x) -> x > 0 or 1 / x > 0) fails with division by zero; DataWeave dw::core::Arrays::some returns true after the first element.
- every([0, 1], (x) -> x > 0 and 1 / (1 - x) > 0) fails with division by zero; DataWeave dw::core::Arrays::every returns false after the first element.

Likely source: callBuiltinSome and callBuiltinEvery use executeLambdaOnArrayElements, whose callback can report an error but cannot signal successful early termination. The functions set found/allTrue and still traverse the remainder.

Acceptance criteria:
- some stops after the first true predicate result.
- every stops after the first false predicate result.
- Predicates that are actually evaluated still require a boolean result and preserve positional errors.
- Empty-array identities remain false for some and true for every.
- Add cucumber regressions with failing unreachable predicates and focused tests proving later predicate calls are skipped.

title: Honor precedence when composing configured infix operators
description:
Configured infix operators work in function-call form but several valid operator chains attach the downstream operation to the wrong operand or generate invalid syntax.

Minimized differential reproductions on the current revision:
- `["a","b"] joinBy "" matches /ab/` returns `true` in DataWeave, but InfoMunge passes the boolean match result as the join delimiter and reports `joinBy: argument 2 expected string, got bool`.
- `"abc" find "b" contains 1` returns `true` in DataWeave, but InfoMunge attaches `contains` to the search operand and reports `contains expects argument 2 to be string or Regex, got int`.
- `"ab" scan /(a)/ contains ["a","a"]` returns `true` in DataWeave, but InfoMunge generates syntax that fails with `unexpected comma; expecting ]`.

The equivalent explicit calls all succeed in InfoMunge:
- `matches(joinBy(["a","b"], ""), /ab/)`
- `contains(find("abc","b"), 1)`
- `contains(scan("ab", /(a)/), ["a","a"])`

This is distinct from the completed additive-left-operand work in bd-h1f1. The remaining failure is composition among configured operator families whose transforms execute at different orders. For example, joinBy runs before matches and consumes the matches expression as its right operand, while other operator orders fail in different directions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Declared precedence and associativity determine grouping independent of transform execution order.
- Cover joinBy followed by match, matches, and scan.
- Cover find and scan results followed by contains.
- Preserve all currently passing additive, collection-result, and same-operator associativity cases.
- Add transform-level grouping assertions and end-to-end differential Cucumber regressions.

title: Fix latent undefined cucumber steps surfaced by failures formatter
description: The failures formatter now reports existing Undefined/Skipped callbacks during the full ./test cucumber run even though Godog exits successfully in non-strict mode. Current surfaced undefined steps include array_indexing.feature range-index fixture setup, input_name_validation.feature file setup scenarios, io_functions.feature structured protobuf invalid key assertion, and runner_header_declarations.feature reserved metadata assertion. Update step definitions or feature wording so the default failures formatter remains concise on a passing full suite.

title: Repair the documented make playground launch path
description:
Problem: README.md tells users to run make playground for the Go server-backed playground, but the Makefile target invokes go run ./cmd/infomunge --server --listen :8080. The server now rejects every unauthenticated non-loopback or wildcard bind, so the documented target exits immediately with ValidationError instead of starting the playground. This is fallout from the server hardening completed in bd-3nhv.

Evidence: running go run ./cmd/infomunge --server --listen :8080 returns "server mode without --api-key must listen on a loopback address". README.md and MIND_MAP.md both direct users to make playground.

Acceptance: change the target to an explicit loopback address such as 127.0.0.1:8080, keep the documentation aligned, and add a focused workflow/command check that would fail if the target reintroduces an unauthenticated wildcard bind.

title: Make filter bind tighter than comparison operators
description: The bounded differential gate generated null != ["a", -42, -3] filter (right, y) -> y == y. DataWeave 2.11 returns true, but InfoMunge rewrites the comparison before filter and errors with filter expects an array, got bool. The saved reproduction is tmp/intensive-testing/failures/097_differential-infomunge-only-error_2026-07-27T09:44:50.json. Acceptance: collection filter expressions bind before surrounding equality and ordering comparisons, callback comparisons remain inside the callback body, existing filter chaining and associativity remain stable, and focused preprocessor plus Cucumber coverage captures the reproduction.

title: Handle implicit $ and $$ safely inside strings and regex literals
description:
Implicit-lambda rewriting performs raw text substitution inside quoted payloads, silently leaking internal parameter names and corrupting regular expressions.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision:
- `[1, 2] map "$"` returns `["__arg","__arg"]`; DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 returns `["1","2"]`.
- `[1, 2] map "$$"` returns `["__idx","__idx"]`; DataWeave returns `["0","1"]`.
- `[1, 2] filter ("$" == "1")` returns `[]`; DataWeave returns `[1]`.
- `["a", "ab", "ba"] map ($ matches /a$/)` returns `[false,false,false]`; DataWeave returns `[true,false,false]`.
- `["a", "ab", "ba"][?($ matches /a$/)]` returns `[]`; DataWeave returns `["a"]`.

Likely source:
- `detectDollarParams` and `replaceImplicitParam` in `internal/preprocessor/transformers_lambda.go` do not track string or regex context.
- Filter-selector rewriting in `transformers_syntax.go` calls the same raw replacement helper.
- Regex literals are converted before implicit-lambda rewriting, so an anchor such as `$` resides inside a generated quoted pattern and is rewritten as though it were a parameter reference.
- Bare `$` and `$$` inside a DataWeave string are implicit interpolation, but replacing them with identifier text inside the quoted literal produces a literal `__arg` or `__idx` rather than the bound value.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implicit-parameter detection and substitution are syntax/context aware.
- Bare `$` and `$$` in collection-lambda strings interpolate the current value/index with language string coercion instead of leaking internal names.
- Dollar signs inside regex patterns and other generated quoted payloads are never rewritten.
- Collection operators and filter selectors share the corrected behavior.
- Add focused preprocessor tests and cucumber regressions for the minimized string, regex-anchor, map/filter, and selector cases.

title: Coerce numeric strings in relational comparisons
description: The 500-case differential audit minimized an InfoMunge-only comparison error to `"-106.003" + 1.254 <= (0.000001)[2]`. The left side is numeric and numeric ordinal indexing produces the string `"0"`; DataWeave 2.11 returns true after numeric coercion, while InfoMunge reports `cannot compare float64 and string with <=`. The simpler matrix `[1 <= "2", "2" > 1, 3 < "2"]` returns `[true,true,false]` in DataWeave but errors at the first element in InfoMunge. DataWeave rejects nonnumeric strings such as `1 < "abc"`, so coercion must be conditional. Acceptance: support numeric string versus number in both operand orders for `<`, `<=`, `>`, and `>=`, preserving exact integer and big-integer behavior; continue rejecting nonnumeric strings and incompatible types; decide explicitly whether collection ordering shares this scalar contract; add focused evaluator, composed ordinal-selector, and differential Cucumber coverage.

title: Correct remaining stale cookbook summary claims
description: The summary table in docs/DATAWEAVE_COOKBOOK_EQUIVALENTS.md contradicts current behavior and earlier sections of the same guide. It says array field selection must use recursive descent or map even though direct array field selection is supported, and says named parameters are required even though implicit $ and $$ callbacks are supported. Audit the summary rows against current behavior, correct the substantiated stale claims, and validate representative examples through the CLI documentation workflow.

title: Make the Godog suite fail on undefined or pending steps
description: Problem: TestFeatures constructs godog.Options without Strict, whose default is false in Godog 0.15.1. Undefined, pending, or ambiguous steps can therefore be reported by the custom formatter while suite.Run still returns success. This exact behavior previously allowed multiple undefined steps to remain latent until bd-19q4 fixed the current examples, but the harness still permits the same class of regression. Evidence: test/godog_test.go sets Format, Paths, Output, and Concurrency only; the dependency help states Strict fails suites with pending, undefined, or ambiguous steps. The full suite currently passes, so enabling the guard should not require accepting known undefined scenarios. Acceptance: enable strict execution for normal and filtered feature runs; add a focused harness-level test proving an undefined, pending, or ambiguous step produces nonzero suite status; retain concise failures-only formatting; run the full Cucumber suite within five minutes.

title: Consolidate remaining duplicated parsing helpers
description:
Problem: several small helpers are still maintained as exact or near-exact copies across packages. internal/runner/declaration_ir.go duplicates evaluator ParseNumericLiteral and ParseBoolLiteral for type-property values; internal/evaluator/builtins_collection.go and builtins_string_text.go contain identical regex-pattern heuristics under different names; internal/preprocessor/mapping_pipeline.go duplicates sourcemap clampIndex.

Impact: each copy is small, but these are semantic policy helpers. A future change to numeric syntax, regex detection, or offset clamping can update one path and silently leave another inconsistent. The duplicates also obscure the intended ownership boundaries established by the recent runner, evaluator, and source-map refactors.

Acceptance: place each shared policy in the narrowest dependency-safe package, remove the duplicate bodies, add table tests at the shared boundary for numeric/bool edge cases and regex classification, and preserve source mapping behavior. If any pair intentionally differs, rename and test the difference instead of retaining byte-identical implementations.

title: Bind default outside complete higher-precedence expressions
description: Adversarial composition found a silent precedence error. With input payload `{name: -635}`, `[1, 2] map (x) -> x + payload.label default 10` returns `[11,12]` in InfoMunge but `[10,10]` in DataWeave 2.11. DataWeave returns `[11,12]` only when the selector fallback is explicitly grouped as `x + (payload.label default 10)`, so InfoMunge is silently applying grouping that the source did not request. Smaller reproductions are `1 + payload.label default 5` returning `6` instead of `5`, `-(payload.label) default 5` returning `-5` instead of `5`, and `!(payload.label) default true` returning `false` instead of `true`. This extends the configured-operator precedence work in bd-19fi and bd-h1f1 to default plus native prefix and additive operators. Acceptance: make ungrouped default consume the complete higher-precedence left expression; preserve explicit grouping; audit unary, multiplicative, additive, comparison, selector, builtin-call, and collection-lambda boundaries; add focused transform tests and end-to-end Cucumber regressions including the map reproduction.

title: Fix CoerceEquals panic on array/object ~= comparisons
description:
`CoerceEquals` can panic when either operand is an uncomparable Go type (`[]interface{}` / `map[string]interface{}`), because it does a direct `left == right` before guarding comparability.

Evidence:
- `internal/evaluator/evaluator.go:624` (`if left == right { ... }`)
- Deterministic failing test repro:
  `go test ./internal/testing/exprgen -run TestExpr_Depth3_DoesNotPanic -rapid.failfile=testdata/rapid/TestExpr_Depth3_DoesNotPanic/TestExpr_Depth3_DoesNotPanic-20260214155635-69581.fail -count=1`
- Failing generated expression: `[] ~= []`

Impact:
- User expressions using `~=` with arrays/objects can crash evaluation instead of returning a value/error.
- This violates no-panic expectations in property tests and is a runtime reliability bug.

Proposed fix:
- Rework `CoerceEquals` to avoid direct interface equality on potentially uncomparable values.
- Reuse `numericEquals`-style comparability checks / `reflect.DeepEqual` for slices/maps before fallback coercion.
- Add focused evaluator tests for `~=` over arrays and objects, including mixed-type coercion cases.

title: Bound ordered-object metadata registry lifecycle
description: Ordered object tracking preserves the public map type by storing key-order records in pkg/values keyed by map identity. The table does not retain object contents, but records are not reclaimed when maps are garbage-collected, so a long-lived high-churn server can accumulate metadata. Design a scoped or reclaimable lifecycle that preserves insertion-order correctness for values crossing evaluator and formatter boundaries, avoids stale pointer-identity reuse, and adds a stress test demonstrating bounded metadata growth.

title: Match DataWeave precedence for infix mod
description:
Adversarial differential review found silent wrong results for valid DataWeave infix mod expressions.

Minimized reproductions (DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 used as the oracle):
- `5 mod 2 * 2`: InfoMunge returns `2`; DataWeave returns `1` (`5 mod (2 * 2)`).
- `5 - 2 mod 2`: InfoMunge returns `5`; DataWeave returns `1` (`(5 - 2) mod 2`).
- `20 mod 6 / 2`: InfoMunge returns `1`; DataWeave returns `2`.

This is distinct from closed issue bd-nkk6, which fixed left scanning for `8 / 4 mod 3` but assumed mod shares multiplicative precedence. The distinguishing expressions show that DataWeave mod binds more weakly than `*`, `/`, `+`, and `-`. README explicitly tells compatible scripts to use `mod`, so the current result violates that contract.

Likely source: `internal/preprocessor/stages.go` declares replaceModOperator at TransformPrecedenceMultiplicative, while `internal/preprocessor/transformers_binary_operators.go` installs multiplicative left/right scanners. Existing cucumber coverage in operator_transformer_coverage.feature locks in the incorrect `20 mod 6 * 4 == 8` expectation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Define and document the intended DataWeave precedence/associativity for infix mod.
- Make the distinguishing repros match DataWeave while preserving explicit parentheses.
- Correct focused preprocessor tests and cucumber expectations.
- Add differential generator coverage that can distinguish keyword-operator precedence instead of only sampling Go-native operators.

title: Propagate null through keys builtin
description: The bounded differential gate generated keys(payload["active"]) with a missing path that resolved to null. DataWeave 2.11 succeeded for the generated case, while InfoMunge failed with keys: argument 1 expected object, got <nil>. Confirm keys(null) and related missing-selector semantics against DataWeave, align the builtin null policy, add focused evaluator and Cucumber coverage, and restore the bounded differential gate.

title: Forward the index argument through Arrays firstWith
description:
Problem

dw::core::Arrays firstWith advertises the DataWeave callback shape with value and index, but the InfoMunge script wrapper creates a one-parameter filter lambda and calls criteria(item). Exact user-function arity then rejects a valid two-parameter callback.

Reproduction

%dw 2.0
import firstWith from dw::core::Arrays
output application/json
---
firstWith([10, 20, 30], (x, i) -> i == 1)

DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 returns 20. InfoMunge fails with function expects 2 arguments, got 1.

Likely source

modules/dw/core/Arrays.im implements firstWith as first(array filter (item) -> criteria(item)), discarding the filter index.

Acceptance criteria

- firstWith forwards both item and zero-based index to a two-parameter callback.
- Preserve support for callback prefixes if InfoMunge intentionally permits a one-parameter callback.
- Add cucumber coverage where only the index selects the result.
- Audit other module wrappers for callback arguments that are accepted publicly but discarded by an inner collection lambda.

title: Decompose structured XLSX support into workbook, worksheet, and cell layers
description:
`pkg/formats/excel_structured.go` bundles workbook metadata parsing, shared-string decoding, worksheet decoding, row/header validation, worksheet encoding, cell serialization, archive assembly, and XML helpers in one large file.

Evidence:
- `pkg/formats/excel_structured.go:164-241` coordinates structured workbook decode/encode and high-level validation.
- `pkg/formats/excel_structured.go:261-339` parses workbook metadata and shared strings.
- `pkg/formats/excel_structured.go:342-621` mixes worksheet row decoding, cell coercion, header extraction, row validation, worksheet encoding, and per-cell XML rendering.
- `pkg/formats/excel_structured.go:632-780` assembles ZIP/XML output and low-level cell reference helpers.

Why this matters:
- Reader and writer concerns are tightly coupled, so changing one side requires reviewing the entire file.
- The workbook/worksheet/cell concepts do not have clear boundaries, which makes it harder to add features like formulas, styles, or alternative sheet-selection behavior safely.
- A single file now contains both business rules (header semantics, strictness) and transport details (ZIP layout, XML fragments).

Suggested direction:
- Split workbook/package concerns from worksheet row decoding/encoding and from cell coercion/rendering.
- Extract a small model for workbook metadata and cell values so read/write paths share behavior intentionally rather than by proximity.
- Add focused tests for worksheet decoding and encoding rules independently from archive assembly.

Acceptance criteria:
- Structured XLSX read/write logic is decomposed into smaller files/modules by concern.
- Worksheet row logic can be tested without exercising ZIP archive generation.
- Cell coercion/rendering rules live behind dedicated helpers instead of being embedded in the worksheet encoder/decoder loops.

title: Support DataWeave sizeOf semantics for numbers
description: The strengthened differential harness in bd-3men found one-sided InfoMunge errors for sizeOf on numeric values. DataWeave returns the character length of the numeric representation, for example sizeOf(211) returns 3, while InfoMunge reports unsupported type int. Acceptance: confirm integer, decimal, sign, exponent, and edge-value behavior against DataWeave; implement numeric sizeOf without lossy formatting; add unit and cucumber coverage; remove the linked differential allowlist rule.

title: Stop collection lambdas before downstream non-collection operators
description:
Adversarial differential testing found that grouped collection lambdas absorb operators that DataWeave applies to the collection result.

Reproductions:
- [1,2] map ($ + 1) ++ [9]
  - DataWeave: [2,3,9]
  - InfoMunge: cannot concatenate mixed types
- [1,2] map ($ + 1) joinBy "-"
  - DataWeave: "2-3"
  - InfoMunge: joinBy argument 1 expected array, got int
- [1,2,3] filter ($ > 1) joinBy "-"
  - DataWeave: "2-3"
  - InfoMunge: joinBy argument 1 expected array, got bool
- [1,2] map ((x) -> x + 1) joinBy "-" also fails, so explicit grouped lambdas are affected.

The preprocessing trace for the first case rewrites the lambda as __lambda("__arg", (__arg + 1) ++ [9]), proving that the trailing operation moved into the lambda body. scanLambdaBodyWithOptions currently recognizes only collection keywords as boundaries after a top-level grouped body.

Acceptance criteria:
- Preserve DataWeave precedence for downstream ++, --, joinBy, contains, and other applicable non-collection operators after grouped implicit and explicit lambdas.
- Do not incorrectly move operators such as as or comparisons out of a lambda when DataWeave keeps them in the body.
- Add focused transformer tests and end-to-end Cucumber differential repro coverage.

title: Support DataWeave array subtraction with single minus
description: The 500-case differential audit minimized an InfoMunge-only error to an array literal inside an object value using single-minus removal. Direct reproduction: `[1, 2, 1] - 1` returns `[2]` in DataWeave 2.11 but InfoMunge reports `cannot subtract []interface {} and int`. An absent candidate is also a valid no-op in DataWeave, for example `[1, 2] - 97` returns `[1,2]`. InfoMunge already supports array removal with the `--` extension and object key removal with single `-`, but the DataWeave-compatible array overload is missing. Acceptance: implement Array minus Value with structural element equality and removal of matching occurrences; retain numeric subtraction, object key removal, and the existing `--` behavior; cover absent values, repeated scalar values, null, nested collections, and a negative right operand such as `[1,2] - -97`; add evaluator and Cucumber differential regressions.

title: Unify preprocessor operator rewriting behind shared scanning rules
description:
The preprocessor’s operator rewriting is only partially declarative. A small config table exists, but several of the most delicate operators still rely on bespoke byte-walking scanners and duplicated precedence logic.

Evidence:
- `internal/preprocessor/transformers_operators.go:31-108` defines declarative configs for some binary operators.
- `internal/preprocessor/transformers_operators.go:168-259` (`as`) and `internal/preprocessor/transformers_operators.go:261-322` (`is`) duplicate string scanning and left-operand extraction patterns.
- `internal/preprocessor/transformers_operators.go:344-417` (`**`) implements a completely separate right-operand scanner.
- `internal/preprocessor/preprocessor.go:133-240` drives a long ordered chain of `handleX()` calls, which means precedence and interaction rules are encoded procedurally rather than described in one place.

Why this matters:
- Adding or changing operators requires understanding several scanner styles and subtle ordering constraints.
- Similar bugs can recur in different operator implementations because the parsing patterns are duplicated.
- The current design hides precedence decisions inside control flow, which raises review cost and makes regressions harder to predict.

Suggested direction:
- Move operator definitions toward a single declarative model (precedence, associativity, operand scanning rules, rewrite form).
- Extract shared operand-scanning helpers for typed operators (`as`, `is`) and infix operators that need custom right-boundary logic.
- Add focused tests around precedence interactions so new operators do not depend on handler ordering alone.

Acceptance criteria:
- `as`, `is`, exponent, and generic binary operators share common scanning infrastructure.
- Operator precedence/stop conditions are documented in one place.
- New operator additions do not require editing multiple unrelated scanning loops.

title: Support boolean selector keys in orderBy minBy and maxBy
description:
The shared comparator used by orderBy, minBy, and maxBy accepts only numeric or string selector values. DataWeave treats booleans as comparable with `false` before `true`, so valid boolean-key collection operations fail in InfoMunge.

Differential reproductions on the current revision:
- `[true,false] orderBy $` returns `[false,true]` in DataWeave; InfoMunge reports `orderBy: cannot compare keys at indexes 1 and 0: cannot compare values: bool and bool`.
- `[true,false] maxBy $` returns `true` in DataWeave; InfoMunge reports `cannot compare values: bool and bool`.
- `[true,false] minBy $` returns `false` in DataWeave; InfoMunge reports the same comparison error.
- `[1,2] orderBy ($ == 1)` returns `[2,1]` in DataWeave but fails in InfoMunge, demonstrating the common real-world combination of a comparison selector with ordering.

Source evidence: `compareValues` in `internal/evaluator/assertions.go` handles exact numerics and strings, then rejects all other pairs. The three collection operations share this helper.

Acceptance criteria:
- Boolean comparison defines `false < true` for orderBy, minBy, and maxBy.
- Numeric exactness and string ordering remain unchanged.
- Mixed incomparable types continue to produce the existing path-aware errors.
- Add Cucumber coverage for literal boolean arrays and comparison-derived selector keys, plus focused comparator tests.
- Do not change the separate historic numeric coercion semantics of the max and min math builtins as part of this ticket.

title: Make mutation package fit bounded repo-wide test runs
description: While working bd-2tf0, direct env INFOMUNGE_SKIP_GODOG=1 go test -v ./... -timeout 5m failed after internal/testing/mutation was killed at about 302s. The Cucumber repo-wide regression now uses package discovery only, but the normal repo-wide package suite still has an intensive mutation path that can exceed the five-minute budget. Acceptance: mutation tests either honor the short CI budget or are split/skipped from normal repo-wide runs, and the documented repo-wide package test command has a clear bounded variant.

title: Choose and document an explicit project license
description: Problem: the repository provides build, installation, server, WASM, and contribution-facing guidance but contains no LICENSE, COPYING, or equivalent file and README.md has no licensing section. Impact: users and contributors cannot determine what rights are granted for use, modification, redistribution, or contribution, which blocks responsible adoption even though the project is presented as buildable software. Acceptance: the owner chooses the intended license, add its complete canonical text in a top-level license file, add a concise README license section, document any required notices or exceptions for bundled/generated assets, and verify dependency or third-party attribution obligations before publication.
notes: Attribution audit completed: production binaries include Go, google.golang.org/protobuf v1.36.5, and gopkg.in/yaml.v3 v3.0.1; the tracked WASM playground also ships wasm_exec.js. THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md now reproduces the applicable upstream notices and README.md links to it. Remaining blocker: repository owner must choose InfoMunge project license and, if the chosen canonical text requires it, provide the copyright holder and year.

title: Preserve keyword operators around as type expressions
description:
The `as` preprocessor consumes or glues surrounding keyword/operator text, so valid composed expressions either fail to parse, absorb the operator into the type name, or evaluate with the wrong precedence.

Minimized reproductions:
- `5 as Number mod 2`: InfoMunge errors `unknown type: Number mod 2`; DataWeave returns `1`.
- `"abc" as String contains "a"`: InfoMunge produces a parse error; DataWeave returns `true`.
- `1 as String ++ "2"`: InfoMunge leaves `++` unparsed; DataWeave returns `"12"`. Parenthesizing `(1 as String) ++ "2"` works, showing this is preprocessing rather than evaluator semantics.
- `null as String default "x"`: InfoMunge returns `"null"`; DataWeave returns `"x"`.

Likely source:
- `scanTypedOperatorRightSpan` accepts identifiers and whitespace without recognizing following keyword-operator boundaries, so `Number mod 2` can become one type expression.
- `replaceTypedOperatorWithMapping` advances to right.Next after trimming the type but does not preserve separator whitespace. Later configured operators require exact spaced tokens such as ` ++ `, so the transform order in functionalProcessingContracts prevents them from matching.
- The typed-operator left-boundary table and earlier default-stage rewrite need a precedence audit as well.

Acceptance criteria:
- `as` and `is` preserve token boundaries and compose with all supported infix keyword/configured operators on either side.
- The minimized expressions match documented/DataWeave precedence without requiring extra parentheses.
- Add table-driven preprocessing tests that cover operators before and after typed expressions, plus cucumber regression scenarios for both wrong-result and parse-error cases.
- Preserve exact source mappings for errors after the rewrite.

title: Make collection ordering exact and propagate comparison errors
description:
Collection ordering helpers can silently emit incorrect order because they convert integers to `float64` and suppress comparator errors.

Minimized reproductions:
- `sort([9007199254740993, 9007199254740992])` returns the original descending pair instead of ascending order.
- `[9007199254740993, 9007199254740992] orderBy $` returns the original descending pair.
- `[9007199254740993, 9007199254740992] minBy $` returns `9007199254740993` instead of `9007199254740992`.
- `[1, "2", 0] orderBy $` returns `[1,"2",0]` even though number and string keys are incomparable; DataWeave reports a comparison error.

Likely root causes:
- `sort` converts all numeric values to `float64`, collapsing adjacent integers above 2^53.
- `compareValues`, shared by orderBy, minBy, maxBy, and assertion matchers, also compares through `ToFloat`.
- The `orderBy` sort closure catches comparison errors and substitutes original-index ordering, so invalid keys look like a successful stable sort.

Acceptance criteria:
- Numeric ordering uses the exact comparison semantics already used by evaluator relational operators.
- sort, orderBy, minBy, and maxBy distinguish integers above 2^53.
- orderBy returns a useful positional error for incomparable keys rather than swallowing it.
- Audit all `compareValues` callers, including assertion matchers, for the same precision behavior.
- Add unit and cucumber regressions for large adjacent integers and mixed incomparable keys.

title: Implement short-circuit evaluation for logical AND and OR
description:
Logical binary expressions currently evaluate both operands before applying AND or OR.

Minimized repros:
- false and (1 / 0 == 0) fails with division by zero; DataWeave returns false.
- true or (1 / 0 == 0) fails with division by zero; DataWeave returns true.

Root cause: internal/evaluator/visitor.go VisitBinaryExpr visits expr.X and expr.Y unconditionally, then calls evalBinaryOp. The land and lor helpers only combine already-evaluated values.

Impact: guarded expressions still fail or execute side effects in branches that should be unreachable.

Acceptance criteria:
- Evaluate the left operand first for logical AND and OR.
- Skip the right operand when the left value determines the result.
- Preserve boolean type errors for operands that are actually evaluated.
- Add cucumber regressions using a division-by-zero right operand and a side-effect-sensitive builtin if practical.

title: Clarify overbroad Go-only and cucumber-for-every-change agent rules
description: Problem: AGENTS.md says `Use golang only` and `Always verify new features or changes by adding a cucumber test`; MIND_MAP.md repeats the Go-only rule. Taken literally, these forbid necessary maintenance of the repository-owned HTML, JavaScript, Markdown, Makefile, and shell-facing assets, and require a new Gherkin scenario even for internal refactors or documentation-only corrections. The repository itself relies on focused Go unit tests for internal packages and has existing non-Go source assets. Impact: agents can refuse in-scope work or add low-value cucumber tests that do not verify the changed layer. Acceptance: define the intended scope of the Go-only preference, require cucumber coverage for new or changed user-visible behavior, allow focused Go tests for internal behavior, define suitable validation for docs/workflow-only edits, and keep AGENTS.md and MIND_MAP.md wording aligned.

title: Align keyed selector behavior on arrays with DataWeave
description: A live differential comparison found divergent keyed bracket selection on arrays. With payload {"age":[-80.45]}, payload.age["score"] returns [null] in InfoMunge and null in DataWeave. Audit keyed bracket and related recursive selector semantics on arrays, document the intended compatibility, add cucumber coverage, and restore nested keyed-index generation to the differential subset once resolved.
close_reason: Aligned array keyed and recursive selector semantics with DataWeave, documented behavior, added unit and Cucumber coverage, and restored nested differential generation.

title: Reject multiple stdin-backed CLI inputs instead of silently returning nil on later reads
description:
`internal/io/input.go` reads `os.Stdin` every time a source starts with `:`. After the first stdin-backed input drains the stream, later stdin-backed inputs receive empty content, and `formats.Read("", mimeType)` returns `nil` without an error.

Evidence:
- Repro: `printf \{"a":1}' | go run ./cmd/infomunge -s json -i extra=:json %im 0.1
output application/json
---
{payload: payload, extra: extra}`
- Actual output: `{"extra":null,"payload":{"a":1}}`

Why this is risky:
- The second stdin consumer looks valid but evaluates as `null`, so users can get corrupted results without any explicit failure.
- The same silent behavior is possible with repeated `-i name=:format` flags.

Code references:
- `internal/cli/app.go:90-97`
- `internal/io/input.go:26-44`
- `pkg/formats/reader.go:15-18`

Expected:
- Either reject multiple stdin-backed inputs up front, or buffer stdin once and fan it out intentionally.

title: Unify do block declarations with shared declaration IR
description: Problem: do and using block declarations are parsed by a separate evaluator mini parser in internal/evaluator/builtins_arrays_do.go. Header and module declarations now use the shared Declaration IR in internal/runner/declaration_ir.go, but do block var and fun declarations still use strings.Split and strings.Index line parsing. Risk: declaration syntax and diagnostics can drift between top level headers, modules, and do blocks. The do path currently handles only simple line oriented var and fun declarations and does not share multiline declaration, comment, parameter type, source map, or validation behavior. Suggested direction: route do block declarations through a shared declaration compiler or extract a small declaration parsing and binding service that both runner and nested runtime constructs can use. Acceptance: do block declarations reuse the shared parser or an intentionally shared subset, behavior drift is covered by cucumber or focused Go tests, and existing do block and update expression scenarios remain green.

title: Honor context cancellation throughout script evaluation
description:
ExecuteString threads context.Context into Scope, but eager evaluation does not inspect it. Only URL IO, lazy streams, and while-loop deadline calculations use the context. A canceled context can therefore keep evaluating ordinary ASTs and collection lambdas; while checks only time.Now against a captured deadline and ignores context cancellation without a deadline or before that deadline. The HTTP handler checks request context only before and after ExecuteString, so work continues inside the call after a client disconnects.

Evidence:
- DefaultVisitor.Visit checks depth but never scope.GoContext().Err().
- map/filter/reduce and related element loops have no cancellation checkpoints.
- checkTimeout compares time with Scope.LoopDeadline but does not check Scope.GoContext().Err().
- Current cucumber coverage proves readUrl cancellation and a request canceled before handler entry, but not cancellation during CPU evaluation.

Acceptance criteria:
- A pre-canceled context makes a normal eager expression return context.Canceled rather than a value.
- Cancellation during while loops and large collection operations stops promptly, including contexts canceled before a later deadline.
- Add low-overhead checkpoints at centralized evaluation/iteration boundaries rather than scattering per-builtin logic.
- Preserve positional errors for language failures while keeping errors.Is compatibility for context.Canceled and context.DeadlineExceeded.
- Add focused runner/evaluator tests plus a server regression demonstrating that in-flight work stops after request cancellation.

title: Support exact minimum-integer double negation
description: The differential harness produced contains(null, -(-9223372036854775808)). DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 evaluates the numeric argument and returns false, while InfoMunge reports integer overflow during negation. Verify DataWeave integer range behavior, preserve exact arithmetic when negating the minimum runtime integer twice, and add focused evaluator and Cucumber coverage without weakening overflow checks for genuinely out-of-range results.

title: Coerce numeric strings across DataWeave arithmetic operators
description: The 500-case differential soak minimized an InfoMunge-only error to -((12.5)[-3]): DataWeave returns -2 while InfoMunge reports cannot negate string. Direct probes show the broader gap: -"2.5" returns -2.5 in DataWeave, "2" * 3 returns 6, "6" / 2 returns 3, "2" - 1 returns 1, 1 - "2" returns -1, and "7" mod 3 returns 1, while InfoMunge rejects all of them. Numeric-string coercion already exists for plus and scalar ordering. Extend the same exact parsing policy to unary negation and the DataWeave arithmetic family without weakening object subtraction or array removal overloads. Preserve arbitrary-precision integer behavior and add Cucumber cases for a composed map and reduce expression plus the number-ordinal selector repro.

title: Centralize lambda invocation and enforce lexical scope and arity
description:
Three separate lambda invocation paths have drifted semantically: callUserDefinedFunction in evaluator.go copies the caller scope, callUserDefinedFunctionWithVisitor uses the captured lexical scope and checks arity, and callUserLambda uses lexical scope but silently truncates or omits arguments.

Reproductions:
- A zero-argument lambda that captures offset = 5 returns 100 when try, orElse, or orElseTry invokes it inside a nested do block that shadows offset = 100. A combined script returns [100,100,100] instead of [5,5,5].
- Arrays::countBy([1,2,3]) reaches an undefined criteria error instead of reporting that two arguments are required.
- Arrays::countBy([1,2,3], (x) -> x > 1, "ignored") succeeds with 2 and silently ignores the extra argument.

Root cause:
- runtime try-family builtins call callUserDefinedFunction, which uses scope.Copy rather than newLambdaInvocationScope.
- module-qualified calls use callUserLambda, which binds only the arguments that happen to exist and has no arity validation.
- ordinary calls use a third helper with the intended lexical and arity behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Route ordinary, module-qualified, try, orElse, and orElseTry calls through one invocation primitive.
- Every user lambda/function uses its captured lexical environment plus explicit parameter bindings.
- Too few and too many arguments fail with a positional function-arity error for both imported and local functions.
- Add cucumber regressions for nested shadowing through all three try-family builtins and for missing/extra module arguments.
- Remove the redundant invocation helpers once callers are migrated.

title: Accept the minimum signed integer literal
description: The valid expression -9223372036854775808 fails with invalid integer literal because evalBasicLit calls strconv.Atoi on the positive token 9223372036854775808 before evalUnaryExpr can apply negation. This makes the negative endpoint of the native int range unrepresentable even though arithmetic explicitly supports minInt and checks overflow. The installed DataWeave CLI evaluates the expression successfully. Acceptance: the minimum signed integer literal evaluates to -9223372036854775808 on 64-bit builds; positive 9223372036854775808 remains rejected or follows the documented numeric-range policy; negation and overflow checks remain safe; add evaluator and cucumber regression coverage.

title: Preserve grouped infix operands before as and is coercion
description:
Grouped operands containing a raw functional infix operator are split at that inner operator by the typed-operator left scan. Minimal repro: `%im 0.1
output application/json
---
(5 mod 2) as String`. Expected JSON is `"1"`; InfoMunge fails with `4:10: expected ), found ,`. A transform trace shows `replaceAsOperator` producing `(5 mod __coerce(2), "String")` instead of coercing `(5 mod 2)`, after which `replaceModOperator` preserves the malformed comma. The same failure occurs with `is` and with grouped `contains`, and it breaks realistic callbacks such as `[1,2,3,4] groupBy ((x,i) -> (x mod 2) as String)`. `findTypedOperatorLeftOperandStartBytes` uses depth-insensitive string searches through `typedOperatorLeftBoundaryOps`, so an operator inside an explicitly grouped left operand is incorrectly treated as a boundary. Preserve explicit grouping for both `as` and `is`, add focused preprocessor coverage, and add cucumber coverage for the minimal coercion plus the groupBy combination.

title: Simplify runtime value alias stack across values formats and evaluator
description: Problem: core runtime value types now flow through several alias layers: pkg/values defines Value, Object, Array, XMLMultiValue, and Namespace; pkg/formats/core aliases them; pkg/formats aliases pkg/formats/core; internal/evaluator aliases pkg/values again. The Result helper also lives in pkg/formats/core but is only used by ReadAsObject, ReadAsArray, FormatResult, and tests. Risk: the extra indirection obscures the actual value ownership boundary and makes simple type changes require scanning several packages that mostly re-export each other. Suggested direction: decide the public compatibility surface, then collapse internal imports toward pkg/values where practical or document the remaining aliases as intentional API shims. Also reassess whether Result belongs in the format core package or should stay only on public helper APIs. Acceptance: internal packages have a single obvious source for runtime value types, unnecessary alias-only layers are removed or documented, and format/evaluator tests remain green.

title: Remove the unused internal error-builder surface
description:
Problem: internal/errors still carries a fluent Builder API plus a broad matrix of positional and wrapping helpers that have no callers outside their own declarations. Unused examples include NewBuilder/NewBuilderf and all Builder methods, NewPositional/NewPositionalf, ParsePositional variants, most Runtime/Validation/User positional variants, and WrapEval/WrapRuntime/WrapIO/WrapValidation/WrapInternal non-formatting variants. Error Context getters and builder-only mutation also appear unused.

Impact: roughly a hundred lines of internal-only API imply supported patterns that production code does not use, make the actual error conventions harder to see, and duplicate direct constructor/WithPosition composition. Because this is an internal package, the dead surface has no external compatibility obligation.

Acceptance: confirm callers with repository-wide search, delete unused builders/helpers/fields or document a concrete retained use, keep only the constructors and wrappers exercised by production paths, and run focused error tests plus the repo-wide package suite. This is a concrete follow-up to the broader adapter cleanup in bd-3tw4.

title: Escape XML output text and attributes
description: The XML writer formats element text and attribute values with raw fmt.Sprintf output. Values containing angle brackets, ampersands, or quotes can produce malformed XML or content injection. Update pkg/formats/xml.go to escape element text and attribute values with encoding/xml-safe helpers and add cucumber coverage for XML output escaping.

title: Anchor intensive-testing artifacts to repository tmp
description: Problem: internal/testing/failures defines default failure and candidate directories as relative tmp/intensive-testing paths. Go tests run with each package directory as the working directory, so mutation and differential callers write beneath the package instead of the repository scratch area. The root ignore rules do not match those nested paths. Evidence: tracked files currently exist under internal/testing/mutation/tmp/intensive-testing/failures and candidates, even though the design, README workflow, .gitignore, and AGENTS.md all place disposable artifacts under repository-root tmp. internal/testing/metrics already discovers the repository root before writing its report, but failures.SaveArtifact and WriteCandidateScenario do not. Impact: soak runs can dirty source packages with generated findings, deduplication and metrics can inspect different artifact stores depending on caller working directory, and generated candidates have been accidentally committed. Acceptance: resolve all default intensive-testing paths from one repository-root-aware helper or an explicit caller-supplied artifact root; keep ToDir test seams; ensure mutation, differential, metrics, and candidate generation share the same store from any package working directory; ignore and clean the accidentally tracked nested artifacts after promoting any still-useful regression; add focused tests that execute path resolution from a nested directory.

title: Native builds cannot load embedded dw::core modules outside repo-root layouts
description:
Problem

The native (non-JS) module loader only resolves imports from filesystem search paths under the script base directory. It never falls back to the embedded `dw::core` module sources, even though those sources are already embedded in `modules/dw/core/sources.go` and the JS loader handles them specially.

Reproduction

1. Build the CLI: `go build -o tmp/infomunge ./cmd/infomunge`
2. Create `tmp/standard-core.im`:
   `%im 0.1`
   `output application/json`
   `import * from dw::core::Arrays`
   `---`
   `countBy([1,2,3], (x) -> x > 1)`
3. Run `./tmp/infomunge -f tmp/standard-core.im`
4. Observe: `module "dw::core::Arrays" not found (searched in [.../tmp .../tmp/modules])`

Expected

`dw::core::*` imports should work from an installed/native binary regardless of where the script lives. The embedded standard modules already exist in the binary and should not depend on repo-relative files being present.

Why this matters

Right now built-in module support is accidentally tied to the repo layout. Scripts that work from the repo root fail when the binary is used from another directory, which breaks portability for the CLI and undermines the value of embedding those module sources.

Code references

- `internal/runner/module_loader.go:23-94`
- `modules/dw/core/sources.go:9-38`
- `internal/runner/module_loader_js.go:27-60` (already has the desired standard-module fallback behavior)

Acceptance criteria

- Teach the non-JS loader to resolve/load standard modules before filesystem lookup.
- Add regression coverage for running a native binary against a script outside the repo root that imports `dw::core::*`.

title: Preserve missing-value fallback through composed expressions
description: A separate default mismatch remains when the missing selector is already on the left of a native operator. With input payload `{name: -635}`, `payload.label + 1 default 5` returns `EvalError: cannot add <nil> and int` in InfoMunge while DataWeave 2.11 returns `5`. This is distinct from bd-1dnt: the source already places the complete addition to the left of default, so fixing right-side left-operand capture does not supply the missing fallback semantics. Literal `1 + null default 5` errors in DataWeave, so the fix must preserve a missing-selector or absence distinction rather than broadly swallowing arithmetic errors or treating every null operation as fallback. Acceptance: model and propagate missing-field absence through composed expressions until default handles it; do not catch unrelated failures such as division by zero; verify direct and nested object selectors, prefix and binary operators, function arguments, and collection callbacks; add evaluator and Cucumber regressions.

title: Reject non-boolean some and every predicate results
description:
The `some` and `every` builtins silently convert predicate type mistakes into plausible boolean results.

Minimized reproduction:
`{someResult: some([1], (x) -> 1), everyResult: every([1], (x) -> 1)}`

Current result:
`{"someResult":false,"everyResult":true}`

Expected:
Both calls should fail because the predicate returned a number rather than a boolean. Eager `filter`, selector filters, and `filterObject` already enforce the same predicate contract.

Likely root cause:
The callbacks in `callBuiltinSome` and `callBuiltinEvery` use a boolean type assertion but update state only when it succeeds. A failed assertion is ignored; `some` keeps its false initializer and `every` keeps its true initializer.

Acceptance criteria:
- `some` and `every` return a positional evaluation error when any predicate result is not boolean.
- Error wording identifies the builtin and actual result type.
- Empty-array behavior remains `false` for some and `true` for every without invoking the predicate.
- Add cucumber coverage for numeric, string, and null predicate results.

title: Remove remaining unused internal helper exports
description: Problem: several exported helpers in internal packages have no repository caller outside their declaration, leaving misleading alternate APIs after recent architecture cleanup. Confirmed examples are handlers.FormatRunResult, preprocessor.IsOperatorChar, version.FullString, evaluator.AsRegex, evaluator.NewDefaultVisitor, and failures.GenerateAllCandidates. Production code uses runner.FormatExecutionResult, package-local scanner policy, version.String, direct regex assertions, NewDefaultVisitorForScope, and GenerateAllCandidatesFromDirs or no candidate batch entrypoint instead. Impact: these names imply supported extension points, obscure the intended single execution and scope paths, and add code and documentation without compatibility value because the packages are internal. Acceptance: confirm repository call graphs after the other open cleanup tickets land; remove truly unused functions and their comments, unexport any helper that gains a local caller, or document and test a concrete retained use; include other declaration-only internal helpers found by the same audit while excluding intentional registration and metadata APIs; run go vet, focused package tests, and the bounded repository suite.

title: Keep update expressions inside collection lambda bodies
description: Problem: an unparenthesized update expression used as an explicit collection lambda body is silently moved outside the collection operation. Reproduction: `%im 0.1 output application/json --- [{a: 1}, {a: 2}] map (item) -> item update { case value at .a -> value * 10 }`. InfoMunge returns `[{"a":1},{"a":2}]`; DataWeave 2.11 and the parenthesized control `map (item) -> (item update {...})` return `[{"a":10},{"a":20}]`. Transform tracing shows the core rewriter emits `__updateExpr(array map (item) -> item, cases)` before the functional collection stage, so `handleUpdateExprBlock` and `findLeftOperandStartBytes` consume the unresolved map expression as the update left operand. Acceptance: preserve update inside unparenthesized explicit collection lambda bodies according to DataWeave precedence; audit other collection operators that can contain update expressions; preserve deliberately parenthesized outer-update behavior; add cucumber coverage for the observable result and focused preprocessor trace or mapping coverage.

title: Centralize output formatting policy across CLI HTTP and WASM
description:
Fresh-eyes cohesion/coupling audit finding.

Problem:
XML output formatting policy is duplicated across runner, HTTP/WASM handlers, and test harness code. Namespace extraction, output option application, and XML writer selection are spread across packages, causing policy drift and forcing adapters to know runner context internals.

Evidence:
- `internal/runner/runner.go` defines `ContextKeyNamespaces`, `ContextKeyOutputOptions`, `ExtractNamespaceVars`, `ApplyXMLOutputOptions`, and XML-specific logic inside `formatOutputWithContext`.
- `internal/handlers/run.go` repeats the same XML path in `FormatRunResult` and imports runner solely to access context keys/helpers.
- `test/godog_test.go` has local copies of XML formatting helper logic around the runner output path.
- `pkg/formats` owns `XMLOutputOptions`, but parsing/applying header output options lives in runner.

Suggested direction:
- Introduce a single output formatting component, for example `internal/output` or a narrowly scoped `runner.FormatExecutionResult`.
- Give it a typed metadata struct instead of magic context keys (`__namespaces__`, `__output_options__`).
- Keep XML option parsing/application in one place and have CLI, server, WASM, and tests call that same function.

Acceptance criteria:
- XML namespace and output-option handling has one production implementation.
- `internal/handlers` no longer reaches into runner context-key constants for formatting policy.
- Test harness uses the same formatting path as production instead of helper copies.
- Add cucumber coverage for at least one XML namespace/options scenario through `/run` or WASM-compatible handler flow plus existing CLI output behavior.

title: Remove declaration-only formatting wrappers left after output consolidation
description: Repository-wide caller searches found three formatting helpers with no caller beyond their declarations: internal/output.FormatResult, pkg/formats.formatXMLWithNamespaces, and pkg/formats.toXML. The active paths use FormatResultWithMetadata, FormatXMLWithOptions, and toXMLWithOptions. These wrappers add alternate entrypoints and comments that imply contracts nobody exercises, while two are package-private and have no compatibility obligation. Acceptance: recheck callers, remove the declaration-only wrappers and stale comments, keep any wrapper only if a concrete caller and distinct contract are documented, and run format, vet, focused package tests, and the bounded repository suite.

title: Replace equality shortcuts with safe exact recursive comparison
description:
Adversarial review found multiple wrong results and a process panic in `numericEquals` and `CoerceEquals`.

Minimized reproductions:
- `[[1] == [1.0], {a: 1} == {a: 1.0}]` returns `[false,false]`; DataWeave returns `[true,true]`.
- `[["1"] ~= [1], {a: "1"} ~= {a: 1}]` returns `[false,false]`; DataWeave returns `[true,true]`.
- `"9007199254740993" ~= 9007199254740992` returns `true`; DataWeave returns `false` because the integers are distinct.
- `null ~= "<nil>"` returns `true`; DataWeave returns `false`.
- `({a: 1, a: 2}).a == ({a: 1, a: 2}).a` panics the CLI with `comparing uncomparable type values.XMLMultiValue`.

Likely root causes:
- Array and Object equality delegates to `reflect.DeepEqual`, so nested numeric equivalence and coercion rules are skipped.
- `XMLMultiValue` is an uncomparable slice type but is omitted from the uncomparable guards before interface equality.
- Coercion equality parses numeric values through `float64`, collapsing integers above 2^53.
- The final `fmt.Sprintf` fallback exposes Go display artifacts such as `<nil>` as language equality semantics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Implement a non-panicking recursive comparator for arrays, XML multi-values, and objects.
- Standard equality treats nested int and exactly equivalent decimal values consistently with scalar numeric equality.
- Coercion equality recursively applies coercion semantics without lossy float conversion or Go formatting artifacts.
- Preserve order-insensitive object equality.
- Add evaluator unit tests and cucumber regressions for every minimized reproduction.

title: Reject extra or ambiguous CLI positional arguments
description: The CLI silently ignores arguments that should be treated as user errors. internal/cli/app.go:111-113 assigns only fs.Arg(0) to the inline script and drops any additional positional args. app.execute then prioritizes -f and ignores an inline script when both are provided. I verified the first case with timeout 5m go run ./cmd/infomunge "%im 0.1 --- 1" unexpected-extra; it exited 0 and printed 1, masking the unexpected-extra argument. This conflicts with the usage shape that allows at most one optional script. Acceptance: parseFlags should return a validation error when more than one positional script argument is present, and when -f is combined with an inline script. Add cucumber coverage for both failure paths and keep the optional run subcommand behavior intact.

title: Stabilize flaky go test all regression feature around lambda stringification
description:
`test/features/go_test_all_regression.feature` currently fails intermittently because `internal/testing/properties.TestEvaluate_NoPanics_Deterministic_AndTypeConsistent` can treat lambda-containing results as nondeterministic.

Observed on April 19, 2026 while verifying `bd-2abm`:
- `go test ./...` failed inside the cucumber scenario.
- The failing generated expression concatenated a string with an array containing a lambda.
- The two evaluations differed only by lambda pointer addresses embedded in the formatted string output.

Example symptom:
- first: `"s[7 0.08718961160566452 0x... cj [<nil> map[D_32110:-25] true]]"`
- second: `"s[7 0.08718961160566452 0x... cj [<nil> map[D_32110:-25] true]]"`

Follow-up work:
- Make lambda stringification deterministic, or
- Teach the property generator / determinism check to avoid this false nondeterminism path, and
- Re-run `test/features/go_test_all_regression.feature` until it is stable.

title: Split high-complexity preprocessor transforms and standardize mappings
description: The review found the preprocessor pipeline has useful contract metadata, but several transformer files remain very large and mix byte scanners, rune scanners, inferred mappings, and exact mappings. Split transformers_syntax.go, rewriter_handlers.go, transformers_operators.go, and transformers_regex.go into cohesive units, prefer shared scanner helpers, and convert high-risk inferred mappings to exact mappings with cucumber coverage for error positions.

title: Split format registry from bundled codec implementations and option dispatch
description:
Problem:
`pkg/formats` contains the public read/write registry, MIME and extension lookup, XML namespace rendering, option dispatch, and all codecs including protobuf, XLSX, Java serialization, multipart, flatfile, CSV, JSON, YAML, and XML. Registering a new option-aware format requires editing central maps in `options_dispatch.go`.

Why it matters:
The package has low cohesion and high compile-time coupling: importing the registry brings every codec and heavy transitive dependency into the same package. It makes the format boundary harder to extract as a library and increases the chance that a format-specific change affects unrelated format behavior.

Evidence:
- `pkg/formats/registry.go` owns global readers/writers/extensions.
- `pkg/formats/options_dispatch.go` is a central list of option-aware codecs.
- `pkg/formats/protobuf*.go`, `xlsx*.go`, `xml.go`, `flatfile.go`, `java.go`, and the light codecs all share one package and init-time registration.

Suggested direction:
Keep a small formats core package for value aliases, registry interfaces, MIME normalization, and option registration. Move heavier codecs into subpackages or registration modules that explicitly install themselves. Let each codec register its own option handlers with the registry instead of editing a central dispatch map.

Acceptance:
- Adding a new option-aware format does not require changing a central options dispatch file.
- Lightweight registry/value tests can run without compiling every codec implementation.
- Existing format behavior remains covered by current reader/writer tests and relevant cucumber features.

title: Align nested collection operators inside explicit lambda bodies
description: A live differential comparison found a collection-lambda boundary mismatch. Minimized shape: [1] map (i, x) -> [] flatMap (x0) -> [true].
