InfoMunge applies flatMap outside the completed map and returns [true], while DataWeave keeps flatMap in the explicit map body and returns [[]]. Audit nested collection operators in explicit arrow bodies, add focused preprocessor and cucumber coverage, and restore nested collection forms to differential generation once resolved.

title: Fix malformed embedded playground CSS selector for toolbar controls
description:
The embedded playground stylesheet contains malformed CSS selector syntax in `internal/cli/webapp.go`, which can break toolbar input/select styling and make UI behavior browser-dependent.

Evidence:
- `internal/cli/webapp.go:65-66`
  - `.toolbar select {`
  - `.toolbar input {`
- Missing comma/brace creates an invalid rule block.

Impact:
- Styles for toolbar form controls are not reliably applied.
- Playground appearance can regress silently without compile-time checks because HTML/CSS is embedded as a raw Go string.

Proposed fix:
- Correct the selector block to a valid grouped selector (`.toolbar select, .toolbar input { ... }`).
- Add a lightweight test/lint check for critical embedded HTML/CSS template validity (or extract template assets for tooling coverage).

title: Unicode string indexing builtins use byte offsets instead of rune indices
description:
Adversarial expression audit found inconsistent Unicode indexing across string builtins.

Repros on current @:
- `charAt("é", 0)` returns `"Ã"` instead of `"é"`
- `charAt("é", 1)` returns `"©"` instead of an out-of-range error
- `charAt("😀", 0)` returns `"ð"`
- `indexOf("éx", "x")` returns `2` instead of `1`
- `lastIndexOf("aéé", "é")` returns `3` instead of `2`
- Combined inconsistency: `[substring("éx", 0, 1), indexOf("éx", "x"), charAt("éx", 1)]` currently evaluates to `["é", 2, "©"]`

Likely root cause:
- `internal/evaluator/builtins_string_basic.go:145-149` uses `len(str)` and `str[idx]` in `charAt`, so it indexes bytes rather than runes.
- `internal/evaluator/builtins_string_basic.go:203-209` and `230-236` delegate string `indexOf`/`lastIndexOf` to `strings.Index` / `strings.LastIndex`, which return byte offsets.
- This conflicts with the surrounding API behavior: `substring` and `charCodeAt` are already implemented in rune space (`internal/evaluator/builtins_string_basic.go:105-126` and `169-174`).

Coverage gap:
- Existing cucumber coverage exercises ASCII-only `charAt`/`indexOf`/`lastIndexOf` cases in `test/features/string_functions_additional.feature:352-555`.
- Unicode coverage currently exists for `substring` in `test/features/string_edge_cases.feature:592-603`, but not for the indexing builtins.

Expected work:
- Make `charAt`, string `indexOf`, and string `lastIndexOf` operate in rune indices/code points.
- Add cucumber regressions covering accented characters and emoji for these builtins.

title: Implement update upsert selectors for missing object fields
description: DataWeave differential repro: {a:1} update { case x at .missing! -> 2 } returns {a:1,missing:2}. InfoMunge silently returns {a:1}, treating the asserted upsert selector as an ordinary missing path. Parse the trailing exclamation marker as update upsert intent, allow creation of a missing terminal object field while retaining ordinary missing-selector no-op behavior, define nested missing-parent behavior consistently with DataWeave, and add Cucumber coverage for simple and nested upserts plus a control case without the marker.

title: Inconsistent use of type aliases vs raw map[string]interface{}
description:
The evaluator package defines type aliases for clarity:
- `type Value = interface{}`
- `type Context = map[string]interface{}`
- `type Object = map[string]interface{}`
- `type Array = []interface{}`

However, many files — especially `builtins_core.go` (27 occurrences), `declarations.go` (13), `runner.go` (15), and `builtins_collection_ops.go` (27) — use the raw `map[string]interface{}` form instead of the aliases. There are 411 total occurrences of `map[string]interface{}` across 68 Go files.

This inconsistency makes the code harder to read and obscures intent. For example, a function parameter typed `map[string]interface{}` could be an evaluation context, an object value, or output options — the alias would disambiguate.

Migrate call sites to use the type aliases where semantically appropriate.

Files:
- `internal/evaluator/types_value.go` (alias definitions)
- All builtin, runner, and declaration files that use raw types

title: Return character offsets from find on Unicode strings
description:
The find builtin reports UTF-8 byte offsets for string searches, while direct selectors, substring, charAt, indexOf, lastIndexOf, and string size operations use character/rune indexes. This silently moves matches after any multibyte character.

Minimized reproductions:
- "éaé" find "é" returns [0,3]; DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 and InfoMunge lastIndexOf both identify the second match at character index 2.
- "éaé" find /é/ returns [[0,2],[3,5]] under InfoMunge existing start/end-pair convention; those are byte spans rather than character spans. Under that convention the spans should be [[0,1],[2,3]].

Likely source: findSubstringInString uses strings.Index offsets directly, while the regex paths expose regexp FindAllStringIndex byte spans. callBuiltinIndexOf already demonstrates the needed runeIndexFromByteOffset conversion.

Acceptance criteria:
- Literal and regex find results use the same character-index space as the rest of the string API.
- Convert both match starts and ends consistently for multibyte input.
- Preserve the existing ASCII result shape and values.
- Add accented-character and emoji cucumber regressions for literal and regex searches plus focused evaluator tests.

title: Return the DataWeave splitWhere fallback when no item matches
description: The dw::core::Arrays splitWhere wrapper is implemented as independent takeWhile and dropWhile calls. For `splitWhere([1,2,3,4], (x) -> x > 9)`, InfoMunge returns `{l:[1,2,3,4],r:[]}`, while DataWeave 2.11.0 returns `{l:[],r:[1,2,3,4]}`. The ordinary first-match case passes, so current coverage misses the sentinel path. Implement the no-match behavior explicitly, preserve null callback short-circuiting, and add exact Cucumber coverage for first match, middle match, no match, empty input, and null input.

title: Lazy filter silently skips non-boolean predicate results
Allow array literals as default-operator fallbacks
description:
The default operator cannot accept an array literal on its right side, preventing a normal fallback pattern and breaking larger collection pipelines.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision:
- `null default [1,2]` fails with `unexpected comma; expecting ]`; DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 returns `[1,2]`.
- `null default []` fails with `expected type, found )`; DataWeave returns `[]`.
- `(null default [1,2]) map $ * 2` fails before mapping; DataWeave returns `[2,4]`.
- `[null] map ($ default [1,2])` also fails, showing the problem inside a lambda body.

Scalar and object fallbacks work. A transform trace shows the core rewriter leaving the right-hand array as source syntax, after which `replaceDefaultOperator` produces `__default(null, [1, 2])`; the Go parser then interprets the bracket expression incorrectly because it was never rewritten to an array literal. This is a preprocessing-order interaction rather than evaluator default semantics.

Acceptance criteria:
- Empty, single-element, multi-element, and nested array literals work as default fallbacks.
- Array fallbacks work at top level, when explicitly grouped, and inside lambda bodies.
- Existing selector, range-selector, object-fallback, and default associativity behavior remains unchanged.
- Add focused preprocessor tests and cucumber regressions including a default-to-array pipeline followed by map.

title: Make direct string indexing and range slicing Unicode-safe
description:
Adversarial expression audit found that direct string selectors still use UTF-8 byte offsets even though string builtins were made rune-aware.

Minimized repros:
- "éx"[0] returns the JSON replacement character instead of "é".
- "éx"[1] returns the replacement character instead of "x".
- "éx"[-2] returns the replacement character instead of "é".
- "éx"[0 to 0] returns the replacement character instead of "é".

DataWeave returns the expected characters for these BMP Unicode cases. InfoMunge length, substring, charAt, charCodeAt, indexOf, and lastIndexOf already use rune indices, so selectors are internally inconsistent too.

Root cause:
- internal/evaluator/eval_index.go evalStringIndex uses len(s) and s[i:i+1].
- internal/evaluator/builtins_arrays_collections.go callBuiltinSlice uses len(strVal) and strVal[start:end] for strings.

This is distinct from closed issue bd-26y9, which fixed Unicode indexing in string builtins but did not cover selector syntax.

Acceptance criteria:
- Direct positive and negative string indexes operate in the same character-index space as the existing string builtins.
- String range slicing uses that same index space.
- Add cucumber regressions covering accented characters and emoji without producing invalid UTF-8.

title: Replace gopherjs with WebAssembly for standalone playground
description:
gopherjs is stuck at Go 1.20 and won't build with Go 1.26+. Replace it with a standard WASM build.

## Work required

1. Create cmd/infomunge-wasm/main.go
   - Build tag: //go:build js
   - Use syscall/js instead of github.com/gopherjs/gopherjs/js
   - Expose infomungeRun as a global JS function via js.FuncOf
   - Block main with a channel (select{}) so the wasm module stays alive
   - Same logic as cmd/infomunge-js/main.go: DecodeRunRequest -> BuildRunContext -> RunStringWithGoContextAndOptionsWithOutput -> ResolveOutputMimeType -> FormatRunResult
   - Return map keys: ok (bool), result (string), mimeType (string), error (string)
   - Note: js.ValueOf does not handle map[string]interface{}; build the return js.Value manually or encode as JSON and parse in JS

2. Build step
   - GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build -o docs/playground/infomunge.wasm ./cmd/infomunge-wasm

3. Copy wasm_exec.js
   - Source: $(go env GOROOT)/lib/wasm/wasm_exec.js (~17KB)
   - Dest: docs/playground/wasm_exec.js
   - Check into repo so playground works without Go toolchain present
   - Must be re-copied when Go toolchain is upgraded

4. Update docs/playground/index.html
   - Replace <script src="infomunge.js"></script> with:
     <script src="wasm_exec.js"></script>
     <script>
       const go = new Go();
       WebAssembly.instantiateStreaming(fetch('infomunge.wasm'), go.importObject)
         .then(result => go.run(result.instance));
     </script>
   - runScript() already checks window.infomungeRun; no other JS changes needed

5. Add Makefile target playground-wasm

6. Verify with a build-smoke cucumber or unit test

## Notes
- cmd/infomunge-js (gopherjs) can be left in place for historical reference
- js.FuncOf callbacks must not be GC'd; hold refs in package-level vars

title: Restore safe input-card DOM construction in the standalone playground
description: Problem: the previously closed XSS issue infomunge-97a6 was fixed in `internal/cli/playground.html`, but `docs/playground/index.html` still builds the input-name field with `card.innerHTML` and interpolates `defaultName` into an HTML attribute. The existing cucumber scenario named `Playground input cards avoid HTML interpolation of input names` only requests the server page, so the standalone regression is invisible and the full suite still passes. Impact: the two maintained playground copies have drifted, and the standalone copy retains an unsafe DOM-construction pattern that can become exploitable as soon as presets or restored state are externally supplied. Acceptance: construct the standalone input card with DOM APIs and `.value`, extend cucumber coverage to assert both playground variants reject the interpolation pattern, and reduce or explicitly manage duplicated shared playground code so future safety fixes reach both copies.

title: Fix dw::core::Arrays module import parse failures in go test ./...
description: After fixing bd-3pj3, repo-root go test ./... no longer fails in tmp but still fails in the Godog suite. The remaining failures are in features/arrays_module.feature, where imports of dw::core::Arrays fail with ParseError at line import statements. This appears unrelated to tmp package discovery and should be handled as a separate bug.

title: Allow contains to consume typeOf results
description: The 500-case differential audit found that function composition exposes an incomplete scalar coercion matrix. `contains(typeOf(71 + "877.003"), false)` returns `false` in DataWeave 2.11 but InfoMunge errors because argument 1 is `values.TypeValue`. Other string builtins already consume TypeValue through the shared scalar coercion helper: `upper(typeOf(1))` returns `"NUMBER"` and `startsWith(typeOf([]), "Arr")` returns true. `contains` has a separate type switch that accepts string, numeric, and boolean scalars but omits TypeValue, leaving the string-builtin coercion work from bd-2q0t inconsistent. Acceptance: align contains with the shared scalar coercion contract for TypeValue without changing array membership semantics; audit Regex and null behavior on both arguments; add focused unit, composed-function Cucumber, and differential coverage.

title: Decode escaped string literals in reduce initial values
description: Reduce accumulator defaults do not preserve ordinary string-literal semantics. With source [] reduce (x, acc = "a\nb") -> acc, current JSON output is "a\\nb" representing a literal backslash plus n, while evaluating the same string literal outside a parameter default produces a newline and serializes as "a\nb". Escapes in default arrays show the same problem. Root cause: parseDefaultValue recognizes surrounding quotes and returns s[1:len(s)-1] without strconv.Unquote, so escaped quotes, tabs, newlines, backslashes, and Unicode escapes are never decoded. Acceptance: reduce initial string values are decoded exactly like ordinary source string literals, including nested array and object defaults; malformed escapes report a positioned error; add focused evaluator and cucumber regressions.

title: Make documented test commands portable and consistently bounded
description: Problem: README.md and docs/TESTING.md wrap the cucumber coverage command with the external GNU `timeout` program even though `go test -timeout 5m` is already present and README lists only Go as a prerequisite. `timeout` is not supplied by a default macOS installation, and AGENTS.md forbids silently installing new software. Separately, MIND_MAP.md node 9 shows bare `go test -v ./test`, contrary to the five-minute policy in AGENTS.md and the other testing docs. The cucumber policy scenario currently hard-codes the external wrapper while omitting MIND_MAP.md from its consistency checks. Acceptance: use a portable bounded command or explicitly declare the dependency, align the MIND_MAP cucumber command with the five-minute policy, and update the policy scenario to enforce the intended command across all authoritative testing docs without requiring undeclared tooling.

title: Parse generated scientific-notation literals consistently
description: The strengthened differential harness in bd-3men found a DataWeave-success and InfoMunge-parser failure for generated exponent literals, including a contains argument using -4.4420514987125e+10 with a default expression containing 3.4133172375e+07. InfoMunge reports that underscore must separate successive digits, indicating exponent syntax is damaged or misparsed before evaluation. Acceptance: isolate the preprocessing or Go-parser interaction, support valid signed exponent notation in nested expressions, add focused preprocessor and cucumber regressions, and remove the linked differential allowlist rule.

title: Bind collection operators outside default expressions
description: The bounded differential suite found a precedence mismatch for `payload.name default flatten([[0]]) reduce (item, x) -> x` with payload `{"name":[]}`. InfoMunge returns `[]`, while DataWeave 2.11 returns `null`. This indicates InfoMunge binds `reduce` inside the right operand of `default`, while DataWeave applies `reduce` to the completed default expression; reducing the selected empty array without an initializer then yields null. Acceptance: align collection-operator precedence relative to `default` with DataWeave, audit the other collection operators at the same boundary, add focused preprocessor and cucumber coverage including the empty-array reproduction, and keep existing explicitly grouped behavior.

title: Make negative CLI cucumber steps assert command failure
description:
Problem:
Several Godog steps whose names say "and it fails" discard the run error and always return nil. Examples include test/godog_test.go:280, :288, :376, :387, :409, and :431. Follow-up assertions often use broad output/error substring checks, so an unexpectedly successful command can be treated as a valid negative-path setup if stdout happens to contain the expected text.

Risk:
Negative CLI scenarios can become vacuous and miss regressions where invalid input starts succeeding.

Required changes:
- Add a shared helper for expected CLI failures that asserts runCLI/runCLIWithStdin returned an error and lastExitCode is non-zero.
- Update all "and it fails" step implementations to use it.
- Keep separate assertions for stderr/stdout content after the failure has been established.
- Add a focused harness unit test or tiny feature scenario proving these steps fail when the command succeeds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every step registered with wording "and it fails" fails the scenario if the command exits successfully.
- Existing negative feature scenarios still pass after the stricter harness check.
- The new harness coverage fails before the fix and passes after it.

title: Bug: << and >> array operators have identical implementation
description:
The `<<` and `>>` operators in `internal/evaluator/evaluator.go` have identical implementations — both append an element to the right side of an array. `appendRight` (>>, line 387) and `arrayAppend` (<<, line 399) produce the same result: `[...array, element]`.

In DataWeave, these operators have distinct semantics. Having two operators that do the same thing is confusing. Either `<<` should prepend (creating `[element, ...array]`), or if both are intentionally append-right, one should be removed or the difference documented.

Test scenarios in `test/features/core_evaluator_runner_coverage.feature:131-179` confirm both produce the same append behavior. The chained test at line 321 (`([1] << 2) >> 3`) also treats them identically.

Files:
- `internal/evaluator/evaluator.go:387-408`
- `test/features/core_evaluator_runner_coverage.feature:131-179`

title: Preserve assigned artifact IDs when generating mutation candidates
description: Problem: recordMutationFailure passes an Artifact by value to failures.SaveArtifact, which assigns the sequential ID only to its private copy. The subsequent WriteCandidateScenario call receives the original zero-ID value, clamps it to ID 1, and therefore writes or skips 001_<property>.feature for every finding. Evidence: the stale mutation store contained artifacts 001 and 002 but only candidate 001. Impact: later unique failures do not receive reviewable candidate scenarios. Acceptance: candidate generation uses the ID assigned during persistence or reloads the saved artifact safely, retains fingerprint deduplication, and focused tests prove two distinct saved failures produce distinct correctly numbered candidates.

title: Collapse runner execution APIs into a cohesive facade
description:
Problem:
The runner exposes several overlapping entrypoints and compatibility wrappers: `RunFromStringWithContextAndOptionsAndGoContext`, `RunStringWithGoContextAndOptionsWithOutput`, `ExecuteStringWithGoContextAndOptions`, `FormatExecutionResult`, `PrintExecutionResult`, plus private `evaluate` and `formatOutput` paths. Callers have to choose between raw value, metadata tuple, structured result, formatted string, and stdout side effects.

Why it matters:
This keeps execution, formatting policy, context metadata, stdout behavior, and compatibility concerns coupled in one package. It makes new adapters such as CLI, HTTP, WASM, and tests more likely to pick a subtly different path and drift in behavior.

Evidence:
- `internal/cli/app.go` uses `ExecuteStringWithContextAndOptions` plus `FormatExecutionResult`.
- `internal/cli/server.go` and `cmd/infomunge-wasm/main.go` use `RunStringWithGoContextAndOptionsWithOutput`.
- `internal/runner/runner.go` still owns stdout helpers and deprecated compatibility wrappers.
- `internal/runner/execution.go` already has `ExecutionResult`, suggesting a better single return shape exists.

Suggested direction:
Make `ExecuteString(ctx, script, inputs/options) (ExecutionResult, error)` the main adapter API, then layer thin CLI stdout and compatibility functions around it or retire unused wrappers. Prefer returning `ExecutionResult` over multi-value tuples.

Acceptance:
- CLI, server, WASM, and godog use the same structured execution path.
- Multi-value runner APIs are deprecated or removed when no external callers remain.
- Formatting and printing stay outside the core execution function.

title: Grouped explicit map callback moves update expression outside the callback
description:
Parenthesizing an explicit callback causes a following update expression to be attached to the completed map instead of the callback body. The update silently becomes a no-op when its selector does not exist on the result array.

Reproduction:
  %dw 2.0
  output application/json
  ---
  [{a:1},{a:2}] map ((item) -> item update {
    case value at .a -> value + 10
  })

Actual InfoMunge:
  [{"a":1},{"a":2}]
Expected / DataWeave 2.11:
  [{"a":11},{"a":12}]

The equivalent ungrouped callback already works:
  [{a:1},{a:2}] map (item) -> item update { case value at .a -> value + 10 }

Parenthesizing the update expression inside the callback also works, so the bug is specifically the grouped-arrow boundary:
  [{a:1},{a:2}] map ((item) -> (item update { case value at .a -> value + 10 }))

Preprocessor evidence: TestPrepareForParsingPreservesParenthesizedOuterUpdate currently expects `source map ((item) -> item) update {...}` to become `__updateExpr(__map(source, (__lambda("item", item))), ...)`. That expectation enshrines the wrong DataWeave grouping: parentheses close the callback value but do not move the update outside the map. updateLeftOperandStartBytes/isCompleteGroupedLambdaBody appears to be the relevant boundary.

Acceptance criteria:
- A grouped explicit callback keeps an unparenthesized update in its body.
- A genuinely grouped completed collection, `(source map (item) -> item) update {...}`, still updates the collection outside.
- Implicit and ungrouped explicit callback behavior remains unchanged.
- Add differential/Cucumber regression coverage for the returned values.

title: Align object subtraction with DataWeave
description: The differential harness produced the minimized expression {} - 0.0. DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 returns {}, while InfoMunge reports cannot subtract map[string]interface {} and float64. Determine the DataWeave object subtraction and key-removal overload matrix, implement matching semantics without disturbing numeric subtraction, and add focused evaluator, Cucumber, and differential coverage.

title: Report undefined, pending, skipped, and ambiguous cucumber steps in failures formatter
description:
Problem:
The custom failures formatter records failed steps, but Skipped, Undefined, Pending, and Ambiguous callbacks are no-ops in test/failures_formatter.go:74-84. If a feature has an undefined or ambiguous step, the suite can return non-zero while the default formatter output omits the actual scenario and step that caused it.

Risk:
Broken step registration or typo regressions become harder to diagnose, especially with the minimal failures formatter used by default. Agents may see only a generic non-zero Godog result instead of the actionable missing/ambiguous step.

Required changes:
- Record undefined, pending, skipped, and ambiguous events with scenario, URI, step text, and any available error.
- Include those events in Summary alongside failed steps, with clear labels for the event type.
- Add formatter unit tests for at least undefined and ambiguous step reporting.

Acceptance criteria:
- A feature containing an undefined step prints the scenario and step text in failures format.
- Ambiguous step output includes the ambiguity error.
- Normal passing output remains concise.

title: Propagate null through supported collection operations
description:
Many supported collection operations reject `null`, while their DataWeave null-helper overloads propagate `null`. One builtin instead silently converts null to zero. This makes optional collection pipelines fail or change meaning.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision, compared with DataWeave CLI 2.11.0:
- `sizeOf(null)` returns `0`; expected `null`.
- `flatten(null)` errors; expected `null`.
- `null map (x) -> x`, `null filter (x) -> true`, and `null flatMap (x) -> [x]` error; each should return `null`.
- `null orderBy (x) -> x`, `null distinctBy (x) -> x`, and `null groupBy (x) -> x` error; each should return `null`.
- `null pluck (v, k) -> v`, `null mapObject (v, k) -> {(k): v}`, and `null filterObject (v, k) -> true` error; each should return `null`.

This does not include `maxBy(null, ...)` or `minBy(null, ...)`, which DataWeave correctly rejects; their empty-array behavior is tracked separately.

Likely source:
- Collection builtins perform concrete array/object assertions before considering a nil source.
- `callBuiltinSizeOf` has an explicit nil branch returning integer zero.
- Special collection operators evaluate and validate the lambda after source validation without a shared null-propagation path.

Acceptance criteria:
- The listed operations return language `null` for a null source, matching DataWeave helper overloads.
- Non-null type errors and lambda arity/type validation remain unchanged.
- Null propagation is implemented through a shared deliberate policy rather than scattered accidental exceptions where practical.
- Update the existing `sizeOf(nil) == 0` cucumber scenario and add null-source regressions across array and object operator families.

title: Apply collection operators to complete additive array sources
description:
An unparenthesized additive array expression followed by a collection operator is split at the final plus or minus token. This can silently map only the right-hand array or leave an unparseable earlier operator.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision:
- `[1,2] + [3,4] map $ * 10` returns `[1,2,30,40]`; based on the declared collection-versus-additive precedence and the explicitly grouped form, expected `[10,20,30,40]`.
- `[1,2] ++ [3,4] map $ * 10` fails with `expected EOF, found ++`; DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 returns `[10,20,30,40]`.
- `[1,2,3] -- [2] map $ * 10` fails with `expected EOF, found --`; DataWeave returns `[10,30]`.

Parenthesizing each complete source before map produces the expected values. A transform trace for the ++ case shows map consuming only `(3 to 4)` or the final array and emitting `++__map(...)` without separator whitespace; the later exact `replaceConcatenateOperator` contract can no longer recognize ` ++ `.

Likely source: `replaceCollectionOperator` uses the generic `FindLeftOperandStart`, whose additive stops prevent it from including the full lower-precedence source. The rewrite also drops the space needed by later configured operator transforms.

Acceptance criteria:
- Collection operators receive the complete left additive array expression according to the declared precedence, matching an explicitly grouped source.
- Cover ordinary array addition plus DataWeave ++ concatenation and -- removal.
- Additive expressions intentionally placed inside a lambda body remain part of the lambda body.
- Preserve left associativity, nested parentheses, string concatenation, object merge/removal, and existing collection-to-collection chaining.
- Add transform tests plus cucumber regressions including the silent partial-map result.

title: Keep bounded package gate under five minutes when dw is installed
description: The documented bounded command INFOMUNGE_SKIP_GODOG=1 go test ./... -timeout 5m times out when the external DataWeave CLI is available. TestDifferential_InfomungeVsDataWeave uses 500 default checks and consumed nearly the entire package budget; TestDWEval_Timeout then started near the deadline and the package was killed at five minutes. The isolated timeout test passed five consecutive runs, and the full package tree passed in 26 seconds when only TestDifferential_ was skipped. Acceptance: keep the default differential coverage meaningfully bounded when dw is installed, preserve an explicit soak path for the larger comparison budget, and make the documented five-minute repository gate pass on hosts both with and without dw.

title: Keep nested selectors inside implicit collection lambda bodies
description:
Selector transforms that run before functional transforms capture the whole outer implicit collection expression instead of the selector expression inside its lambda body. Clean wrong-result repro: `%im 0.1
output application/json
---
[{a: [1, 2]}, {a: [0, 3]}] map $.a[?($ == 2)]`. InfoMunge returns `[]`; the equivalent explicit lambda `map (x) -> x.a[?($ == 2)]` returns `[[2],[]]`. The transform trace shows `replaceFilterSelectors` rewriting the source as the completed `array map $.a`, then `replaceMapOperator` nests that map under `__filter_selector`. The same capture class affects range selectors: implicit `map $.a[0 to 0]` returns `[[1,2]]` instead of the explicit-lambda result `[[1],[0]]`; recursive descent `map $..name` returns `['a','b']` instead of `[['a'],['b']]`. Preserve lambda-local selector sources across filter, range, recursive, and metadata selector preprocessing, while retaining current top-level selector behavior. Add focused transform tests and cucumber regressions for at least filter, range, and recursive selectors.

title: Align infix mod precedence with DataWeave comparisons
description:
The recent infix mod precedence work aligned arithmetic operands but places mod above comparisons, which is not DataWeave precedence.

Minimized distinguishing expression:
10 mod 3 == 1

Current InfoMunge result: true
DataWeave CLI 2.11.0: evaluation error because it groups the expression as 10 mod (3 == 1), so the divisor is Boolean.
Both runtimes return true for the explicitly grouped (10 mod 3) == 1.

InfoMunge prepares the ungrouped source as:
mod(10, 3)== 1

Existing Cucumber coverage in operator_transformer_coverage.feature explicitly expects the incompatible true result, and TestModContractDeclaresDataWeavePrecedence asserts TransformPrecedenceComparison < TransformPrecedenceModulo. README calls infix mod the DataWeave-compatible operator and describes its unusual weak arithmetic precedence, so this remaining comparison boundary is surprising and can silently change whether a script succeeds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Verify and encode infix mod precedence relative to equality, ordering, logical, type, default/null-chain, and collection operators using DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 as the oracle.
- Ungrouped and explicitly parenthesized distinguishing cases match DataWeave.
- Correct contradictory transform and Cucumber expectations.
- Expand README's precedence note so users know where parentheses are required.
- Keep the left associativity and arithmetic precedence fixed by bd-1fm4.

title: Make post-processing pipeline mapping-aware
description:
The post-processing pipeline (CreateModularPostProcessingPipeline in internal/preprocessor/stages.go) runs approximately 40 transform stages after the rewriter phase. These stages (string interpolation, operator rewrites, arrow functions, filter/map/reduce operators, selector processing, syntax transforms) can all change string lengths.

However, ModularPipeline.Execute() only returns a string, not (string, []int). This means the character-level position mapping built by the rewriter is stale for the final output that goes to the Go parser. Error positions reported for expressions that undergo significant post-processing transforms may be approximate rather than exact.

To fix: each PipelineStage.Execute() would need to return (string, []int, error) and each transformHandler would need to produce a mapping. This affects approximately 40 transform functions across stages.go, transformers_syntax.go, transformers_lambda.go, transformers_operators.go, and related files.

title: Align string builtin coercion with DataWeave
description: The strengthened differential harness in bd-3men found DataWeave-success and InfoMunge-error cases for lower, upper, trim, startsWith, endsWith, and contains when generated arguments are numbers, booleans, or null. Current InfoMunge handlers require exact string operands while DataWeave applies broader coercion or null semantics. Acceptance: verify the overload/coercion matrix against DataWeave, implement the supported semantics consistently through shared helpers, add focused unit and cucumber coverage, and remove the linked differential allowlist rules.

title: Make test harness package vet- and build-compatible
description: Problem: go vet ./... and go build ./... fail in package infomunge/test because non-test step-definition files reference testContext, which is declared only in godog_test.go. The same package succeeds under go test because _test.go files are present. Impact: standard repository-wide vet and build gates cannot complete, masking findings in other packages. Acceptance: arrange the test harness types and step files so go vet ./... and go build ./... both succeed without weakening go test coverage; retain the existing cucumber behavior and bounded test commands.

title: Honor DataWeave callback arity across collection operators
description:
Problem

Collection operators reject callbacks that intentionally ignore supplied values, and `mapObject` also rejects the valid index parameter. DataWeave permits callbacks to declare any prefix of the parameters supplied by the operator.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision, compared with DataWeave CLI 2.11.0:

- `[1,2] map () -> 9` errors with `map lambda must have 1 or 2 parameters`; expected `[9,9]`.
- `[1,2] distinctBy () -> 0` errors; expected `[1]`.
- `{a:1,b:2} filterObject (v) -> v > 1` errors; expected `{b:2}`.
- `{a:1,b:2} mapObject (v) -> {(v as String): v}` errors; expected `{"1":1,"2":2}`.
- `{a:1,b:2} mapObject (v,k,i) -> {(k): i}` errors; expected `{a:0,b:1}`.

Likely source

`evalArrayAndLambdaWithNullPolicy` validates array callbacks against a minimum of one parameter. `evalMapObjectInputs` requires exactly two parameters. `callBuiltinFilterObject` requires two or three. The invocation helpers already bind only parameters that are present in several neighboring paths, such as `pluck`.

Acceptance criteria

- Array selector/predicate callbacks may declare zero through the maximum supported parameters and ignore the rest. Cover map, filter, flatMap, orderBy, distinctBy, groupBy, maxBy/minBy, takeWhile/dropWhile, and some/every where applicable.
- Object callbacks for mapObject, filterObject, and pluck consistently allow zero through three parameters: value, key, index.
- `mapObject` binds and exposes the index parameter.
- Direct user-function calls remain exact-arity; this change applies only when collection operations supply callback arguments.
- Null propagation and short-circuit behavior remain unchanged.
- Add focused evaluator tests and cucumber comparisons for zero-, one-, and three-parameter callbacks.

title: Correct the stale mapObject parameter-order cookbook note
description: docs/DATAWEAVE_COOKBOOK_EQUIVALENTS.md still states that InfoMunge reverses mapObject parameters and demonstrates `(key, val)`. Current evaluator behavior, MIND_MAP.md, feature coverage, and the completed compatibility work use DataWeave `(value, key, index)` order by default, with only a narrow legacy-name heuristic retained for compatibility. Update the syntax note and example to describe current behavior accurately, including any supported legacy form, and validate the example through the CLI documentation workflow.

title: Nested presence selector materializes false as null after a missing input path
description:
A nested dot-notation presence selector returns evaluator absence/null when an intermediate external-input field is missing, instead of the Boolean false. This can also make an if condition fail.

Minimal reproduction:

payload.json:
  {"items":[{"profile":{"age":20}},{}]}

script:
  %dw 2.0
  output application/json
  ---
  payload.items map $.profile.age?

Actual InfoMunge result:
  [true,null]

Expected result (and DataWeave 2.11 result):
  [true,false]

A composed condition fails more severely:
  payload.items map (if ($.profile.age?) $.profile.age else 0)

InfoMunge errors with "if condition must be a boolean, got *evaluator.absentValue"; DataWeave returns [20,0].

Likely cause: VisitIndexExpr/evalAbsentAware preserves the absent provenance when evalIndex on a materialized-null intermediate returns nil. selectorModePresence is a semantic boundary and should consume an absent source as false, analogous to missing-key presence on an object.

Acceptance criteria:
- Presence on a missing final or intermediate external-input path returns false.
- It remains Boolean inside conditionals and collection callbacks.
- Existing default/absence propagation for ordinary selectors is unchanged.
- Add focused evaluator coverage and end-to-end Cucumber coverage.

title: Align cucumber test commands with the 5-minute timeout policy
description:
Problem:
AGENTS.md requires a 5 minute timeout for cucumber tests, but Makefile cucumber targets use go test -timeout 10m at Makefile:9, :13, and :17, while the single-feature target at Makefile:21 has no explicit timeout. The nested "go test ./..." cucumber step in test/godog_test.go:296-306 also runs without an explicit timeout.

Risk:
Local and agent-driven cucumber runs can exceed the intended feedback budget or hang longer than expected, especially through the repo-wide regression feature.

Required changes:
- Change cucumber Makefile targets to use a 5 minute go test timeout.
- Add an explicit timeout to the single-feature target.
- Give the nested repo-wide go test step a bounded timeout, either through context cancellation or a go test -timeout value, while preserving INFOMUNGE_SKIP_GODOG=1.
- Update docs/TESTING.md if it documents a different expected command.

Acceptance criteria:
- All cucumber entry points have an explicit 5 minute timeout.
- The repo-wide go test regression step cannot run unbounded inside a cucumber scenario.
- The full cucumber suite and the go_test_all_regression feature still pass.

title: Fix stale CLI examples and format notes in docs
description: Fresh-eyes audit found several user-facing docs examples that no longer match the CLI. README.md:28-29 use -i payload <payload.json> and -i input2 <inout2.json>, but the parser validates inputs as name=source in internal/io/input.go and the help text says -i name=source. Shell input redirection makes the README examples fail instead of binding files. docs/DATAWEAVE_COOKBOOK_EQUIVALENTS.md:775,895,902,905 and docs/lazy-evaluation.md:43 repeat the stale -i payload file shape. README.md:65-68 uses double backslashes at bash line ends, which breaks the curl line continuation. README.md:157-160 and tmp/README.md mention go run ./inspect.go even though no tmp/inspect.go exists. README.md:8-9 implies Java properties can be emitted, but pkg/formats/properties.go only registers a reader. Acceptance: update examples to current syntax such as -i payload=payload.json or explicit stdin via -s json, fix curl continuations, remove or generalize nonexistent tmp helper references, and align the format support wording with registered readers/writers.

title: Provide a working launch workflow for the standalone WASM playground
description: Problem: README.md:91 and MIND_MAP.md node 16 tell users to open `docs/playground/index.html` directly. The page bootstraps with `fetch("infomunge.wasm")`, which requires an HTTP origin in normal browsers, and its own error text says to serve it over HTTP. Calling it a local JS runner is also inaccurate because JavaScript only bootstraps the Go WASM runner. Impact: following the documented standalone instructions leaves `window.infomungeRun` unavailable and the playground cannot execute scripts. Acceptance: provide a repository-supported HTTP serving command or Make target that needs no undeclared software, update README.md and MIND_MAP.md with the exact build and launch flow, distinguish local WASM from `/run` server mode, and add a browser or cucumber smoke check that loads the WASM assets through that documented flow.

title: Preserve nested collection expressions inside lambda bodies
description:
Nested collection operators inside an outer lambda body are regrouped as operations on the lambda or outer collection instead of remaining inside the body.

Minimized differential reproduction on the current revision:
- Expression: `[[1]] map ($ map 1)`
- DataWeave 2.11.0: `[[1]]`
- InfoMunge: `map expects a lambda function, got []interface {}`

Explicit lambdas expose the same boundary failure:
- `[[1]] map ((x) -> x map (y) -> y)` succeeds in DataWeave with `[[1]]` but InfoMunge reports `map expects an array, got *evaluator.Lambda`.
- Adding parentheses around the inner collection expression makes the explicit form work, which shows that the individual map implementations are sound and the expression boundary is wrong.

Likely seam: `replaceImplicitLambdas`, `scanLambdaBody`, and `replaceArrowFunctions` each scan collection keywords while transforms run to a fixpoint. A nested collection keyword can terminate or rewrite the outer body before ownership of the nested expression is preserved.

Acceptance criteria:
- Nested collection expressions remain inside explicit and implicit outer lambda bodies.
- Cover implicit outer plus implicit inner, explicit outer plus explicit inner, and mixed explicit or implicit combinations.
- Cover grouped and ungrouped inner bodies and at least map, filter, and flatMap.
- Add focused preprocessor trace or transform tests plus end-to-end Cucumber regressions against the minimized expressions.

title: Make the test-unit target run the repository unit suite
description:
Problem: Makefile describes test-unit as "Run unit tests only (exclude cucumber)", but it runs only go test ./test -run Test[^F]. That omits every unit-test package under internal and pkg, and the name-based filter also excludes legitimate tests whose names begin TestF, including failures-formatter tests. The command succeeds while exercising only a small fraction of what its name promises.

Evidence: make test-unit reports only package infomunge/test. The documented repository unit command already exists in README.md and docs/TESTING.md as INFOMUNGE_SKIP_GODOG=1 go test ./... -timeout 5m.

Acceptance: make test-unit uses the bounded repo-wide non-Godog path, does not filter legitimate tests by name, and a workflow test or documented validation proves representative internal, pkg, and test-package unit tests are included. Consolidate the duplicate test and test-failures targets if no distinct behavior is intended.

title: Align numeric ordinal indexing with DataWeave
description: While defining numeric keyed-selector behavior for bd-3ryv, a live DataWeave comparison showed that ordinal indexing also differs: (1)[0] returns the string "1" in DataWeave while InfoMunge reports cannot index into int. Audit integer and decimal values with positive, negative, and out-of-range ordinal indexes; define number string-rendering semantics; add focused evaluator and Cucumber coverage; and add differential generation when compatible.

title: Make runner stdout capture safe for large output and panics
description:
Problem:
captureRunnerStdout redirects process-global os.Stdout to a pipe, runs runner.RunFromStringWithContext synchronously, then reads the pipe after the runner returns (test/godog_test.go:687-702). If the runner writes more than the pipe buffer, the test can deadlock because no goroutine is draining stdout. os.Stdout is also restored only after the run and read complete, so a panic would leave the process stdout redirected.

Risk:
Cucumber scenarios using "I run the script through the runner output path" can hang on large outputs and can contaminate later tests if a panic escapes while stdout is redirected.

Required changes:
- Drain the pipe concurrently while runner.RunFromStringWithContext executes.
- Restore os.Stdout with defer immediately after a successful pipe swap.
- Close pipe descriptors on all paths.
- Add focused harness coverage with output large enough to exceed a typical pipe buffer.

Acceptance criteria:
- Large runner-output-path scenarios complete without deadlock.
- os.Stdout is restored even when the runner path returns an error or panics in a controlled test.
- Existing runner_output_formatting cucumber scenarios still pass.

title: Document the complete supported-format and fidelity matrix
description: Problem: README.md only names JSON, XML, CSV, YAML, Java properties, and text, while `pkg/formats` registers additional NDJSON, URL-encoded, multipart, flatfile, protobuf, XLSX, Java, Avro, DataWeave, and binary MIME types and extensions. Some binary families default to opaque byte passthrough and only gain structured behavior through format-specific options, so a flat list of claimed support would also be misleading. No current user-facing document gives readers the MIME aliases, extensions, read/write direction, option requirements, or fidelity level. Impact: implemented capabilities are undiscoverable and users cannot tell a structured codec from raw passthrough. Acceptance: add a user-facing matrix sourced from the registry that lists canonical MIME types and aliases, extensions, input/output support, structured options or schema requirements, and explicit limitations; link it from README.md; keep Java properties input-only wording; and add a Go or cucumber consistency check so registrations and documentation cannot silently drift.

title: Support inline if values in one-line object literals
description: While working bd-3ko6, PrepareForParsing rejected one-line object values such as foo: if (true) 1 else 2 when wrapped as a top-level object. The core rewriter branch scanner can treat the object-closing brace as a branch close and report branch scan or brace errors before the intended parse result. Acceptance: add cucumber or unit coverage for object fields whose value is an inline if expression; fix branch scanning so object boundaries terminate the value cleanly without corrupting source maps.

title: Preserve fractional bounds in to ranges
description:
The to builtin silently truncates decimal bounds to int64 before constructing a range, changing both the values and the number of values returned.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision:
- 1.9 to 3.1 returns [1,2,3]; DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 returns [1.9,2.9].
- 3.1 to 1.9 returns [3,2,1]; DataWeave returns [3.1,2.1].
- Function syntax to(1.9, 3.1) reaches the same implementation and has the same truncation.

Likely source: callBuiltinTo in internal/evaluator/builtins_math.go casts float64 bounds to int64, then appends float64(i). This is separate from range-selector indexing, where truncating numeric indexes matches the observed DataWeave behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Generated ranges begin at the exact supplied numeric bound and advance or retreat by one until the opposite bound would be crossed.
- Integer inputs retain the existing inclusive integer results.
- Decimal ascending and descending ranges do not silently discard fractional components.
- Add evaluator and cucumber coverage for both infix and function syntax, ascending and descending decimal ranges.

title: Make builtin registration domain-owned and descriptor-based
description:
Fresh-eyes cohesion/coupling audit finding.

Problem:
Builtin registration is centralized in one large evaluator registry even though implementations are split by domain. This creates a high-coupling edit point for every builtin addition and makes metadata like arity, evaluation strategy, module ownership, and docs implicit.

Evidence:
- `internal/evaluator/modular_registry.go` manually lists all special and regular builtins in two large maps.
- Handler functions live across many `builtins_*` files, but each new function still requires editing the central registry.
- Special vs regular evaluation strategy is represented only by which map the name appears in.
- There is no first-class builtin descriptor carrying arity, category/module, laziness, or user-facing docs.

Suggested direction:
- Introduce `BuiltinSpec` descriptors with name, category/module, arity, evaluation mode (eager/special), and handler.
- Let each builtin domain file register or expose its own specs, with the central registry only aggregating slices.
- Keep thread-safe override hooks for tests.

Acceptance criteria:
- Adding a builtin in one domain can be done without editing a giant cross-domain map.
- Registry tests validate duplicate names, invalid specs, and special/eager dispatch.
- Existing builtin lookup APIs continue to work during migration.
- Add a small docs/test helper that can enumerate builtins by category to prove metadata is usable.

title: Support text/plain output formatting
description: text/plain is registered only as an input reader, but server output normalization can select text/plain and scripts may reasonably request text/plain output. Formatting then fails with unsupported output mimeType. Register a text/plain writer with documented stringification semantics and add cucumber coverage for CLI and /run text/plain output.

title: Keep DW-incompatible plus extensions out of differential generation
description:
The current 500-case differential soak can generate mixed array/string plus expressions under DWCompatExpression even though InfoMunge and DataWeave intentionally assign different semantics to that shape.

Command:
INTENSIVE_TEST_SOAK=1 go test -v ./internal/testing/differential/ -timeout 15m

Observed seed: 12564718022417330621
Rapid minimized expression: [""] + ""

Current InfoMunge result: the string "[]", via InfoMunge's documented string + any concatenation extension.
DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 result: ["",""], because array + value appends the value.

The soak failed after 79 generated cases and wrote a differential artifact/failfile. This is not an evaluator regression under the stated InfoMunge extension; it is a false DW-compatible classification. The existing generator guidance notes that nonnumeric string concatenation is an extension and assumes DataWeave will reject it, but DataWeave accepts array + string with array-append semantics, so the harness reaches StructuralCompare and fails.

Acceptance criteria:
- DWCompatExpression emits + only for operand-type combinations with shared InfoMunge/DataWeave semantics.
- In particular, do not generate array-left/string-right as a compatible string-concatenation case.
- Add generator self-tests for allowed and excluded + operand categories.
- Add a regression using the minimized expression or recorded seed without relying on a persistent Rapid failfile.
- The bounded and 500-case differential workflows no longer fail on this known language extension.

title: Remove stale helper layers and test-only error-discarding adapters
description:
Repository-wide caller searches found a new layer of stale production helpers left behind by recent refactors. Several have no callers at all, while a family of preprocessor adapters exists only so unit tests can call a string-only wrapper that discards mapping and error results.

No-caller examples:
- preprocessor: inferredErrorTransform, findTypedOperatorLeftOperandStart, scanTypedOperatorRight, isBranchOpener, appendDotNotationSelector, normalizeCondition, and replaceRegexLiterals.
- runner: isDirectiveLine, collapseWhitespaceOutsideStrings, and parseFunctionDeclarationLine.
- expression generator: expressionAtDepth.
- evaluator: withGoContext and GetGoContext.

Test-only evaluator surface:
AsString, AsInt, AsFloat, AsNumber, AsBool, IsNil, and IsNumeric are referenced only by tests; production uses direct assertions or the actually shared AsArray, AsObject, and AsLambda helpers.

Test-only preprocessor adapters:
replaceDefaultOperator and many parallel replaceXOperator wrappers delegate to the mapping/error-aware implementation and discard returned errors. The production stage registry uses configuredBinaryOperatorTransform or mapping-aware handlers directly. Focused tests can exercise those real handlers instead of preserving a second API.

Acceptance criteria:
- Recheck callers with symbol-aware or repository-wide search and remove helpers with no production or compatibility obligation.
- Migrate focused tests to mapping/error-aware implementations before deleting string-only wrappers.
- Keep helpers that encode a genuinely distinct contract and document that distinction.
- Reassess RegisterObjectOrder: its keys parameter is never passed anything but nil in-tree, so fold it into NewObject or add the missing concrete use rather than retaining an unused public mutation seam.
- Run vet, focused package tests, and the bounded repository suite after removal.

title: Keep identifier-sourced collection pipelines inside ungrouped explicit lambdas
description:
Adversarial differential review found a remaining lambda-body ownership defect after the prior nested-collection fixes.

Silent wrong-result reproduction:

%im 0.1
output application/json
var xs = [[1], [2,3]]
---
[0,0] map (ignored) -> xs map sizeOf($)

Current InfoMunge result: [2,2]
DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 result: [[1,2],[1,2]]

The prepared source is:
__map(__map([]interface{}{0,0,}, __lambda("ignored", xs)), __lambda("__arg", sizeOf(__arg)))

The inner identifier-sourced map escaped the explicit lambda and became a second outer map. This also breaks lambdas outside collection callbacks:
- [1,2] then (xs) -> xs map ($ * 2) errors with "map expects an array, got *evaluator.Lambda"; DataWeave returns [2,4].
- A captured identifier in null onNull () -> xs map ($ * 2) fails the same way.
- fun apply(v, f) = f(v) followed by apply([1,2], (xs) -> xs map ($ * 2)) fails; DataWeave returns [2,4].

Grouping the lambda body, such as (xs map ($ * 2)), makes these expressions work. Array literals and completed calls as inner sources also work, isolating the gap to identifier-sourced pipelines and delimiter/context handling.

Likely seam: collectionSourceOwnsOperator deliberately treats scalar-looking identifiers as outer-chaining bodies, and replaceArrowFunctions/collection scans lose the fact that an explicit arrow is bounded by a call argument, configured-operator RHS, or enclosing lambda. The fix must retain InfoMunge's documented unparenthesized outer chaining where the operator really follows a completed lambda.

Acceptance criteria:
- Identifier-sourced collection operators remain inside ungrouped explicit arrow bodies when the arrow is syntactically bounded by a callback, function argument, then, or onNull expression.
- The silent wrong-result reproduction matches DataWeave.
- Cover map/filter/reduce plus at least one object operator.
- Preserve existing outer-chaining cases and grouped-body behavior.
- Add focused prepared-source assertions and end-to-end Cucumber regressions.

title: Resolve negative indexes in update expression paths
description: DataWeave differential repro: [1,2,3] update { case x at [-1] -> x * 10 } returns [1,2,30]. InfoMunge silently returns [1,2,3]. The nested form {a:[1,2,3]} update { case x at .a[-1] -> x * 10 } fails the same way. Direct selectors already resolve negative indexes from the end, but getValueAtPath and setValueAtPath reject every negative update index. Normalize negative update indexes relative to each current array before bounds checks, retain no-op behavior for truly out-of-range paths, and add top-level and nested Cucumber regressions.

title: Improve post-processing mapping precision with per-transform mappings
description:
Current pipeline mapping support is stage-level and uses inferred string alignment between each stage's input/output. This is a major improvement over stale mappings, but it can still be approximate for heavily rewritten middle segments.

Follow-up:
- Add optional exact mapping support to individual transform handlers (for operators/selectors/syntax rewrites with known token edits)
- Prefer exact per-transform composition where available, and fall back to inferred alignment otherwise
- Add focused cucumber scenarios that assert exact columns for representative complex rewrites

title: Preserve exact integers when decoding JSON and NDJSON
description: JSON decoding uses json.Decoder.Token without UseNumber, so every JSON number arrives as float64. A file containing value 9007199254740993 is read and emitted as 9.007199254740992e+15, silently changing the integer. NDJSON delegates to the same reader. This conflicts with the evaluator exact-integer work and can make input equality, ordering, aggregation, and output mathematically wrong even when the script performs no arithmetic. docs/FORMATS.md currently hides the loss behind the phrase Go JSON semantics rather than stating the precision boundary. Acceptance: decode integral JSON numbers into the runtime exact integer representation when in range, apply an explicit policy for out-of-range integers and decimals, preserve trailing-content validation and object order, cover JSON and NDJSON with values on both sides of 2^53 and runtime integer bounds, and update the fidelity matrix to state the resulting contract.

title: Fix multi-character single-quoted output option values
description: Problem: runner output-option parsing explicitly accepts both double- and single-quoted values, but unquoteOptionValue delegates both forms to strconv.Unquote. Go treats single quotes as rune literals, so a multi-character value such as skipNullOn='elements' is left with quote characters and later rejected by XML option validation. Single-character values happen to work, making the behavior inconsistent. Evidence: go run ./cmd/infomunge with output application/xml skipNullOn='elements' returns a ValidationError whose invalid skipNullOn value still contains the surrounding single quotes. The equivalent double-quoted value is covered and works. Code: internal/runner/runner.go parseOutputOptions and unquoteOptionValue. Acceptance: parse supported single-quoted option strings with InfoMunge/DataWeave string rules rather than Go rune rules; keep escaping behavior defined; add table-driven runner tests for empty, one-character, multi-character, escaped, and malformed values in both quote styles; add user-visible XML output coverage proving a multi-character single-quoted value such as elements works.

title: Keep string search operands literal unless explicitly Regex
description:
Several string operations guess whether an ordinary string is a regex by inspecting its characters. Valid literal delimiters can therefore change operator semantics and silently produce unrelated results even though InfoMunge already has explicit Regex values from /.../ literals and regex(...).

Minimized reproductions on the current revision (DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 as oracle):
- "abc" contains "|" returns true; DataWeave returns false.
- "abc" find "|" returns [[0,0],[1,1],[2,2],[3,3]]; DataWeave returns [].
- "a|b" replace "|" with "X" returns "XaX|XbX"; DataWeave returns "aXb".
- "a|b" splitBy "|" returns ["a","|","b"]; DataWeave returns ["a","b"].

Likely source: looksLikeRegexPattern in internal/evaluator/regex_policy.go treats metacharacters in string values as an implicit regex signal. contains, find, replace, and splitBy all use this heuristic. Existing ASCII scenarios cover some heuristic behavior but do not distinguish ordinary metacharacter text from explicit regex syntax.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ordinary string operands use literal substring/delimiter semantics regardless of regex metacharacters.
- Explicit Regex values continue to use regular-expression semantics for every supported operation.
- Audit all looksLikeRegexPattern callers and update tests that currently encode implicit-regex guessing.
- Add cucumber regressions for pipe, brackets, backslash, plus, and question-mark literals alongside explicit regex equivalents.

title: Align out-of-range selector behavior with DataWeave
description: DataWeave 2.11 returns null when a range selector includes an index outside the collection, while InfoMunge preserves its historical slice-style behavior by clamping an end bound or returning an empty collection for some invalid starts. Confirmed with array ranges 1 to 5, -5 to 1, and 5 to 7 against a three-element array while completing bd-cjj3. Decide and document the intended InfoMunge subset contract. If compatibility is intended, update __rangeIndex and add Cucumber coverage for ascending and descending out-of-range selectors over arrays and strings, including how this relates to InfoMunge direct-index errors.

title: Reject unresolved identifiers instead of evaluating their names as strings
description:
Adversarial expression audit found that unresolved identifiers silently evaluate to their source spelling.

Minimized repros on the current revision:
- missing returns the JSON string missing.
- missing + 1 returns missing1.
- missing == "missing" returns true.

DataWeave rejects each expression because the reference cannot be resolved. The current behavior can fabricate successful output from a misspelled variable name.

Root cause: internal/evaluator/evaluator.go evalIdent returns e.Name when the identifier is absent from the context. That fallback is also used to make unquoted object keys work because VisitCompositeLit evaluates key identifiers through the general expression visitor.

Expected work:
- Return a positional unresolved-reference error for identifiers not present in scope.
- Preserve unquoted object-literal keys by handling identifier keys explicitly in VisitCompositeLit rather than weakening general name resolution.
- Verify declared variables, lambda parameters, builtin identifiers, and object keys remain valid.
- Add cucumber coverage showing a misspelled reference fails instead of becoming output data.

title: Count Unicode characters instead of bytes in size operations
description: Unicode size expressions count UTF-8 bytes while the rest of the string API uses character indexes. On current @, sizeOf("é") and "é".^size both return 2 instead of 1; "é🙂" returns 6 while length("é🙂") returns 2. A composed repro, "é"[0 to sizeOf("é") - 1], returns null because the byte count produces an out-of-range character bound instead of returning "é". Root cause: callBuiltinSizeOf and callBuiltinMetadata use len(string); the haveSize assertion matcher does the same. Direct indexes, range indexes, substring, charAt, and length already operate on runes. Acceptance: all user-visible string cardinality operations use the same Unicode character unit; preserve byte counts only for explicit binary values; add accented-character and emoji cucumber regressions plus focused tests for metadata and assertion size.

title: Support implicit $ and $$ callbacks for mapObject
description:
Implicit lambda rewriting covers the collection-operator family except mapObject, so valid DataWeave shorthand is left as raw dollar tokens.

Minimized reproduction:
{a:1,b:2} mapObject {($$): $ * 10}

Current InfoMunge result: parse error "illegal character U+0024 '$'"
DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 result: {"a":10,"b":20}

The prepared InfoMunge source remains:
mapObject(map[string]interface{}{"a":1,"b":2,}, map[string]interface{}{($$): $ * 10,})

A composed reproduction also fails:
[{a:1,b:2}] map ($ mapObject {($$): $ * 10})
DataWeave returns [{"a":10,"b":20}], while InfoMunge eventually tries to multiply the outer object by 10.

Source evidence: implicitLambdaOperators in internal/preprocessor/transformers_lambda.go includes map, filter, reduce, groupBy, sort, extrema, orderBy, distinctBy, filterObject, flatMap, and pluck, but omits mapObject even though CollectionOperators includes it and the evaluator supports value/key callbacks.

Acceptance criteria:
- mapObject accepts implicit callbacks with $ bound to value and $$ bound to key.
- Direct and nested mapObject shorthand match the equivalent explicit (value, key) -> callback.
- Dollar handling inside strings and regex payloads retains the existing syntax-aware behavior.
- Add focused preprocessor and Cucumber coverage, including a nested collection expression.

title: Complete null-helper behavior for dw::core::Arrays functions
description:
Problem

The null propagation work in bd-2of4 covers core collection operators but leaves public dw::core::Arrays functions inconsistent with their DataWeave null helper overloads. Optional array pipelines therefore error or return a non-null structure.

Confirmed against DataWeave CLI 2.11.0

- some(null, (x) -> true) errors; expected false.
- every(null, (x) -> true) errors; expected true.
- takeWhile(null, (x) -> true) and dropWhile(null, (x) -> true) error; expected null.
- divideBy(null, 2), firstWith(null, ...), and indexWhere(null, ...) error; expected null.
- partition(null, (x) -> true) returns {success: null, failure: null}; expected null.
- The same wrapper pattern affects splitWhere and sumBy, whose DataWeave signatures include null helpers returning null.

Likely source

Native array callbacks use rejectNullCollectionSource, and module scripts compose null-propagating operations into later builtins that reject null or wrap it in an object.

Acceptance criteria

- Match the DataWeave null overload result for every exported Arrays function.
- Do not evaluate callback bodies for null inputs.
- Preserve current non-null type and callback validation.
- Add table-driven or cucumber coverage for native-backed and script-composed module functions, including the false and true identities of some and every.

title: Correct stale cookbook body syntax and output claims
description: docs/DATAWEAVE_COOKBOOK_EQUIVALENTS.md still contains stale claims outside the summary table. CLI validation shows object values accept concatenation and other operator expressions without parentheses, and nested mapObject callbacks can return object literals inside mapped object values, contrary to the opening syntax note and section 4 limitation note. The keysOf and entriesOf examples also show alphabetical output despite current insertion-order behavior. Audit the body examples, remove or revise substantiated obsolete limitations, align expected object-order output, prefer current DataWeave callback order where examples rely on legacy parameter-name heuristics, and validate representative examples through the CLI documentation workflow.

title: Remove the redundant XML pre-validator that rejects valid XML
description: pkg/formats/readXML first runs a 268-line hand-written XMLStateMachine and then parses the same input with encoding/xml. The pre-validator is not XML compliant: it only understands double-quoted attributes and treats every declaration beginning with <! as a comment. A valid input containing marker=greater-than in a single-quoted attribute plus a CDATA section is rejected before encoding/xml can parse it. This duplicates parsing logic, adds maintenance surface, and creates false negatives. Acceptance: make encoding/xml the single syntax authority while retaining explicit InfoMunge depth, element, attribute, and text limits; remove obsolete state-machine code and declaration-only wrappers where possible; add cucumber and focused regressions for single-quoted attributes, CDATA, comments, processing instructions, and malformed nesting.

title: Align nested typeOf results with DataWeave Type values
description: The bounded live differential gate found typeOf(typeOf(false)) returns String in InfoMunge but Type in DataWeave. Reproduction: %dw 2.0 output application/json --- typeOf(typeOf(false)). Audit runtime Type value representation and typeOf behavior, then add focused evaluator, Cucumber, and differential regression coverage. Discovered while validating bd-2urk with rapid seed 5845521610449147825.

title: Split runner execution engine from formatting and IO adapters
description:
Fresh-eyes cohesion/coupling audit finding.

Problem:
`internal/runner` currently owns too many responsibilities at once:
- file reading and base-dir discovery (`Run`, `RunWithConfig`)
- header parsing and context construction (`evaluateWithContext`, `parseHeaderWithGoContext`)
- module loading setup (`NewModuleLoader`)
- preprocessing and source-map composition
- evaluator invocation
- lazy/stream resolution
- output serialization and stdout printing (`formatOutputWithContext`)
- XML-specific output option interpretation (`ApplyXMLOutputOptions`)

This makes the runner the gravitational center for unrelated changes. A change to output formatting, module loading, source-map handling, or evaluation API tends to touch `internal/runner/runner.go`, which increases regression risk and makes library extraction harder.

Evidence:
- `internal/runner/runner.go` is 526 lines and imports evaluator, preprocessor, sourcemap, stringutils, formats, os, filepath, strconv, and fmt.
- The public runner API has overlapping entrypoints (`RunFromStringWithContextAndOptions`, `RunStringWithGoContextAndOptionsWithOutput`, `RunStringWithGoContext`, etc.) that expose internal pipeline shape rather than a cohesive execution result.
- `formatOutputWithContext` prints to stdout directly, while other adapters need returned strings.

Suggested direction:
- Introduce a small execution service/API that returns a structured `ExecutionResult` containing value, header/output metadata, eval context, and source-map-aware errors.
- Move stdout/file adapters to CLI-facing code.
- Move result resolution and output serialization behind explicit collaborators rather than keeping them in runner.
- Preserve current public functions as compatibility wrappers initially.

Acceptance criteria:
- New internal API can evaluate a script without printing or formatting.
- CLI output path is an adapter over that API.
- Existing runner entrypoints remain behavior-compatible or have focused migration notes.
- Add/adjust cucumber coverage for CLI output plus an in-process runner path to catch behavior drift.

title: Split structured protobuf format support into smaller modules
description:
`pkg/formats/protobuf_structured.go` is carrying too many responsibilities in one 1.5k-line file: option parsing, schema construction from two sources, descriptor traversal, raw wire decoding, raw wire encoding, map-entry handling, packed-field support, and number coercion helpers.

Evidence:
- `pkg/formats/protobuf_structured.go:80-215` handles option parsing plus descriptor-backed schema construction.
- `pkg/formats/protobuf_structured.go:290-544` builds schema objects from descriptors and schema literals.
- `pkg/formats/protobuf_structured.go:547-861` performs decode-time wire parsing, including map-entry handling.
- `pkg/formats/protobuf_structured.go:863-1173` performs encode-time wire generation with large kind switches.
- `pkg/formats/protobuf_structured.go:1175-1507` contains low-level wire skipping and numeric conversion helpers.

Why this matters:
- There is no narrow seam for reviewing or testing changes to just schema handling, decoding, or encoding.
- The same domain concepts (`protobufField`, wire types, strictness rules) are touched by distant sections of the same file, increasing change risk.
- Future features like enum names, unknown-field preservation, or oneof support will compound the existing file-level complexity.

Suggested direction:
- Split this implementation into smaller files/modules by concern: options/schema, descriptor import, decoder, encoder, wire helpers/conversions.
- Introduce targeted tests per layer instead of relying on large end-to-end coverage only.
- Consider small internal types/interfaces that make encode/decode rules composable without sharing one giant switch surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- Structured protobuf logic is split into smaller units with clear ownership boundaries.
- Decoder and encoder logic can be tested independently from schema parsing.
- Numeric coercion and wire helper code are isolated from high-level format option handling.

title: Remap evaluator builtin positional errors instead of rendering 0:0
description: Many evaluator builtins construct failures through newPosError. That helper calls EvalPositional with an empty token.FileSet, which eagerly attaches a zero line and column. sourcemap.Map.FormatEvalError trusts any attached unified error position and therefore renders :0:0 instead of remapping the generated AST token position. This was reproduced while fixing orderBy: using a posError with the AST position correctly rendered 4:1. Repository search finds hundreds of newPosError call sites. Acceptance: make the common positional error path preserve generated token positions for source-map remapping, audit callers that genuinely need already-resolved positions, add focused evaluator and runner regressions proving representative builtin failures report source line and column rather than 0:0, and keep error types and messages compatible.

title: Return client errors for invalid server output formatting
description: Problem: the /run handler treats every runner.FormatExecutionResult failure as an internal fault: it logs the error and returns HTTP 500 with internal server error. Many formatting failures are caused entirely by the request or script, such as selecting CSV for a scalar or object, requesting an unsupported qualified MIME type, or providing invalid XML output options. The same validation errors are reported directly by the CLI, but the server misclassifies them and hides actionable feedback. Evidence: internal/cli/server.go sends StatusInternalServerError for any format error after request parsing and evaluation; pkg/formats returns ValidationError for incompatible CSV shapes and unsupported writers. No server feature covers this boundary. Acceptance: distinguish client-caused parse, validation, and unsupported-format failures from genuine internal formatting faults; return a sanitized 4xx response with useful diagnostics for the former while retaining generic 5xx handling and server-side logging for the latter; add /run coverage for incompatible CSV output, invalid XML options, and an unsupported requested MIME type.

title: Prevent user functions from hijacking generated syntax helpers
description:
Problem

Preprocessing lowers language syntax to ordinary names such as __default, __lambda, __map, and __coerce. User function resolution intentionally wins over builtins, so a user declaration with one of those implementation names intercepts generated calls and changes unrelated language syntax.

Reproduction

%im 0.1
fun __default(a, b) = 99
output application/json
---
null default 5

Current result: 99. Expected result: 5. A __lambda declaration can likewise break every generated arrow lambda. Shadowing __default also changes lazy default evaluation into eager ordinary argument evaluation.

Likely source

The functional and operator preprocessors emit registry helper names, while evalCallExprWithVisitor resolves every lexical Lambda before special and regular builtins. The lexical precedence fix in bd-14o7 is correct for public builtin names, but generated implementation calls need an unshadowable dispatch path or a reserved identifier rule.

Acceptance criteria

- User functions continue to shadow public builtins as covered by function_shadowing.feature.
- Generated syntax helpers cannot be intercepted by local or imported user bindings.
- Cover at least default laziness, arrow lambda construction, one collection operator, and one type operator.
- Either reject reserved declarations clearly or represent generated helper dispatch so it bypasses ordinary lexical name resolution.

title: Prevent recursive YAML aliases from hanging evaluation and reject trailing documents
description: Fresh format audit found two violations in pkg/formats/yaml.go. decodeYAMLNode follows AliasNode targets recursively without tracking active nodes, so a valid recursive alias such as root: &root followed by self: *root never returns; the CLI remained stuck until interrupted. yaml.Unmarshal into one document also accepts a multi-document stream and the reader silently returns only the first document, despite docs/FORMATS.md defining single-document YAML. Acceptance: detect alias cycles and return a typed validation error without hanging or panicking; enforce exactly one YAML document or document and implement an explicit multi-document result; add focused format tests and cucumber regressions for recursive aliases and trailing documents; preserve ordinary non-cyclic aliases and merges.

title: Deduplicate full and post preprocessor pipeline stage construction
description: Problem: internal/preprocessor/stages.go builds the full pipeline and the post-rewriter pipeline with manually duplicated stage lists. CreateFullPreprocessingPipelineWithOptions includes string, operator, selector, functional, and syntax stages after the core rewriter. CreateModularPostProcessingPipelineWithOptions repeats that same suffix. Risk: future stage additions or ordering changes can update one path and forget the other, producing different behavior for PrepareForParsing and direct rewriter Rewrite calls. Suggested direction: extract a postProcessingStages helper used by both pipeline constructors, and add a small test that the full pipeline suffix matches the standalone post pipeline. Acceptance: the post-rewriter stage order is declared once, TraceTransforms output remains unchanged, and existing preprocessor tests stay green.

title: Add size limits for script and file-backed CLI inputs
description: The CLI and runner use os.ReadFile for script files and file-backed inputs without a project-level size limit, while stdin, server request bodies, readUrl, and XLSX decompression already enforce limits. Add bounded readers for script files and input files, choose documented limits, preserve filenames in errors, and add cucumber coverage for oversized file input and script paths.

title: Allow identity coercion to Array and Object
description:
Direct coercion to structural built-in types is internally inconsistent and rejects values that already have the requested type.

Minimized reproductions:
- `[1] as Array` errors `unknown type: Array`; DataWeave returns `[1]`.
- `{a: 1} as Object` errors `unknown type: Object`; DataWeave returns the object.
- In contrast, `[1] as Array | String` and `{a: 1} as Object | String` already succeed in InfoMunge.

Likely source: `matchesTypeExactly` recognizes Array and Object, and union coercion calls it before conversion, but the direct switch in `coerceToTypeWithVisited` handles only String, Number, Boolean, Null, and Namespace before reporting an unknown type. This makes direct and union forms disagree.

Acceptance criteria:
- Identity coercion to Array and Object returns the original value (without losing object order metadata).
