- Direct and union coercion paths agree for already matching built-in types.
- Decide and test the equivalent behavior for other exact-only built-ins recognized by matchesTypeExactly (Function and Regex) rather than leaving another inconsistent branch.
- Add focused evaluator tests and user-visible cucumber coverage.

title: Extract embedded playground HTML from Go string to go:embed file
description:
The entire playground HTML/CSS/JS (558 lines) is embedded as a raw string constant in `internal/cli/webapp.go`. This makes it impossible to:

- Lint or format the HTML/CSS/JS with standard tools
- Test the frontend code independently
- Get syntax highlighting or editor support when editing the UI
- Run security scanners on the client-side JavaScript

Go's `embed` directive (`//go:embed`) would allow the HTML to live in a proper `.html` file while still being compiled into the binary. The standalone WASM playground already uses separate HTML files in `docs/playground/`.

Consider extracting to `internal/cli/playground.html` with `//go:embed playground.html` and keeping the same server behavior.

Files:
- `internal/cli/webapp.go` (558 lines, all one string constant)

title: Align out-of-range integer literals with DataWeave
description: The bounded differential gate generated 9223372036854775808. DataWeave 2.11 evaluated the expression, while InfoMunge failed with invalid integer literal because strconv.Atoi overflowed. Reproduce the minimized boundary case, decide the runtime representation and arithmetic semantics for integer literals beyond the Go int range, add focused evaluator and Cucumber coverage, and restore the bounded differential gate.

title: Honor joinBy and splitBy precedence before concatenation
description:
Combining joinBy or splitBy with a following ++ silently changes which value is used as the separator, producing a wrong result or a misleading type error.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision, compared with DataWeave CLI 2.11.0:
- `["a","b"] joinBy "-" ++ "c"` returns `"a-cb"`; expected `"a-bc"`.
- `"a,b" splitBy "," ++ ["c"]` errors with `cannot concatenate mixed types`; expected `["a","b","c"]`.

The explicitly grouped forms `(["a","b"] joinBy "-") ++ "c"` and `("a,b" splitBy ",") ++ ["c"]` work. Transform traces show the ungrouped forms becoming `joinBy(["a","b"], __concat("-", "c"))` and `splitBy("a,b", __concat(",", ["c"]))`, so the concatenation is incorrectly absorbed into the delimiter argument.

Likely source: the configured splitBy and joinBy right-operand scans stop only at another occurrence of the same operator. Their declared transform order and scanner boundaries do not preserve the DataWeave grouping when additive concatenation follows.

Acceptance criteria:
- joinBy and splitBy complete before a following ++ at the same nesting depth, matching the explicitly grouped forms and DataWeave.
- Concatenation intentionally placed inside a delimiter expression remains possible with parentheses.
- Same-operator chains, regex splitBy operands, strings containing operator text, and nested calls remain unchanged.
- Add exact transform tests and cucumber regressions that assert both the silent joinBy wrong result and the splitBy array composition.

title: Preserve object insertion order for ordinal selectors and object iteration
description:
Object operations currently sort keys alphabetically, changing user-visible ordinal and iteration results from source or input order.

Minimized repros:
- {b:2,a:1}[0] returns 1; DataWeave returns 2.
- {b:2,a:1} pluck (v,k) -> k returns ["a","b"]; DataWeave returns ["b","a"].
- keysOf({b:2,a:1}) returns ["a","b"]; DataWeave returns ["b","a"].
- valuesOf({b:2,a:1}) returns [1,2]; DataWeave returns [2,1].

Root cause: evaluator.Object is a map alias with no insertion-order metadata, and evalObjectOrdinalIndex plus object collection builtins explicitly sort keys for deterministic output.

Impact: ordinal selectors can return the value for the wrong field, and index-aware object lambdas observe different key/index pairs. Determinism should preserve stable input/source order rather than invent alphabetical order.

Expected work:
- Introduce or propagate ordered-object metadata across literals, format readers, merges, selectors, lambdas, and writers.
- Keep structural object equality order-insensitive where appropriate.
- Update tests that currently codify sorted key order and add cucumber regressions for non-alphabetic literal and parsed-input order.

title: Preserve left associativity across mixed rewritten infix operators
description: Adversarial expression review found that different operators sharing a precedence level do not associate left-to-right even though their transform contracts declare left associativity. Repros on current @: [1,2] -- [2] ++ [3] fails to parse at -- instead of returning [1,3]; [1] ++ [2] -- [1] returns [1,2] instead of [2]; "a,b" splitBy "," joinBy "-" errors because joinBy receives a string instead of returning "a-b". The installed DataWeave CLI confirms the expected results for all three expressions. Likely root cause: transforms run one operator at a time, while binaryOperatorConfigs stop only at the same operator or at punctuation; the declared precedence and associativity metadata in stages.go is not used to coordinate mixed operators at the same level. Acceptance: mixed ++/-- and splitBy/joinBy chains preserve left associativity without parentheses; add focused preprocessor tests and cucumber regressions; audit onNull/then and other operators that share a TransformPrecedence value.

title: Unify script header and module directive parsing
description:
Fresh-eyes cohesion/coupling audit finding.

Problem:
Script header parsing and module parsing duplicate directive recognition and declaration application. The two paths have subtly different control flow, offset accounting, context updates, and supported directives, which makes grammar changes expensive and risky.

Evidence:
- `internal/runner/header_directives.go` parses directives into `headerDirective` values and applies them through `applyHeaderDirective`.
- `internal/runner/module_parser.go` independently loops over lines, switches on the same directive prefixes, calls many of the same declaration helpers, and maintains its own offset/line-context handling.
- `internal/runner/declarations.go` has declaration parsing/evaluation helpers shared by both, but orchestration still lives in two places.

Suggested direction:
- Extract a shared declaration/directive parser that can run in script-header mode and module-header mode.
- Model mode-specific policy explicitly, e.g. whether `output`, `input`, namespace declarations, imports, and `---` are allowed.
- Return typed declarations plus source spans, then have separate applicators for script context and module namespace.

Acceptance criteria:
- Adding a new header/module declaration requires changing one parser, not separate script and module loops.
- Module mode still rejects `---` with source context.
- Existing import, var, fun, and type behavior remains covered by focused tests.
- Add cucumber or runner/module tests proving a multiline `var` or `fun` behaves consistently in script headers and modules.

title: Finish pulling preprocessor rewrites into explicit transform stages
description:
Problem:
`PrepareForParsing` still has a bespoke flow before the contract pipeline: comment stripping, regex replacement, implicit object wrapping, top-level object wrapping, the stateful rewriter, recursive second-pass if handling, and only then `CreateModularPostProcessingPipelineWithOptions`. The rewriter itself has a hard-coded handler order in `RewriteWithDepth`.

Why it matters:
Syntax behavior, source-map composition, and transform ordering are spread across `preprocessor.go`, `rewriter_handlers.go`, `stages.go`, and the transform files. New syntax changes have to reason about two transformation systems and multiple mapping composition points.

Evidence:
- `internal/preprocessor/preprocessor.go` composes regex, wrapping, rewriter, and post-pipeline mappings manually.
- `internal/preprocessor/rewriter_handlers.go` contains the core if/while/do/update/object-key rewrite order.
- `internal/preprocessor/stages.go` exposes `TransformContract` ordering only for post-rewriter transforms.

Suggested direction:
Represent the pre-rewriter wrappers and core rewriter as named transform contracts or phase objects with explicit mapping mode and order. Keep the byte-walking rewriter if needed, but make it a stage in the same pipeline contract and trace output.

Acceptance:
- `TraceTransforms` includes every transform that can change source text.
- There is one documented transform order for the full preprocess path.
- Source-map tests cover at least one failure position through regex/wrap/rewriter/post-pipeline composition.

title: Support exact nested negation of the minimum integer literal
description: The bounded differential suite generated -(-(-9223372036854775808)). DataWeave 2.11 returns a numeric result while InfoMunge reports integer overflow during negation. This extends the closed bd-1rbi double-negation case: another surrounding unary minus bypasses the syntactic exactness handling. Acceptance: support nested syntactic unary negation around the minimum literal whenever the exact result is representable by the runtime number model; preserve overflow errors for computed minimum-int negation and genuinely out-of-range operations; add focused evaluator, Cucumber, and differential regression coverage. Reproduction artifact: tmp/intensive-testing/failures/098_differential-infomunge-only-error_2026-07-27T09:54:36.json.

title: Compare both runtimes before skipping differential errors
description: The differential harness returns immediately whenever InfoMunge errors, so it never learns whether the same generated DW-compatible expression succeeds in DataWeave. In the 500-case soak on 2026-07-26, 129 cases were classified only as `infomunge_errors`; any one-sided InfoMunge parser or evaluator failure is therefore invisible rather than a mismatch. The reverse path also skips DataWeave errors without distinguishing shared failures from intentional differences. This weakens the harness precisely for missing or broken combined-feature support. Acceptance: evaluate both runtimes before classifying an outcome; report both-error, InfoMunge-only error, DataWeave-only error, and both-success separately; save reproducible artifacts for one-sided InfoMunge errors; fail or require a narrowly documented allowlist for those cases; retain the structural-comparison coverage threshold and bounded runtime; add unit coverage for the outcome accounting.
notes: Follow-up to closed bd-3pj0: that ticket added warning normalization, outcome counts, and a minimum structural-comparison threshold. This ticket addresses the remaining classification blind spot by evaluating the other runtime after either side errors.

title: Make the default server example and listen address safe for unauthenticated use
description: Problem: the CLI default listen address is `:8080`, which binds on all available interfaces, the API key defaults to empty, and README.md presents `./infomunge --server --listen :8080` before the authenticated variant. The `/run` endpoint accepts and evaluates caller-supplied transformation scripts. Authentication support closed infomunge-tbem, but the current default and primary example still expose an unauthenticated script runner to the local network rather than only to the local machine. Impact: a user following Getting Started can unintentionally make compute and allowed runtime capabilities reachable by other hosts. Acceptance: default to a loopback address or reject/warn on non-loopback unauthenticated binds, make the safe local command the primary README example, clearly document the trust boundary and API-key requirement for network exposure, and add cucumber coverage for default binding plus unsafe configuration behavior.

title: Propagate null through keysOf and valuesOf builtins
description: DataWeave CLI 2.11 returns null for both keysOf(null) and valuesOf(null). InfoMunge currently rejects null in callBuiltinKeysOf and callBuiltinValuesOf. Align these canonical object builtins with DataWeave null propagation, audit the related namesOf and values aliases, and add focused evaluator and Cucumber coverage while preserving non-object validation.

title: Separate evaluator scope from runtime capabilities and output metadata
description:
Problem:
`evaluator.Context` is currently `map[string]Value` and is used for user bindings plus runtime services and adapter metadata. Examples include `__go_ctx__`, `__deadline`, `__format_service__`, `__url_read_service__`, `__output_metadata__`, and `__input_mime__`.

Why it matters:
This couples evaluator, runner, output, CLI/HTTP adapters, and IO services through magic string keys. It makes user namespace collision behavior implicit, makes lambda context copying need to know runtime capabilities, and weakens the library extraction goal in README.md.

Evidence:
- `internal/evaluator/types_value.go` stores Go context and deadline in `Context`.
- `internal/evaluator/io_capabilities.go` stores format and URL services in `Context`.
- `internal/output/output.go` stores XML/output metadata in `Context`.
- `internal/runner/execution.go` merges header/additional bindings and installs capabilities into the same map.

Suggested direction:
Introduce a typed execution scope, for example `Scope{Vars, Capabilities, OutputMetadata}`, or keep `evaluator.Context` only for user/module symbols and pass services/metadata through typed evaluator/run options. Add guardrails for reserved names.

Acceptance:
- User/module bindings are separated from non-user runtime metadata.
- Lambda/function context copying no longer needs a hard-coded hidden-key list.
- Existing CLI, server, WASM, and module declaration behavior stays covered by cucumber or focused Go tests.

title: Harden DataWeave differential runs against zero comparisons and stdout warnings
description: The external DataWeave harness can report a green property run without proving that results were compared. On this installation, when `DW_HOME` is unset, `dw` writes an ANSI setup warning to stdout before valid JSON. `DWEval` then treats the warning plus JSON as an opaque string instead of parsing the structured result. A curated valid expression showed this directly, while the 500-check generated soak still passed because InfoMunge errors and DataWeave errors are silently skipped and the harness does not report or assert a successful-comparison count. Normalize or reject non-result stdout safely, configure a stable `DW_HOME` when appropriate, count generated cases by outcome, and fail when zero or an unexpectedly low number reach `StructuralCompare`. Add a command-level regression with warning-prefixed valid JSON and a test that cannot pass when every generated case is skipped.

title: Keep scratch Go programs under tmp from breaking go test ./...
description:
A plain `go test ./...` from the repo root currently fails because scratch programs in `tmp/` are treated as part of module package `infomunge/tmp`, and multiple files define `main`.

Evidence:
- Command: `go test ./...`
- Failure includes:
  - `tmp/inspect_dkes.go:8:6: main redeclared in this block`
  - `tmp/inspect_dkes2.go:9:6: main redeclared in this block`
  - `tmp/repro_dkes.go:9:6: main redeclared in this block`
  - `tmp/repro_tmjo.go:9:6: main redeclared in this block`
  - `tmp/test_preprocessor.go:8:6: main redeclared in this block`

Why this matters:
- It breaks the standard Go quality gate and makes it harder to trust quick verification commands during development and review.

Possible fixes:
- Move scratch programs outside the module package tree
- Add build tags so ad hoc helpers are excluded from normal test/package discovery
- Standardize on a single helper entrypoint instead of accumulating multiple `package main` files in `tmp/`

Code / repo references:
- `tmp/inspect.go`
- `tmp/inspect_dkes.go`
- `tmp/inspect_dkes2.go`
- `tmp/repro_dkes.go`
- `tmp/repro_tmjo.go`
- `tmp/test_preprocessor.go`

title: Align reduce callback parameter order with DataWeave
description: A live differential comparison found that an uninitialized reduce callback uses accumulator-first semantics in InfoMunge but item-first semantics in DataWeave. Repro: [true, "", null, 0, 31] reduce (i, right) -> right returns 31 in InfoMunge and true in DataWeave. Audit the supported legacy and default-accumulator forms, choose a compatibility policy, update runtime behavior and documentation, and add cucumber coverage. The differential generator should restore reduce coverage once resolved.

title: Let codecs handle empty input and null output instead of bypassing validation
description: pkg/formats/ReadWithOptions returns null before looking up a reader whenever content is empty, and FormatWithOptions returns the literal null before looking up a writer whenever the value is null. These central shortcuts bypass both MIME validation and codec-specific semantics. Confirmed repro: read of empty content as application/csv, application/x-www-form-urlencoded, and application/x-unknown returns [null,null,null]. Output null with application/x-unknown succeeds, and output null with application/csv emits null even though README says non-array CSV results are validation errors. The shortcuts also make the empty handling already implemented by CSV, NDJSON, and URL-encoded readers unreachable. Acceptance: resolve and invoke the selected codec before applying value shortcuts; let each codec define empty and null behavior; reject unsupported MIME types regardless of content or value; add table-driven tests across structured, text, raw, and unknown formats plus cucumber coverage for user-visible cases.

title: Centralize source mapping and diagnostic offset handling
description:
The source-location mapping logic is spread across the preprocessor, runner, and evaluator, with hand-adjusted offsets in multiple places.

Evidence:
- `internal/preprocessor/preprocessor.go:32-64` mutates the mapping after top-level object wrapping with bespoke index rewriting.
- `internal/runner/runner.go:159-181` threads `bodyOffset`, raw source, and preprocessor mappings into evaluation.
- `internal/runner/declarations.go:45-53`, `internal/runner/declarations.go:130-140`, and `internal/runner/runner.go:481-506` compute offsets manually for declaration and header diagnostics.
- `internal/evaluator/evaluator.go:76-185` contains separate parse-error and eval-error remapping paths that depend on those offsets staying aligned.

Why this matters:
- Small syntax rewrites can silently break line/column reporting because mapping assumptions are duplicated.
- Error-reporting fixes become invasive: any change to preprocessing, header normalization, or declaration parsing can affect diagnostics.
- This code is difficult to reason about because the mapping contract is implicit rather than represented as a dedicated type.

Suggested direction:
- Introduce a dedicated source-map type with clear invariants and helpers for composition, slicing, and offset shifting.
- Stop open-coding byte-offset math in runner declaration parsing.
- Add focused tests that assert stable diagnostics across header/body rewrites.

Acceptance criteria:
- Mapping transformations and offset shifts are centralized behind a dedicated API.
- Header/body/declaration callers use shared helpers instead of manual arithmetic.
- Regression tests cover representative rewrites (`if/else`, object wrapping, multiline `var`/`fun`) and verify original source positions.

title: Do not leak Go null formatting into language results
description:
Several successful language expressions stringify null through fmt.Sprintf and expose the Go implementation spelling <nil>, even though InfoMunge central string coercion defines null as "null". The result is inconsistent across equivalent expressions and can create wrong object keys.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision:
- null as String returns "null", but [null] joinBy "," and join([null], ",") return "<nil>".
- {(null): 1} returns {"<nil>":1}.
- [null] groupBy $ returns {"<nil>":[null]}.

Likely source:
- internal/evaluator/visitor.go formats dynamic object keys with fmt.Sprintf("%v", key).
- internal/evaluator/builtins_collection_ops.go does the same for groupBy keys.
- internal/evaluator/builtins_string_text.go and builtins_collection.go format join elements directly with fmt.Sprintf.
- internal/evaluator/types.go already provides coerceToString, which maps nil to the language spelling null and lambdas deterministically.

Acceptance criteria:
- No successful expression exposes <nil> as the implicit spelling of language null.
- Dynamic keys, groupBy keys, join, and joinBy share a deliberate language-level coercion policy, or reject unsupported values with a clear error instead of using Go formatting.
- Preserve documented scalar joining behavior for numbers, booleans, and strings.
- Audit nearby fmt.Sprintf value-to-string conversions for the same abstraction leak and add cucumber regressions for null in each affected operation.

title: Refactor runner header parsing into a parse-first pipeline
description:
The runner header path mixes parsing, preprocessing, evaluation, module loading, context mutation, and source-offset bookkeeping in one flow.

Evidence:
- `internal/runner/runner.go:153-186` evaluates the body immediately after header parsing and threads raw source, body offsets, and preprocessor mappings through the same path.
- `internal/runner/runner.go:325-520` stores mutable parser state (`context`, `namespaces`, `outputMimeType`, `headerOffset`, `fullRaw`, `loader`, `goCtx`) and drives directives through closure-based registrations.
- `internal/runner/declarations.go:20-58`, `internal/runner/declarations.go:68-145`, and `internal/runner/declarations.go:193-217` duplicate the work of parse -> preprocess -> evaluate/compile for variable and function declarations.

Why this matters:
- Adding a new directive currently means reasoning about parsing semantics, evaluation order, and diagnostics at the same time.
- The coupling makes regression scope large whenever header behavior changes.
- Unit-testing directive parsing in isolation is harder than it should be because evaluation is embedded in the parser path.

Suggested direction:
- Introduce an explicit header AST / directive model.
- Parse directives first, then evaluate declarations/imports in a second pass.
- Move line-offset/error-context handling behind a smaller interface so directive handlers are not responsible for source bookkeeping.

Acceptance criteria:
- Header parsing can be tested without invoking evaluator execution for every directive.
- `fun`, `var`, `type`, `import`, `ns`, and `output` handling no longer rely on closure registrations mutating shared parse state directly.
- Existing header diagnostics remain covered by focused tests.

title: Refresh contributor extension guidance for current registries and pipelines
description: Problem: README.md and MIND_MAP.md direct contributors to `docs/EXTENDING.md`, but that guide no longer describes the current code. It tells operator authors to edit nonexistent `internal/preprocessor/pipeline.go`, builtin authors to register only in `internal/evaluator/modular_registry.go`, and format authors to register in `pkg/formats/registry.go`. The current implementation uses transform contracts and ordered stages in `stages.go` and `transform_contract.go`, builtin spec files, and codec-local `init` plus option-handler registration. The old pipeline file was deliberately removed under infomunge-ew7q.14. Impact: contributors are sent to missing or wrong extension points and can omit ordering, source mapping, specs, or format options. Acceptance: update `docs/EXTENDING.md` for the current operator, builtin, and format workflows; name the required registration and test locations; document transform ordering/mapping requirements; and add a lightweight check that every referenced repository path exists.

title: Align scalar selector null propagation with DataWeave
description: The strengthened differential harness in bd-3men found repeated one-sided failures where DataWeave returns null for field or keyed selection on scalar values but InfoMunge errors with cannot index into a scalar type. Repros include payload.name.name when payload.name is an integer, payload.age["age"] when payload.age is an integer, and x.items inside a map when x is numeric. Acceptance: define and implement DataWeave-compatible scalar selection behavior across dot and bracket forms and collection callbacks; add focused evaluator tests and cucumber regressions; remove the linked differential allowlist rule.
close_reason: Aligned numeric string-key selector null propagation with DataWeave across dot, bracket, callback, presence, and assert forms; added unit and Cucumber regressions; documented behavior; and removed the differential allowance.

title: Align groupBy scalar coercion with DataWeave
description: The bounded differential gate found that DataWeave accepts numeric scalar groupBy sources by coercing the scalar to a string, while InfoMunge returns groupBy expects an array. Minimal reproduction: 1.5 groupBy (item) -> typeOf(item). DataWeave 2.11 returns an object with key String and value 1.5. Acceptance: establish DataWeave scalar groupBy semantics across numbers, booleans, strings, and null; align InfoMunge or document deliberate divergence; add focused evaluator and cucumber coverage; update differential accounting if needed.
close_reason: Implemented DataWeave-compatible groupBy semantics for string, numeric, boolean, and null sources; preserved array behavior and object rejection; added evaluator, Cucumber, README, and durable behavior coverage; differential and full quality gates pass.

title: Remove or promote unreferenced root-level repro scripts
description:
Problem: the repository root contains thirteen tracked test_*.im scripts (for dollar parameters, groupBy, mapObject, nested mapObject, sort, and syntax errors). None is referenced by README.md, documentation, Makefile targets, Go tests, or feature files, and they have remained untouched since the initial commit. Their names and contents look like ad-hoc manual reproducers rather than maintained examples or fixtures.

Impact: these files clutter the project entry point, duplicate behavior now covered by automated tests, and leave contributors unsure whether changes must preserve them.

Acceptance: inspect each script, migrate any unique regression into a focused Go or Cucumber test, move any intentional user example under a documented examples directory, delete the remaining scratch files, and keep future ad-hoc reproducers under ignored tmp/ as required by AGENTS.md.

title: Keep builtin arity metadata aligned with runtime handlers
description:
Problem

The modular builtin registry advertises arities that several runtime handlers reject. Any tooling, documentation generator, or extension code using `BuiltinSpec.Arity` receives a false callable contract.

Confirmed mismatches on the current revision:

- `leftPad` and `rightPad` specs advertise two or three arguments, while handlers and cucumber behavior require exactly three.
- `hash` advertises one or two arguments, while its handler requires exactly two.
- `log`, `logDebug`, `logInfo`, `logWarn`, and `logError` advertise one or two arguments, while handlers require exactly one.

Example: `leftPad("x", 3)` is valid according to registry metadata but fails at runtime with `leftPad requires exactly 3 arguments`. `hash("abc")` and `log("prefix", 1)` show the same contract drift.

Acceptance criteria

- Decide the intended public arity for each mismatched builtin and align both metadata and handler behavior. Preserve existing documented cucumber behavior unless an optional argument has a defined default.
- Add a registry contract test that exercises every builtin at its advertised minimum and maximum arity, or otherwise mechanically verifies handler and metadata contracts without triggering side effects.
- Make future arity drift difficult by centralizing validation at dispatch or sharing the declared contract with handler validation.
- Keep error messages positional and function-specific.

title: Reduce legacy parser and error adapter surface
description: The review found several compatibility helpers that appear unused in production paths, including older runner declaration handlers and internal/errors adapter types. Audit these APIs, remove or clearly mark test-only compatibility paths, and consolidate duplicated declaration/property parsing around the shared Declaration IR. Add focused regression coverage where behavior is preserved.

title: Clarify or implement input header directives instead of no-op acceptance
description: Problem: script headers accept input directives and parse them into InputDeclaration, but applyInputDeclaration in internal/runner/runner.go is a no-op. The in-process cucumber scenario named Input directive sets mime type only returns a constant string and does not prove any input mime behavior. DataWeave cookbook docs also show input directives, so the accepted syntax looks meaningful even though payload parsing is actually controlled by CLI, server, or test harness inputs. Risk: users and tests can believe input application/json or named input declarations affect parsing when they currently do not. Suggested direction: either implement defined input directive semantics, including named inputs if supported, or explicitly document and test the directive as compatibility-only no-op syntax. Acceptance: cucumber coverage demonstrates the chosen behavior using payload data, docs match the implementation, and inert input directives no longer have misleading test names.

title: Preserve implicit-lambda index selectors through preprocessing
description:
Implicit lambda values cannot be indexed, so common tuple and regex pipelines fail even though the equivalent named-lambda form works.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision:
- `[[1,2],[3,4]] map $[0]` fails with `expected operand, found ]`; expected `[1,3]`. The named form `[[1,2],[3,4]] map (x) -> x[0]` returns the expected result.
- `zip(1 to 2, 3 to 4) map ($[0] + $[1])` fails with the same parse error; DataWeave CLI 2.11.0 returns `[4,6]`.
- `("abc" scan /./) map $[0]` fails; DataWeave returns `["a","b","c"]`.

A transform trace shows `rewriteCoreSyntax` changing `$[0]` into `$[]interface{}{0,}` before `replaceImplicitLambdas` changes `$` into the generated parameter. The final source contains `__arg[]interface{}{0,}`, which is invalid Go syntax. Named parameters avoid the corruption because the core rewriter recognizes their bracket expression as indexing.

Acceptance criteria:
- `$[index]` and chained selectors on `$` survive preprocessing as selectors inside implicit collection lambdas.
- Behavior matches the equivalent explicit named-lambda expression for map, filter, flatMap, orderBy, and other implicit-lambda operators.
- Preserve array literal rewriting elsewhere, including array literals used inside implicit lambda bodies.
- Add focused transform tests plus cucumber regressions for tuple indexing, zip composition, and scan result indexing.

title: Return null for empty extrema and reduce operations
description:
Supported aggregation operations reject empty arrays where DataWeave returns `null`, so valid composed expressions fail instead of producing the language null value.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision, compared with DataWeave CLI 2.11.0:
- `max([])` errors with `max function requires non-empty array`; expected `null`.
- `min([])` errors with `min function requires non-empty array`; expected `null`.
- `[] maxBy (x) -> x` errors with `cannot find extremum of empty array`; expected `null`.
- `[] minBy (x) -> x` reports the same error; expected `null`.
- `[] reduce (acc, x) -> acc + x` errors because there is no initial value; expected `null`.

Likely source:
- `callBuiltinMax` and `callBuiltinMin` explicitly reject empty array arguments in `builtins_math.go`.
- `findExtremumByLambda` explicitly rejects empty arrays in `builtins_collection_ops.go`.
- `handleReduceEmptyArray` returns an error when no accumulator default exists.
- Existing cucumber scenarios explicitly expect these errors and therefore protect the incompatible behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Empty-array `max`, `min`, `maxBy`, `minBy`, and reduce-without-default resolve successfully to `null`.
- Reduce with an explicit accumulator default continues to return that default.
- Non-empty behavior, numeric precision, and lambda validation remain unchanged.
- Update the contradictory cucumber scenarios and add focused evaluator coverage for each empty operation.

title: Make flatten remove exactly one array nesting level
description:
Problem

InfoMunge flatten recursively removes every nested array boundary, while DataWeave flatten removes exactly one level. This silently changes nested data shape and changes downstream function results.

Minimized reproduction on the current revision, compared with DataWeave CLI 2.11.0:

`sizeOf(flatten([[1, [2, 3]], [4]]))`

Current InfoMunge result: `4` because flatten returns `[1,2,3,4]`.
Expected result: `3` because one-level flatten returns `[1,[2,3],4]`.

Likely source

`callBuiltinFlatten` in `internal/evaluator/builtins_collection.go` uses a recursive `flattenHelper`, so every nested Array is traversed instead of only appending the direct child elements.

Acceptance criteria

- `flatten` removes exactly one array nesting level.
- Deeper nested arrays remain intact after one call and can be flattened by repeated calls.
- Existing null propagation remains unchanged.
- `flatMap` keeps its existing one-level behavior.
- Add focused evaluator coverage and a cucumber regression with a nested array followed by `sizeOf`.

title: Clean up legacy gopherjs playground artifacts
description:
Standalone playground now boots from wasm (`wasm_exec.js` + `infomunge.wasm`), but legacy `docs/playground/infomunge.js` and `docs/playground/infomunge.js.map` still exist and may cause confusion.

Follow-up:
- Decide whether to remove old gopherjs artifacts from the repo.
- If removal is approved, update any docs/scripts that still refer to `infomunge.js`.
- Optionally add a compatibility note in README for teams still using older snapshots.

title: Retire or refresh the stale coverage workflow
description:
Problem: COVERAGE.md and coverage.sh describe an obsolete testing workflow that conflicts with README.md and docs/TESTING.md. COVERAGE.md reports January-era package coverage such as runner 0%, references a nonexistent make coverage target, points to nonexistent test/assertions.go, claims CI uploads coverage despite there being no repository CI configuration, and recommends unbounded go test ./... commands that also run Godog. coverage.sh implements the same stale unbounded command, while a generated root coverage.html from the initial commit remains tracked even though coverage outputs are ignored.

Impact: contributors have multiple contradictory coverage sources, documented commands fail or run the wrong scope, and generated output adds repository noise.

Acceptance: choose README.md/docs/TESTING.md as the authoritative bounded workflow or update one consolidated coverage entry point; remove false metrics, paths, make/CI claims, and stale generated reports; ensure any retained script uses the same Godog separation and timeouts as current guidance; validate every documented command.

title: Align Arrays slice negative-bound semantics with DataWeave
description: The dw::core::Arrays slice wrapper delegates to the generic native slice helper, which interprets negative bounds relative to the end of the array. DataWeave 2.11.0 instead clamps the bounds for this module function. Repros: `slice([1,2,3,4], -2, 4)` returns `[3,4]` in InfoMunge but `[1,2,3,4]` in DataWeave; `slice([1,2,3,4], 1, -1)` returns `[2,3]` in InfoMunge but `[]` in DataWeave. Audit the full start/end boundary table, separate module semantics from any intentionally different generic string or array slice behavior if needed, and add exact Cucumber cases for negative, reversed, and out-of-range bounds.

title: Arrays leftJoin and outerJoin expose null keys for unmatched rows
description:
The embedded dw::core::Arrays join wrappers construct explicit null-valued keys for unmatched rows. DataWeave omits the missing side entirely, so keysOf and presence selectors give the wrong result even though the serialized row can look superficially similar.

Left-side reproduction:
  %dw 2.0
  output application/json
  import * from dw::core::Arrays
  ---
  [keysOf(leftJoin([{id:1}], [], (l)->l.id, (r)->r.owner)[0]),
   leftJoin([{id:1}], [], (l)->l.id, (r)->r.owner)[0].r?]

Actual InfoMunge:
  [["l","r"],true]
Expected / DataWeave 2.11:
  [["l"],false]

Right-side reproduction:
  [keysOf(outerJoin([], [{owner:1}], (l)->l.id, (r)->r.owner)[0]),
   outerJoin([], [{owner:1}], (l)->l.id, (r)->r.owner)[0].l?]

Actual InfoMunge:
  [["l","r"],true]
Expected / DataWeave 2.11:
  [["r"],false]

Likely cause: modules/dw/core/Arrays.im builds {l: l, r: null} and {l: null, r: r}; the compatible result needs conditional object construction that omits the unmatched member. outerJoin inherits the left-side problem from leftJoin and adds the right-side problem itself.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unmatched leftJoin rows contain only l.
- Unmatched outerJoin rows omit whichever side is absent.
- Matched join rows remain unchanged and preserve ordering.
- Cover keysOf and presence, not only JSON text.
close_reason: Omit unmatched join members and cover JSON shape, keysOf, presence, matches, and ordering

title: Rewrite every valid range index instead of only one literal non-negative span
description:
The range-index preprocessor handles only one narrow occurrence and leaves other valid range selectors to be parsed as an array-valued index.

Confirmed repros:
- ["hello"[0 to 0], "world"[1 to 2]] fails with string index must be an integer, got array, although each selector works alone.
- [1,2,3][-2 to -1] fails instead of returning [2,3] as DataWeave does.
- A range with a computed end is left unrewritten because replaceArrayRangeIndexing requires strconv.Atoi on the end expression.

Root cause: internal/preprocessor/transformers_syntax.go replaceArrayRangeIndexing scans only the last closing bracket, runs once in the String Processing stage, rejects a leading minus sign, and requires the end bound to be an integer literal before emitting slice(..., end+1).

Acceptance criteria:
- Rewrite all independent range selectors in one expression.
- Support negative bounds and expression bounds with correct inclusive-end semantics.
- Respect strings and nested bracket structure.
- Add preprocessor unit tests plus cucumber regressions for multiple, negative, and computed ranges.
close_reason: Implemented complete range-index rewriting with negative, computed, multiple, nested, chained, descending, and Unicode-safe coverage

title: Fix exact-number cucumber assertions to reject fractional outputs
description:
Problem:
theOutputShouldBeValidJSONWithNumber in test/godog_test.go:1001 parses JSON numbers as float64, then compares int(v) to the expected integer at line 1014. That means an output like 42.9 would satisfy an assertion expecting 42.

Risk:
Feature scenarios using "Then the output should be valid JSON with number: N" can miss numeric regressions involving fractions, rounding, or accidental decimal output.

Required changes:
- Compare the parsed JSON number exactly against the expected integer value without truncation.
- Consider allowing the step regex to express negative integers if exact negative checks are useful.
- Add unit coverage for the step helper showing 42.0 passes for 42 and 42.9 fails for 42.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fractional JSON numbers no longer pass integer exact-number assertions.
- Existing features using the step continue to pass.
- There is direct test coverage for the assertion helper behavior.

title: Clarify br sync and compact agent memory docs
description: Fresh-eyes audit found agent workflow docs that can mislead future agents. br sync --help says br sync never executes git commands and exposes explicit modes such as --flush-only, but AGENTS.md:14 says br sync syncs with git and AGENTS.md:26 and :38 just say br sync. MIND_MAP.md:31 and :41 mirror that wording, and GEMINI.md has the same stale quick reference. This repo also says to use jj only, so the workflow should say that br exports beads state and jj commits the resulting files. MIND_MAP.md:3 asks agents to keep 20-50 nodes, but the file currently has 67 nodes and multiple repeated entries for the same rg, br, and jj mistakes. Acceptance: update AGENTS.md, GEMINI.md, and MIND_MAP.md so br sync guidance is explicit and compatible with jj, remove any implication that br itself syncs with git, and compact repeated MIND_MAP pitfalls while preserving the important user preferences and high-signal prevention notes.

title: Redundant error wrapping in app.go duplicates error message
Make range(end) reject lossy numeric bounds
description: While completing bd-175s, the numeric conversion audit found that callBuiltinRange in internal/evaluator/builtins_collection_object_ops.go still converts float64 bounds directly to int64 and emits every index as float64. A bound at 9223372036854775808.0 can wrap or be misclassified, and integer results above 2^53 lose precision. Acceptance criteria: validate finite and runtime-supported bounds before allocation; preserve integer range elements as exact runtime ints; return a clear range or precision error instead of wrapping or rounding; add focused evaluator and cucumber coverage at 2^53 and int64 boundaries.

title: Align sizeOf boolean coercion with DataWeave
description: The bounded differential gate minimized an InfoMunge-only failure to sizeOf(false). DataWeave 2.11 returns 5 after coercing false to its string representation, while InfoMunge reports sizeOf: unsupported type bool. Acceptance: establish sizeOf semantics for both boolean values, align runtime behavior or document a deliberate divergence, add focused evaluator and Cucumber coverage, and verify the differential gate no longer reports this signature.
close_reason: Implemented DataWeave-compatible boolean sizeOf rendering with evaluator, Cucumber, and deterministic differential coverage.

title: Fix remaining broken README command examples and DataWeave wording
description: Problem: README.md still contains two commands that do not work as written. Line 43 uses `dw run -i payload <payload.json>`, but the installed DataWeave CLI reports `-i=<Name=File>` and the shell treats angle brackets as redirection. Line 69 puts `\\n` inside a single-quoted JSON body, so JSON decoding yields literal backslash-n text; the current runner then reports that the script has no `---` header separator. The introduction and comparison section also use stale, subjective open-source wording and inconsistent DataWeave, MuleSoft, and InfoMunge capitalization. Evidence: `dw run --help` confirms the Name=File contract, and executing the escaped script against the current CLI reproduces the ParseError. Acceptance: use valid DataWeave input assignment syntax, encode actual JSON newlines with `\n`, verify both examples end to end, replace time-sensitive claims with concise sourced wording, and add cucumber coverage that catches command-example regressions.

title: User-defined functions ignore captured lexical scope and can be caller-shadowed
description:
Problem

User-defined functions do not use their definition environment at call time. `buildFunLambda` stores `Env`, but `callUserDefinedFunctionWithVisitor` ignores it and instead copies the caller context. That makes imported functions / closures dynamically scoped and lets caller variables shadow module-local values.

Reproduction

1. Create `tmp/modules/Shadow.im`:
   `%im 0.1`
   `var offset = 5`
   `fun addOffset(x) = x + offset`
2. Create `tmp/shadow-scope.im`:
   `%im 0.1`
   `import modules::Shadow`
   `var offset = 100`
   `output application/json`
   `---`
   `Shadow::addOffset(10)`
3. Run `./tmp/infomunge -f tmp/shadow-scope.im`
4. Observe current output: `110`

Expected

The imported function should evaluate against the module scope it was defined in, so the result should stay `15` even when the caller defines its own `offset`.

Why this matters

This is a real semantic bug, not just an implementation detail. Any imported function or closure that refers to surrounding variables can silently change behavior based on the caller's locals. That makes module APIs brittle and will break future closure-heavy features.

Code references

- `internal/runner/declarations.go:235-240` stores `Env` on `Lambda`
- `internal/evaluator/visitor.go:270-296` ignores `lambda.Env` and copies the caller `context` instead

Acceptance criteria

- Call user-defined functions from their captured lexical environment, then bind parameters on top of that environment.
- Decide explicitly how much of the caller context should remain visible, if any, and document that rule.
- Add coverage for module-variable shadowing and for lambda/function closure capture.

title: Preserve additive left operands for lower-precedence configured operators
description:
Configured infix operators do not preserve a higher-precedence ++ or -- expression on their left. This produces both parse failures and silent wrong values.

Reproductions:
- ["a"] ++ ["b"] joinBy "-"
  - DataWeave: "a-b"
  - InfoMunge: expected EOF, found ++
- [1] ++ [2] contains 2
  - DataWeave: true
  - InfoMunge: expected EOF, found ++
- "a" ++ "b" matches /ab/
  - DataWeave: true
  - InfoMunge: "afalse"
- "a,b" splitBy "," ++ ["c"] joinBy "-"
  - DataWeave: "a-b-c"
  - InfoMunge: expected EOF, found ++
- 1 to 3 -- [2] joinBy "-"
  - DataWeave: "1-3"
  - InfoMunge: expected EOF, found --

A preprocessing trace for the split/concat/join chain ends at splitBy("a,b", ",") ++joinBy(["c"], "-"). The configured joinBy transform runs before the additive transform and its left-operand scan stops at the plus signs instead of retaining the complete higher-precedence concatenation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Preserve complete ++ and -- left operands for configured lower-precedence operators including find, contains, splitBy, joinBy, match, matches, and scan where semantically applicable.
- Maintain existing left associativity within same-precedence operator groups.
- Add focused transform tests and end-to-end Cucumber cases, including a silent-wrong-result assertion for concatenation followed by matches.

title: Align README issue-tracker guidance with beads_rust
description: Problem: README.md ends by saying the project uses Beads and links to `steveyegge/beads`, while AGENTS.md and MIND_MAP.md correctly require `br` from beads_rust, `br sync --flush-only`, and `jj`. A new contributor following README can select the wrong implementation and inherit incompatible sync or VCS assumptions. The `bv --robot-triage` JSON also still emits legacy `bd` commands, so the authoritative docs need to be especially explicit. Acceptance: link README.md to the actual beads_rust project used here, name the `br` executable, point contributors to AGENTS.md for the jj-safe workflow, and document that any legacy `bd` command suggestions from `bv` output must be translated rather than copied.

title: Prevent duplicated agent instructions from drifting
description:
Problem: AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md duplicate the same 55-line workflow almost verbatim, so every policy correction requires synchronized edits. They have already drifted: AGENTS.md says not to install software and to ask when a new ability may be needed, while GEMINI.md flatly says not to install software. MIND_MAP.md agrees with the approval-based wording. The earlier bd-dhcc had to update all three documents manually for the same reason.

Impact: different agents can follow different repository rules depending on which entry file they load, and repeated workflow prose increases maintenance and review cost.

Acceptance: make one file the authoritative shared instruction source where supported, or add a lightweight validation/generation mechanism for the intentionally duplicated sections; align the current software-installation wording; preserve tool-specific entry filenames and any deliberately different guidance; document how future policy edits stay synchronized.

title: Track sourcemap coverage for early preprocessor transforms
description: replaceRegexLiterals and wrapImplicitObjectLiteralBodies still run before the main mapped rewriter, so future diagnostic regressions in those transforms should move onto the shared sourcemap pipeline too.

title: Compose infix to ranges with downstream operators
description:
An unparenthesized infix to expression does not act as the source for downstream collection and concatenation operators. Instead the following operation is applied to the upper bound, producing errors for valid DataWeave-style pipelines.

Minimized reproductions on the current revision, compared with DataWeave CLI 2.11.0:
- `1 to 3 map $ * 2` errors with `map expects an array, got int`; expected `[2,4,6]`.
- `1 to 4 reduce ($$ + $)` errors with `reduce expects an array, got int`; expected `10`.
- `1 to 3 joinBy "-"` errors because joinBy receives integer `3`; expected `"1-2-3"`.
- `1 to 2 ++ [3]` errors with `cannot concatenate mixed types`; expected `[1,2,3]`.

Adding parentheses around the range makes every case work. The operator pipeline rewrites to before functional operators, and the to right-operand scanner does not stop at these downstream operators. For example the map form is grouped like `to(1, map(3, ...))` instead of `map(to(1, 3), ...)`.

Acceptance criteria:
- A completed infix range can feed map, filter, reduce, joinBy, concatenation, and other supported downstream operators with DataWeave-compatible grouping.
- Explicit parentheses can still override normal grouping.
- Negative and fractional bounds, chained to operators, range selectors, and existing to associativity remain correct.
- Add transform-contract and cucumber regressions across at least one collection lambda, one string conversion, and one concatenation case.

title: Distinguish literal question and bang keys from selector suffixes
description: Quoted bracket keys ending in ? or ! are interpreted as presence or assert selectors because dot notation encodes selector mode by appending the suffix to the string index. DataWeave treats [{"score?": 7}]["score?"] and [{"score!": 8}]["score!"] as literal key selection, while InfoMunge returns presence semantics or attempts assertion. Replace the ambiguous string-suffix encoding with explicit internal selector operations, preserve dot .field? and .field! behavior for objects and arrays, and add preprocessor, evaluator, and cucumber regressions for literal punctuation keys.

title: Make Arrays divideBy handle fractional and non-positive chunk sizes
description: The dw::core::Arrays divideBy wrapper composes take and drop using a raw Number size, but those native helpers truncate to int and the wrapper special-cases size <= 0 as an empty result. Differential repros against DataWeave 2.11.0: `divideBy([1,2,3], 0)` and size `-1` return `[]` instead of `[[1],[2],[3]]`; size `1.5` returns `[[1],[2],[3]]` instead of `[[1,2],[3]]`; size `2.9` returns `[[1,2],[3]]` instead of `[[1,2,3]]`. More seriously, size `0.5` repeatedly takes and drops zero elements until InfoMunge reports the evaluation depth limit, while DataWeave returns singleton chunks. Implement the DataWeave chunk-size normalization semantics without recursive non-progress, and add Cucumber coverage for zero, negative, sub-one fractional, and larger fractional sizes.

title: Use exact numeric semantics instead of truncating, overflowing, or losing integer precision
description:
Adversarial expression audit found three classes of silent wrong numeric results on the current revision.

Minimized repros:
- 5 / 2 returns 2; DataWeave returns 2.5.
- 9223372036854775807 + 1 returns -9223372036854775808; DataWeave returns 9223372036854775808.
- 9007199254740993 == 9007199254740992.0 returns true and the corresponding greater-than comparison returns false; DataWeave returns false and true.
- 9007199254740993 + 0.0 returns 9.007199254740992e+15, losing one; DataWeave preserves 9007199254740993.

Likely root cause:
- internal/evaluator/evaluator.go quo uses the integer branch of numericOp when both inputs are ints, so division truncates.
- add, sub, and mul use native int arithmetic without overflow checks.
- numericCompare, numericEquals, and mixed numericOp paths convert ints to float64 through BothFloats, losing precision above 2^53.
- pkg/values/literals.go represents numeric literals as native int or float64, which cannot model DataWeave exact-number behavior across these cases.

Impact: valid transformations can successfully emit plausible but mathematically incorrect values, including sign flips and false equality.

Acceptance criteria:
- Integer division preserves fractional results.
- Integer arithmetic cannot silently wrap; use exact arithmetic or return an explicit overflow error if exact support is intentionally bounded.
- Mixed integer/decimal arithmetic and comparisons do not silently collapse distinct integers above 2^53.
- Add focused evaluator tests and cucumber regressions for all minimized repros.

title: Align filter selector no-match and source-type semantics with DataWeave
description: DataWeave differential repro: sizeOf(([1][?($ > 9)] default [7])) evaluates to 1 because a filter selector with no matches returns null and default runs. InfoMunge returns 0 because it returns an empty array. The object form sizeOf(({a:1}[?($ > 9)] default {fallback:0})) likewise returns 0 instead of 1. Unsupported sources also silently return null in InfoMunge, while DataWeave rejects examples such as "abc"[?($ == "b")], 123[?($ == "2")], and null[?($ == 1)]. Update callBuiltinFilterSelector to preserve successful matches, return null when array or object matches are empty, and report a typed error for unsupported sources. Add focused evaluator tests and Cucumber coverage showing interaction with default for both arrays and objects plus scalar rejection.

title: Expand builtin arg-validation helper into declarative wrappers
description: This ticket introduced shared requireExactArgs/requireMinArgs helpers and migrated math/runtime/string builtins. Remaining builtins still repeat argument count and type assertion boilerplate. Follow up by adding declarative wrapper helpers for common signatures (no args, unary string, unary number, binary string/string, etc.) and migrate additional builtin families incrementally while preserving existing error messages and cucumber coverage.

title: Either support percent modulo expressions or remove them from the InfoMunge generator contract
description:
The repository expression generator treats percent as supported InfoMunge arithmetic syntax, but the runtime rejects it.

Minimized repro: 5 % 2 fails with unsupported operation instead of producing 1.

Evidence:
- internal/testing/exprgen/operators.go includes percent in FeatureArithmetic and documents the generated expressions as syntactically valid InfoMunge expressions.
- internal/evaluator/evaluator.go evalBinaryOp has no token.REM case.
- No preprocessor transform rewrites percent to mod.
- Closed issue infomunge-2zwr states that InfoMunge uses percent and that the preprocessor rewrites it internally, which is no longer true on the current revision.
- The supported DataWeave-compatible spelling 5 mod 2 still works.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decide and document whether percent is supported InfoMunge syntax.
- If supported, implement token.REM or a correct precedence-aware rewrite and add cucumber coverage.
- If unsupported, remove it from FeatureArithmetic and update stale issue/documentation assumptions so intensive tests do not generate expressions outside the language contract.

title: Fix XML pretty-print indentation for inline elements in playground
description: Pretty print in both playground UIs mis-indents XML when an element opens and closes on the same line (e.g. 1 siblings). Update the JavaScript pretty printer used by server and standalone playground pages so inline close elements do not increase indentation.

title: Preserve left associativity when mod follows multiplicative operators
description:
Adversarial expression review found a silent precedence error in the DataWeave-compatible `mod` operator.

Minimized reproduction:
- Script body: `8 / 4 mod 3`
- Current InfoMunge result: `8`
- Expected mathematical and DataWeave result: `2`
- `8 * 4 mod 3` similarly returns `8` instead of `2`.

Likely root cause:
`replaceConfiguredBinaryOperatorWithMapping` scans only the immediate left operand because the default stop bytes include `*` and `/`. The transform therefore rewrites `8 / 4 mod 3` as `8 / mod(4, 3)`, even though `mod`, multiplication, and division share multiplicative precedence and must associate left-to-right. The transform contract declares multiplicative precedence and left associativity, but that metadata is not enforced by the scanner.

Acceptance criteria:
- Mixed `*`, `/`, `%`, and `mod` chains preserve documented multiplicative precedence and left associativity.
- `8 / 4 mod 3` and `8 * 4 mod 3` both return `2`.
- Parentheses continue to override associativity.
- Add focused preprocessor tests plus cucumber coverage for mixed multiplicative chains.

title: Bind object filter selector double-dollar to the object key
description: DataWeave differential repro: {a:1,b:2,c:3}[?((($$ as String) == "b"))] returns {b:2}. InfoMunge returns {} because callBuiltinFilterSelector binds the second object callback parameter to the ordinal index instead of the object key. Array filter selectors must keep binding the second parameter to the numeric index. Bind object filter selector callbacks as value and key, preserve observable key order, and add Cucumber coverage that combines $$ key selection with pluck or valuesOf so the wrong binding cannot hide behind a simple predicate.

title: Use structural typed keys for unique distinct and distinctBy
description:
The collection uniqueness builtins derive identity from `fmt.Sprintf`, which collapses distinct language values and silently drops data.

Minimized reproductions:
- `[1, "1"] distinctBy $` returns `[1]`; DataWeave returns `[1,"1"]`.
- `[true, "true", null, "<nil>"] distinctBy $` returns `[true,null]`; all four values are distinct.
- `unique([{a: 1}, {a: "1"}])` returns only the first object.
- `distinct([[1], ["1"]])` returns only the first array.

Likely root cause:
`callBuiltinDistinctBy` uses `fmt.Sprintf("%v", key)` while `unique` and `distinct` prefix only the top-level Go type. Nested element types are therefore erased, and nil uses the Go-specific `<nil>` rendering.

Acceptance criteria:
- Uniqueness uses structural, type-aware language equality rather than display strings.
- Distinct scalar types with the same rendering remain distinct.
- Nested arrays and objects retain values that differ only by nested type.
- Equal nested structures are still deduplicated and first-occurrence order is preserved.
- Reuse the central equality semantics where practical and add cucumber regressions for the minimized examples.

title: Decouple evaluator value model from format and IO packages
description:
Fresh-eyes cohesion/coupling audit finding.

Problem:
Evaluator value types and format-layer types are coupled in both directions of responsibility. The evaluator imports `pkg/formats` for `Namespace` and `XMLMultiValue`, while IO builtins call `formats.Read/Format` directly. This blurs the boundary between language semantics and serialization adapters and works against the README goal that domain logic can be extracted as a library.

Evidence:
- `internal/evaluator/types_value.go` aliases `XMLMultiValue = formats.XMLMultiValue` and treats `formats.Namespace` as an evaluator kind.
- `internal/evaluator/types.go` checks/coerces `formats.Namespace`.
- `internal/evaluator/builtins_io.go` directly owns `read`, `write`, and `readUrl` behavior using `pkg/formats`, HTTP, DNS validation, and response limits.
- `pkg/formats` defines its own `Object`/`Array` aliases that mirror evaluator values, which hides rather than removes the shared value-model dependency.

Suggested direction:
- Define a core value model in a package that is intentionally shared by evaluator and formats, or move namespace/multivalue concepts out of `pkg/formats` if they are language-level values.
- Keep serialization and network IO behind interfaces injected into evaluator builtins or registered as optional capabilities.
- Separate pure evaluation from environmental IO so embedders can use the evaluator without pulling in all format/network behavior.

Acceptance criteria:
- Evaluator no longer needs to import XML/serialization implementation packages for core value kinds.
- `read`/`write` builtins use an explicit format service boundary.
- `readUrl` is isolated as an IO capability with tests for disabled/unavailable environments.
- Existing format and IO cucumber coverage remains behavior-compatible.

title: Support negative object ordinal selectors
description:
Object ordinal indexing rejects negative positions even though array and string indexing resolve them from the end and DataWeave does the same for objects.

Minimized reproduction:
- `{a: 1, b: 2}[-1]`
- InfoMunge: `object index out of bounds: -1 (object has 2 keys)`
- DataWeave CLI 2.11.0: `2`

Likely source: `evalObjectOrdinalIndex` checks `i < 0` immediately, whereas `evalArrayIndex` and `evalStringIndex` first add the collection length for negative indexes. Object insertion order is already tracked through values.ObjectKeys, so the missing normalization is localized.

Acceptance criteria:
- Negative object ordinals count backward through the observable insertion order: `-1` is the last value and `-len` is the first.
- Values below `-len` and values at or above `len` retain a clear bounds error.
- Cover literal objects, parsed JSON objects, and XML child objects to ensure ordering metadata is respected.
- Add cucumber coverage for user-visible selector behavior and focused evaluator boundary tests.

title: Align mixed string and number plus semantics with DataWeave
description: A live differential comparison found divergent plus behavior for mixed number and string operands. Repro: 0.08003611321817175 + "1" returns the string "0.080036113218171751" in InfoMunge and the number 1.0800361132181717 in DataWeave. Audit mixed-type plus and coercion semantics, document the intended policy, add cucumber coverage, and restore plus to the differential-compatible operator set once resolved.

title: Duplicated XML output helpers in runner.go and handlers/run.go
description:
Both `internal/runner/runner.go` and `internal/handlers/run.go` contain near-identical implementations of:

1. `extractNamespaceVars` / `ExtractNamespaceVars` — iterate context map looking for `formats.Namespace` values
2. `applyXMLOutputOptions` / `ApplyXMLOutputOptions` — apply raw string options to `XMLOutputOptions`

The handlers version exports these functions (uppercase), while the runner version keeps them unexported. The runner's `formatOutputWithContext` and the handlers' `FormatRunResult` both format XML output using the same pattern: extract namespaces, apply options, call `formats.FormatXMLWithOptions`.

This shared XML output formatting logic should live in one place. The handlers package already exports the helpers — the runner should call them instead of maintaining duplicates.

Files:
- `internal/runner/runner.go:478-516` (unexported versions)
- `internal/handlers/run.go:140-179` (exported versions)

title: Duplicated stripLineComments implementations in preprocessor and declarations
description:
Both `internal/preprocessor/preprocessor.go` and `internal/runner/declarations.go` define their own `stripLineComments` and `stripSingleLineComment` functions. The preprocessor version uses `ScanState` for string tracking, while the declarations version uses manual `inString`/`stringChar`/`escaped` booleans.

These are independently maintained implementations of the same logic that could diverge silently. The preprocessor version also calls `isRegexContext`/`parseRegexLiteral`, while the declarations version calls the exported `preprocessor.IsRegexContext`/`preprocessor.ParseRegexLiteral`.

Consolidate into a single shared implementation — likely in `internal/stringutils` or within the preprocessor package with an exported function.

Files:
- `internal/preprocessor/preprocessor.go:314-346`
- `internal/runner/declarations.go:436-485`

title: Remove evaluator dependency on preprocessor for nested expressions
description:
Problem:
The main architecture is runner preprocesses source, then evaluator executes the parsed expression. That layering is inverted inside evaluator builtins: `builtins_arrays_do.go` and `builtins_update.go` import `internal/preprocessor`, preprocess quoted expression strings at runtime, parse them with `go/parser`, and then evaluate the resulting AST.

Why it matters:
Evaluator behavior now depends directly on source rewrite rules and preprocessor options. Nested expression semantics can drift from top-level semantics, source-map handling becomes harder, and the evaluator cannot be treated as a clean AST/runtime layer.

Evidence:
- `internal/evaluator/builtins_arrays_do.go` calls `preprocessor.PrepareForParsing` for do-block expressions and declarations.
- `internal/evaluator/builtins_update.go` calls `preprocessor.PrepareForParsing` for update case expressions.
- `internal/preprocessor/rewriter_handlers.go` emits `__do` and `__updateExpr` calls with quoted source fragments that the evaluator later reparses.

Suggested direction:
Move nested expression compilation behind a typed boundary. Options include compiling do/update bodies during preprocessing into AST-compatible calls, introducing an evaluator-injected `ExpressionCompiler` interface owned by runner, or creating a shared parser/compiler package that both runner and nested-expression features use without evaluator importing preprocessor directly.

Acceptance:
- `internal/evaluator` no longer imports `internal/preprocessor`.
- Top-level, do-block, and update-expression preprocessing use the same option and source-map policy.
- Existing do/update cucumber and unit coverage still passes, with at least one nested syntax regression test added.

title: Remove over-extracted trivial constants from constants.go
description:
`internal/evaluator/constants.go` extracts trivially obvious numeric literals into named constants that add indirection without aiding readability:

- `ParityDivisor = 2` (used for `n % 2`)
- `DecimalBase = 10` (used in `strconv.FormatInt(..., 10)`)
- `FloatBitSize = 64` (used in `strconv.ParseFloat(..., 64)`)
- `BoolTrueAsInt = 1`, `BoolFalseAsInt = 0`
- `SpaceCharacter = ' '`
- `FirstMonthOfYear = 1`, `FirstDayOfMonth = 1`
- `SundayWeekday = 0`, `DaysInWeek = 7`

These are universally understood values. Wrapping them in constants forces readers to navigate to the definition just to confirm the obvious. The useful constants in the file (`MaxEvalDepth`, `MaxDeepDepth`, `DefaultLoopTimeout`, `TimeoutCheckInterval`) should stay.

Inline the trivial ones and keep only the non-obvious constants.

Files:
- `internal/evaluator/constants.go:53-85`

title: Apply overlapping update cases with DataWeave conflict semantics
description: Problem: `applyUpdateCases` mutates `result` after every case and feeds that intermediate value into the next case. Overlapping selectors therefore compound changes and silently disagree with DataWeave. Reproduction: `{a: {b: 1}} update { case whole at .a -> {b: whole.b + 1} case leaf at .a.b -> leaf * 10 }` returns `{"a":{"b":20}}` in InfoMunge but `{"a":{"b":2}}` in DataWeave 2.11. Reversing the two cases returns 11 in InfoMunge but still 2 in DataWeave. Repeating `.a` with `+ 1` then `* 10` returns 20 in InfoMunge while DataWeave returns 2. Disjoint selectors correctly apply both cases. Acceptance: evaluate and merge update cases with DataWeave conflict semantics rather than sequential intermediate mutation; cover ancestor then descendant, descendant then ancestor, repeated identical selectors, disjoint selectors, and overlapping array or object paths; retain object insertion order and deep-copy isolation.

title: Align CSV header-order documentation with insertion-order behavior
description: docs/FORMATS.md says CSV output uses the sorted union of object keys. formatCSV instead walks each row in array order and each tracked object through values.ObjectKeys, so ordered objects preserve first-seen insertion order. The existing writer test explicitly expects an object inserted as b then a to emit header b,a. Either the implementation or the fidelity matrix is wrong, and callers cannot know whether output is stable lexical order or stable source order. Acceptance: choose and document the intended CSV header-order contract, align implementation and tests with it, cover heterogeneous rows with overlapping fields, and keep the format documentation consistency checks green.

title: Give preprocessor transforms explicit contracts and ordering
description:
Fresh-eyes cohesion/coupling audit finding.

Problem:
The preprocessor combines a byte-level recursive rewriter with a large fixpoint post-processing pipeline of independent string transformers. Ordering, precedence, mapping accuracy, and termination behavior are encoded implicitly in `stages.go` plus many `replace*` functions, so adding syntax requires understanding the whole pipeline.

Evidence:
- `internal/preprocessor/preprocessor.go` does comment stripping, regex replacement, object wrapping, recursive rewrite, then `CreateModularPostProcessingPipeline`.
- `internal/preprocessor/stages.go` contains long ordered transform lists, including loops over operator and functional transforms with independent iteration guards.
- Many transforms use inferred mappings via `inferStageMapping`; only some provide exact mappings.
- Prior mistakes in `MIND_MAP.md` repeatedly mention preprocessor regressions from scanner ordering, broad patches, multiline parsing assumptions, and mapping/transform fragility.

Suggested direction:
- Define a transform contract with explicit metadata: name, phase, precedence/associativity where relevant, exact mapping support, and idempotence/loop expectations.
- Split lexical scanning/tokenization concerns from syntactic rewrites where possible.
- Prefer table-driven binary/operator transforms for common cases instead of bespoke `replace*` functions.
- Add a preprocessor debug trace option to show phase-by-phase output for failing syntax cases.

Acceptance criteria:
- There is a documented transform lifecycle and ordering rule in code or docs.
- New operator additions can use a shared path for precedence/scanning/mapping instead of custom pipeline surgery.
- At least one existing operator family is migrated to the new contract as a proving slice.
- Cucumber or unit tests verify source-map error locations for a migrated transform.

title: Retire stale completed design and audit documents
description: Problem: docs contains several historical plans and audits presented as current guidance after their work completed. docs/WHILE_LOOPS.md says loops will be added and describes completed checklist items as an implementation plan. docs/chaining_audit.md still announces confirmed operator-chaining bugs and obsolete line-specific root causes even though its example expressions now run successfully and CollectionOperators is centralized. docs/VACUOUS_CUCUMBER_AUDIT_2026-02-13.md points to five follow-up tickets that are all closed. CODE_REVIEW_2026-05-02.md similarly describes fixed defects and removed file shapes, while three overlapping intensive_expression_testing_proposal variants preserve superseded recommendations even though the test system exists. Impact: contributors cannot tell normative documentation from historical evidence, searches surface false current defects, and duplicated proposals add maintenance and review noise. Acceptance: choose which completed reports still provide durable value; delete redundant drafts, archive retained historical reports under an explicitly historical location or banner with completion status and issue links, rewrite WHILE_LOOPS as current behavior only if it remains user-facing, and ensure README plus docs indexes link only to authoritative current guidance. Keep any unique rationale compact rather than retaining line-number snapshots of obsolete code.

title: Consolidate duplicate cucumber test scenarios across feature files
description:
Multiple cucumber feature files contain identical test scenarios with the same names and assertions. Examples include:

- "sum basic usage" in aggregation_functions.feature and math_functions.feature
- "mod basic usage" in math_functions.feature and utility_functions.feature
- "avg basic usage" and "avg with floats" duplicated across files
- "filter Object basic usage" and "filterObject on non-object fails" duplicated
- "log requires exactly one argument", "logWith" scenarios duplicated
- "envVar" scenarios duplicated

There are approximately 30+ duplicated scenario names. Each duplicate runs the same assertion twice, inflating test counts without adding coverage and creating a maintenance burden where changes must be made in multiple places.

Fix: consolidate each scenario to a single canonical location. Choose the most appropriate feature file for each and remove duplicates from the others.

title: Prevent Unicode corruption in capitalize and camelize
description: Text transformation builtins split UTF-8 strings at byte offsets and emit replacement characters for non-ASCII leading characters. Repros on current @: capitalize("éclair") returns "��clair" instead of "Éclair"; capitalize("🙂 smile") returns four replacement characters before " Smile"; camelize("éclair_test") returns replacement characters before "clairTest". Root cause: splitCamelCase mixes byte offsets from range with direct byte lookup, capitalize slices word[:1], lowercaseFirst slices s[:1], and camelize uppercases part[:1]. Related dasherize and underscore boundary checks also index neighboring bytes and should be audited. Acceptance: these transforms never create invalid UTF-8; character case and word boundaries operate on runes; add accented-letter, emoji, and mixed camel-case cucumber regressions.

title: Remove empty builtins.go redirect file
Input readers need size limits for stdin, multipart parts, and XLSX ZIP entries
description:
Problem

Several ingestion paths read unbounded data into memory with `io.ReadAll` and do not enforce size or entry-count limits. The obvious cases are CLI stdin, multipart parts, and XLSX ZIP entries.

Examples in code

- `internal/io/input.go:42` reads all stdin into memory
- `pkg/formats/multipart.go:47` reads every multipart part body into memory
- `pkg/formats/xlsx_workbook.go:69-83` reads every ZIP entry into memory with no decompressed-size guard

Why this matters

A large input or crafted archive can drive excessive allocations or OOM the process. XLSX is especially risky because a small compressed file can expand dramatically when decompressed. The server already enforces a 1 MiB request-body cap, but these lower-level readers still have no independent safety rails and can be reached from the CLI and builtins.

Expected

Parsing paths should fail fast with validation errors once they exceed explicit limits (total bytes, per-part bytes, ZIP entry count / decompressed bytes, etc.) rather than consuming unbounded memory.

Acceptance criteria

- Define explicit size limits for stdin-backed inputs and format readers that currently slurp data wholesale.
- Add decompressed-size / entry-count protections for XLSX parsing.
- Add regression tests that assert oversized inputs fail cleanly instead of being fully materialized.

title: CLI -f resolves imported modules relative to cwd instead of the script file
description:
`internal/cli/app.go` reads the script file and then calls `runner.RunFromStringWithContextAndOptions(...)` without setting `RunnerOptions.BaseDir`, so module resolution falls back to `os.Getwd()` instead of the script file's directory.

Evidence:
- Repro fixture under `tmp/review_import/` with `script.im` importing `modules::MathUtils` fails from the repo root: `go run ./cmd/infomunge -f tmp/review_import/script.im`
- Error searched only in repo-root paths: `/Users/david/Documents/code/repos/infomunge` and `/Users/david/Documents/code/repos/infomunge/modules`
- The same script succeeds when run from `tmp/review_import`: `go run ../../cmd/infomunge -f script.im` -> `42`

Code references:
- `internal/cli/app.go:133-141`
- `internal/runner/runner.go:74-83`
- `internal/runner/runner.go:163`

Expected:
- `-f <path>` should resolve relative imports from the script file's directory, matching `runner.RunWithConfig` behavior.

title: Line comment stripping breaks regex literals with //
description: Current preprocessing strips // line comments before regex literals are replaced. Regex like /https?:\/\/.+/ is truncated at //, causing parse errors or incorrect behavior. Consider making comment stripping regex-aware or move stripping after regex literal replacement, with tests.

title: Test: Create comprehensive error handling test suite
description:
Issue: Error handling coverage is minimal across test suite

Current state:
- error_reporting.feature: Only 4 scenarios, minimal validation
- Most feature files only test happy path or check 'should fail' without validating error message

Missing error scenario testing:
1. Division by zero error messages
2. Type mismatch error messages  
3. Out of bounds/index errors
4. Null pointer operations
5. Invalid function arguments
6. File I/O errors (not found, permission denied)
7. Invalid JSON/XML/YAML format errors
8. Circular dependency errors in imports
9. Timeout/resource exhaustion errors

Recommendation: Create error_messages.feature with 30+ scenarios validating:
- Exact error text for each error condition
- Line/column accuracy in error reporting
- Error messages for common user mistakes

title: Implement missing Strings module functions (appendIfMissing, charCodeAt, fromCharCode, etc.)
description: Implement missing dw::core::Strings functions such as appendIfMissing, charCodeAt, fromCharCode, etc. Add tests for each function.

title: Add take() and drop() array functions
description: DataWeave has take() and drop() functions for array slicing, e.g., take([1,2,3,4,5], 3) returns [1,2,3], drop([1,2,3,4,5], 2) returns [3,4,5]. These are missing in infomunge.

title: Audit operator chaining for body boundary detection issues
description:
The fix for $.*field with chained collection operators (filter...map) revealed that body boundary detection wasn't stopping at collection operators.

Similar issues may exist with:
1. Other collection operators: reduce, groupBy, flatMap, pluck, sort, orderBy, distinctBy, filterObject, mapObject
2. Binary operators that should end lambda bodies: update, as, is, contains, splitBy, joinBy, ++, etc.
3. Nested/recursive lambda expressions
4. Complex expressions mixing multiple operator types

Investigation needed:
1. Create test cases for various operator chaining scenarios
2. Verify body extraction stops at correct boundaries
