3. Check if the current list of 'stopping operators' in scanLambdaBody, replaceArrowFunctions, and replaceCollectionOperator is complete
close_reason: Audit complete. Found two bugs: infomunge-t4z2 (missing operators) and infomunge-bs2s (chaining failure). See tmp/chaining_audit.md

title: Define error result types with type-specific information
description: Many functions return (interface{}, error) losing type information. Create typed Result[T] type (like Rust's Result) for functions that have known output types. Examples: ReadObject(string) Result[Object], FormatAsJSON(Object) Result[string]. Improves error handling and reduces type assertions.

title: Create Cucumber tests for DataWeave core functions
description:
Epic to create comprehensive Cucumber BDD tests for all DataWeave core functions implemented under infomunge-j1t.

Should cover:
- groupBy, pluck
- avg, sum, maxBy, minBy, orderBy
- distinctBy, filterObject, find
- flatMap, match, matches, scan
- isBlank, isDecimal, isInteger, isEven, isOdd

- mapObject, splitBy, lower, upper

- to, zip, unzip, range

Create tests for range and zip functions: to, range, zip, unzip
Create tests for I/O functions: write, read, readUrl
Create tests for date/time functions: now, daysBetween, isLeapYear
Create tests for operators: ++ (concatenate) and -- (remove)
Create tests for utility functions: with, xsiType, mod, evaluateCompatibilityFlag

Create tests for filtering/transformation: distinctBy, filterObject, find, filter, map

Add DataWeave-compatible format support: flatfile
description: MIME type: application/flatfile. Add flat file reader/writer support (including fixed-width/copybook-style mappings as feasible).

title: Support 'pluck' on Objects with lambda
description:
In DataWeave, 'pluck' can be used on an Object to iterate over keys and values, returning an array. It takes a lambda (value, key, index) -> result.

In InfoMunge, 'pluck' currently seems to only support extracting a field from an array of objects (e.g. 'payload pluck "name"').

Reproduction:
%im 0.1
output application/json
---
{"a": 1, "b": 2} pluck (v, k) -> k

Error: lambda expression requires exactly 2 arguments... (or similar parse error indicating lambda not accepted for pluck)

title: LazyMap/LazyFilter silently drop errors from lambdas
description: LazyMap and LazyFilter currently ignore lambda evaluation errors (continue), which can hide failures and produce partial output. Decide on an error propagation strategy (e.g., emit a control/error value, return a LazyValue that fails on GetValue, or surface via a paired error channel) and update behavior/tests. Ref: internal/evaluator/lazy.go:23-67.

title: Intensive Expression Testing
description: Implement grammar-aware property-based testing, mutation testing, and differential testing for infomunge expressions using the rapid library. Goal: greatly improve robustness without manually authoring large numbers of test expressions. See docs/intensive_expression_testing_proposal.md for the full proposal.

title: Add rapid dependency
description: Add pgregory.net/rapid (v1.2.0+) as a test dependency via go get. Verify it compiles and a trivial rapid.Check test passes. This is the foundation library for all property-based and fuzz testing work.

title: Add collection operator and lambda generators
description:
Create internal/testing/exprgen/collections.go with generators for:

- Collection operators: map, filter, reduce, flatMap applied to array expressions
- Lambda expressions: (param) -> expr and (param, index) -> expr forms
- Implicit dollar-sign lambda: $ and $$ references
- The generator must track lambda parameter names in scope so that nested lambdas reference the correct variables

Update ExprGen to include CollectionOpGen and LambdaGen. Add self-tests verifying generated collection expressions parse correctly.

title: Add conditional, default, string interpolation, and builtin call generators
description:
Expand the expression generator to support:

- Conditional: if (expr) expr else expr
- Default operator: expr default expr
- String interpolation: "text $(expr) text"
- Builtin function calls: builtin(expr, ...) for a subset of builtins: sizeOf, typeOf, upper, lower, flatten, keys, values, trim, isEmpty, contains, startsWith, endsWith
- Case expression: case expr { pattern => expr, ... } (stretch — add if straightforward)

Each builtin call generator should respect the function's arity. Add generator self-tests.

title: Add remaining binary operators to generator
description:
Expand the operator generator to include the full operator set:

- Arithmetic: **, % (in addition to existing +, -, *, /)
- Comparison: <=, >= (in addition to existing <, >, ==, !=)
- String/array concatenation: ++
- Regex match: ~=
- Logical: complete set (&&, || already exist)

Update operator weights so common operators are exercised more frequently than rare ones. Add self-tests.

title: Implement algebraic property tests
description:
Create internal/testing/properties/properties_test.go with algebraic property tests:

Arithmetic identities (generate numeric x):
- x + 0 == x
- x * 1 == x
- x * 0 == 0
- x ** 1 == x

Commutativity (generate numeric a, b):
- a + b == b + a
- a * b == b * a

Associativity (generate small numeric a, b, c — use tolerance for floats):
- (a + b) + c == a + (b + c)

Default operator (generate arbitrary x, y):
- x default x == x
- x default y == x when x is non-null
- null default y == y

Boolean logic (generate boolean x):
- !(!x) == x
- x && true == x
- x || false == x

Collection identity (generate array arr):
- arr map (x) -> x == arr
- arr filter (x) -> true == arr

Concatenation (generate array arr):
- [] ++ arr == arr
- arr ++ [] == arr

String operations (generate string s):
- upper(lower(s)) preserves length
- sizeOf(s) >= 0

Each property test uses rapid.Check. Build full infomunge scripts for each property and evaluate via the runner.

title: Implement structural property tests
description:
Create internal/testing/properties/roundtrip_test.go with structural and round-trip property tests:

Structural properties (generate arrays/objects with the expression generator):
- sizeOf(arr map f) == sizeOf(arr) for any non-erroring f
- sizeOf(arr filter f) <= sizeOf(arr)
- sizeOf(flatten(arr)) >= sizeOf(arr) for arrays of arrays
- sizeOf(keys(obj)) == sizeOf(values(obj))

Round-trip property (generate JSON-safe values):
- read(write(val, 'json'), 'application/json') == val

Stability property:
- Byte-identical output when the same expression+input is evaluated multiple times in sequence

Each test uses rapid.Check with the expression and context generators. Verify these properties hold across thousands of generated cases.

title: Implement coverage-guided fuzz targets
description:
Bridge the expression generator to Go's native fuzzer via rapid.MakeFuzz.

Create internal/testing/properties/fuzz_test.go with:

1. FuzzExprEval — generates expressions at depth 3, evaluates with sample context, checks:
   - No panics (implicit via recover)
   - Successful results are JSON-serializable
   - Type consistency
2. FuzzExprPreprocess — generates expressions, runs through preprocessor only, checks no panics
3. FuzzExprDeep — generates expressions at depth 5-6 for deeper exploration

Usage: go test -fuzz=FuzzExprEval -fuzztime=10m ./internal/testing/properties/

Note on rapid.MakeFuzz: rapid provides structured generation within Go's fuzz infrastructure. The coverage guidance comes from Go's fuzzer driving the byte stream; rapid interprets the bytes into structured expressions. This means most exploration hits valid expressions rather than random byte noise.

Add a testdata/fuzz/ directory for corpus persistence across runs.

title: Build cucumber corpus extractor
description:
Create internal/testing/mutation/extractor.go:

Parse .feature files under test/features/ to extract expression/input/expected-output triples:
- Extract the script text from 'When infomunge processes' steps
- Extract input payloads from 'Given input payload is' steps (and named inputs)
- Extract expected outputs from 'Then' steps
- Store as a structured corpus: []CorpusEntry{Script, Inputs, ExpectedOutput, SourceFile, ScenarioName}

ExtractCorpus(featuresDir) returns all entries. This is a one-time extraction that can be re-run as the test suite grows.

Include unit tests that run against the actual test/features/ directory and verify the extractor finds a reasonable number of entries (sanity check).

title: Build expression mutation engine
description:
Create internal/testing/mutation/mutator.go with mutation operators that transform infomunge source-level expressions:

Mutation operators:
- OperatorSwap: replace a binary operator with another (+ → -, map → filter, == → !=, etc.)
- LiteralPerturb: change literals (1 → 0, "a" → "", true → false, null → 0)
- SubtreeSwap: exchange subexpressions between two corpus entries (requires basic expression boundary detection)
- ArgManipulate: remove/add/reorder arguments in function calls
- NestWrap: wrap a subexpression in an extra layer (x → [x][0], x → (x))
- ParenMutate: insert or remove parentheses to stress precedence handling
- FunctionSwap: substitute among compatible builtins (same arity)

Mutate(expr string, rng *rand.Rand) returns a mutated expression string. Each mutation operator works at the source text level using simple pattern matching (not full parsing).

MutateN(expr, n, rng) applies n random mutations in sequence.

Include unit tests verifying each operator produces syntactically different output.

title: Implement mutation-based property tests
description:
Create internal/testing/mutation/mutation_test.go:

For each corpus entry extracted from cucumber features:
1. Apply 1-3 random mutations to the expression
2. Evaluate the mutated expression with the original inputs
3. Assert the invariant: mutated expressions should either produce a result or return an error — never panic
4. Optionally check determinism: same mutation evaluated twice gives same result

Use rapid.Check to drive the random mutation selection. Feed any panics or unexpected failures into the failure artifact pipeline (artifact.go + scenario_gen.go).

Run configuration:
- Default: process a random subset of 100 corpus entries per test run (fast CI mode)
- Full soak: process all entries with up to 10 mutations each (local/nightly mode, controlled by env var)

Include a test that verifies the mutation engine produces at least some non-trivial mutations (i.e., not all mutations result in identical expressions).

title: Build DataWeave CLI harness
description:
Create internal/testing/differential/dw_harness.go:

Wrap the DataWeave CLI (dw run -i payload ...) for differential comparison:
- DWAvailable() checks if the dw command is on PATH; all differential tests skip if not
- DWEval(script, inputs) shells out to dw, captures stdout/stderr, returns parsed result or error
- Timeout: 10 seconds per evaluation (dw can hang on invalid input)
- Normalization rules for known divergences between infomunge and DataWeave:
  - Numeric precision: compare with tolerance for floats
  - Null/missing conventions: map known null representation differences
  - Key ordering: compare objects as unordered key-value sets
  - Whitespace/formatting: compare parsed values, not raw strings

StructuralCompare(infomungeResult, dwResult) returns a detailed diff on mismatch.

Include unit tests with mocked dw output to verify normalization and comparison logic.

title: Build literal expression generator
description:
Create internal/testing/exprgen/literals.go with rapid generators for the minimal literal subset:

- Integers (including zero, negatives, large values)
- Floats (including zero, negatives, edge cases like very small/large)
- Strings (including empty, special characters, unicode)
- Booleans (true, false)
- Null

Each generator should produce a valid infomunge source-level string representation. Include unit tests in literals_test.go verifying that generated literals are syntactically valid.

title: Implement differential comparison tests
description:
Create internal/testing/differential/differential_test.go:

- Add a DW-compatible flag to the expression generator: tag each generated expression with whether it uses infomunge-only features (e.g., while loops). Only generate DW-compatible expressions for differential tests.
- For each generated expression+context:
  1. Evaluate in infomunge
  2. Evaluate in DataWeave via the harness
  3. Compare results using StructuralCompare
  4. On mismatch, save failure artifact and log the expression with both results
- Use rapid.Check with moderate iteration count (1000 — dw CLI is slow)
- All tests skip gracefully if dw is not available (t.Skip)

Feed discrepancies into the failure artifact pipeline for triage and potential cucumber scenario generation.

title: Add CI integration for property and fuzz tests
description:
Configure CI-friendly test runs for the intensive testing suite:

Short-budget CI run (must complete in under 60 seconds):
- Property tests with fixed seed and reduced iteration count (e.g., 500 cases)
- Mutation tests on a random subset of 50 corpus entries
- Fuzz test with -fuzztime=30s

Local/nightly soak run:
- Property tests with 50000+ iterations
- Full mutation corpus with 10 mutations each
- Fuzz test with -fuzztime=30m
- Controlled by INTENSIVE_TEST_SOAK=1 environment variable

Corpus management:
- Persist interesting fuzz corpus entries across runs in testdata/fuzz/
- Add testdata/fuzz/ to version control so corpus grows over time
- Add tmp/intensive-testing/ to .gitignore

Add a Makefile target or script for running the soak tests locally.

title: Implement success metrics reporting
description:
Add metrics collection and reporting to the intensive testing suite:

Track and report after each run:
- Unique failures found (count distinct fingerprints)
- Shrink ratio (average minimized expression length / original length, target ≤ 20%)
- Time-to-minimal-repro (wall-clock from detection to shrunk artifact, target < 30s)
- Promoted cucumber regressions (count scenarios in test/features/ originating from intensive testing)
- Coverage deltas (run go test -coverprofile before/after, diff preprocessor + evaluator line coverage)
- Panic rate (count panics per run, target: 0)
- Mutation kill rate (ratio of detected vs undetected non-equivalent mutations)

Output a summary report to stdout at end of test run. Optionally write to tmp/intensive-testing/report.json for trend tracking.

Review metrics after each phase to decide whether to continue investing or redirect effort.

title: Mutation corpus extractor captures non-equality Then assertions as expected output
description:
Extractor currently treats any quoted Then step as ExpectedOutput (e.g. 'Then the output should contain "x"' and 'Then the error should contain "x"'). This pollutes corpus entries with substring/error assertions as if they were exact output expectations.

Scope:
- Restrict expected-output extraction to exact-equality Then steps only (docstring and scalar forms).
- Ignore contain/error/valid-JSON style Then assertions for ExpectedOutput.
- Add regression tests to prevent reintroduction.

title: Build operator expression generator
description:
Create internal/testing/exprgen/operators.go with rapid generators for the minimal operator subset:

- Binary operators: +, -, *, /, ==, !=, <, >, &&, ||
- Unary operators: !, - (negation)
- Parenthesized expressions: (expr)

Generators must be recursive with a max-depth parameter (start with depth 3-4). Use rapid's Deferred for recursive references. Ensure brackets are balanced by construction. Include array literal generator: [expr, ...] with 0-5 elements.

Include unit tests verifying generated expressions are syntactically valid at various depths.

title: Build test context/payload generator
description:
Create internal/testing/exprgen/context.go with rapid generators for test contexts:

- SampleContext() generates a payload with a mix of:
  - Flat objects with string/number/boolean/null fields
  - Nested objects (1-2 levels)
  - Arrays of objects, arrays of primitives
  - Empty objects and arrays
- Variable reference generator (IdentGen) that only produces identifiers in scope: payload, payload.field for fields that exist in the generated context

The context generator must produce both the Go value (for passing to the runner) and the JSON string (for use as CLI input). Include unit tests.

title: Build core expression generator with script wrapping
description:
Create internal/testing/exprgen/generator.go that composes the literal, operator, and context generators into a complete expression generator.

- Expression(maxDepth) returns a rapid generator that produces full infomunge source-level expression strings
- WrapScript(expr) wraps an expression in a valid script with header: '%im 0.1\noutput application/json\n---\nexpr'
- Feature subset parameter to control which expression forms are enabled (start with arithmetic/comparison/arrays only)
- Lightweight validity guard: skip generated cases that fail preprocessing with a syntax error (don't count toward test budget)

Include generator_test.go with self-tests:
- Generated expressions have bounded depth
- Generated expressions are syntactically valid (pass through preprocessor without panic)
- Feature subset parameter actually restricts output

title: Implement no-panic property test
description:
Create internal/testing/properties/nopanic_test.go with the foundational property test:

- For any generated expression and context, evaluating the expression should either produce a result or return an error — never panic
- Use rapid.Check with a high iteration count (e.g., 10000)
- Recover from panics and report them as test failures with the expression and context that caused the panic
- Include the determinism property: eval(expr, ctx) called twice produces identical output
- Include the type consistency property: typeOf(eval(expr)) returns a valid type string

This single test file is the highest-value deliverable — it will likely surface bugs immediately.

title: Implement failure artifact capture
description:
Create internal/testing/failures/artifact.go:

- Artifact struct recording: minimized expression, input/payload, violated property name, actual vs expected result (or panic stack trace), original pre-shrink expression, random seed for reproducibility
- SaveArtifact() writes a JSON file to tmp/intensive-testing/failures/ with a sequential ID and timestamp in the filename (e.g., 001_nopanic_2026-02-10T14:30:00.json)
- Deduplication via fingerprinting: hash of (minimized expression + violated property). Skip saving if fingerprint already exists in the failures directory
- LoadArtifacts() reads all artifacts from the directory for reporting

Include unit tests for serialization round-trip and deduplication logic. Ensure tmp/intensive-testing/failures/ is in .gitignore.

title: Implement cucumber scenario auto-generator
description:
Create internal/testing/failures/scenario_gen.go:

- GenerateScenario(artifact) produces a .feature scenario skeleton from a failure artifact
- Template includes: comment with property name, shrunk expression, original seed; Given step with input payload; When step with script; Then step with placeholder for expected result or error
- WriteCandidateScenario() saves the generated .feature text to tmp/intensive-testing/candidates/ for human review
- Batch mode: GenerateAllCandidates() processes all artifacts that don't already have a corresponding candidate

Example output:
  # Auto-generated from intensive testing failure 001
  # Property: no-panic
  Scenario: Expression does not panic on null index arithmetic
    Given input payload is ...
    When infomunge processes ...
    Then the error should contain '...'

Include unit tests verifying generated scenarios are valid Gherkin syntax. Ensure tmp/intensive-testing/candidates/ is in .gitignore.

title: Add object literal and dot/index access generators
description:
Expand the expression generator to support:

- Object literals: {key: expr, ...} with 0-5 fields, string keys
- Dot access: expr.field (field names drawn from context shape)
- Index access: expr[expr] (integer and string indices)
- Range index: expr[expr to expr]

Update the ExprGen OneOf to include these forms. Ensure generated field names are valid identifiers. Add generator self-tests for syntactic validity of new forms.

title: Add union types
description: Support union type syntax for accepting multiple types. Example: String | Number | Null

title: Improve Java-to-Go Date Pattern Mapping
description: The convertJavaDatePatternToGo function provides only partial mapping. Document the supported subset of Java date patterns explicitly and consider using a more comprehensive library or mapping strategy to improve DataWeave compatibility.

title: Consolidate XML namespace functions with generics
description: Replace buildNamespaceDeclsFromMap and buildNamespaceDeclsFromStringMap with a generic version

title: Code smell: No input validation in Read/Format functions
description: formats package doesn't validate inputs. Empty strings, very large inputs, or malformed data could cause issues.

title: Simplify RewriteWithDepth by extracting handler methods
description:
The RewriteWithDepth function in preprocessor.go is complex (130+ lines) with nested conditionals. The handleIfElse, handleAndOr, handleNewline, handleOpenBrace, handleCloseBrace, and handleUnquotedKey methods help but the main loop is still hard to follow.

Consider:
- Adding more focused helper methods for the string state machine
- Better separation of concerns between parsing structure and transformation
- Extracting the bracket/brace/quote tracking into a separate state machine

title: Robust string and escape handling in preprocessor
description: Replace the current quote-conversion heuristic with a proper lexer/parser for pre-processing DataWeave-style strings.

title: Implement missing DataWeave operators
description:
Implement DataWeave operators that are currently missing from infomunge to improve compatibility with MuleSoft DataWeave expressions.

Reference: https://docs.mulesoft.com/dataweave/latest/dw-operators

## Missing Operators

1. **Logical operators**: `or`, `not` keyword
2. **Array operators**: `>>` (prepend), `<<` (append)  
3. **Equality**: `~=` (coercion equality)
4. **Flow control**: `do` scoped blocks
5. **Update syntax**: DataWeave pattern-matching update expressions

## Current Status

- `or` - errors with 'unsupported operation: true || false'
- `not` - parse error
- `>>` / `<<` - unsupported operation errors
- `~=` - parse error
- `do { ... }` - parse error  
- `update { case ... }` - parse error

title: Implement 'or' logical operator
description:
Implement the `or` logical operator for DataWeave compatibility.

## Current Behavior
```
./infomunge '%im 0.1
output application/json
---
true or false'
```
Error: `4:1: unsupported operation: true || false`

## Expected Behavior
Should return `true` (same as DataWeave).

## Notes
The error suggests `or` is being parsed and converted to `||` internally, but the evaluation fails. Need to check the evaluator for binary logical operations.

title: Implement 'not' keyword operator
description:
Implement the `not` keyword as a logical negation operator.

## Current Behavior
```
./infomunge '%im 0.1
output application/json
---
not true'
```
Error: `4:5: expected 'EOF', found true`

## Expected Behavior
Should return `false` (same as DataWeave).

## Notes
The `!` operator already works (`!true` returns `false`), so this is a parsing issue. Need to add `not` as a unary prefix operator in the lexer/parser.

title: Implement '>>' prepend and '<<' append operators
description:
Implement array prepend (`>>`) and append (`<<`) operators.

## Current Behavior
```
1 >> [2]    # Error: unsupported operation: 1 >> [2]
[1] << 2    # Error: unsupported operation: [1] << 2
```

## Expected Behavior
```
1 >> [2]    # Returns [1, 2] (prepend 1 to array)
[1] << 2    # Returns [1, 2] (append 2 to array)
```

## Notes
- `>>` prepends the left operand to the array on the right
- `<<` appends the right operand to the array on the left
- Currently `++` can concatenate arrays but doesn't handle single element + array

title: Implement '~=' coercion equality operator
description:
Implement the `~=` coercion equality operator that compares values after type coercion.

## Current Behavior
```
./infomunge '%im 0.1
output application/json
---
"1" ~= 1'
```
Error: `4:5: expected 'EOF', found '~'`

## Expected Behavior
Should return `true` because "1" coerced to number equals 1.

## DataWeave Behavior
- Tries to coerce one value to the type of the other
- `"1" ~= 1` returns `true`
- `"abc" ~= 123` returns `false` (coercion fails)

## Notes
Need to add `~=` as a binary operator in lexer/parser and implement type coercion logic in evaluator.

title: Implement 'do' scoped block expressions
description:
Implement the `do` keyword for creating scoped blocks with local variables.

## Current Behavior
```
do {
  var x = 1
  var y = 2
  ---
  x + y
}
```
Error: `4:4: expected 'EOF', found 'map'`

## Expected Behavior
Should return `3` - evaluating the expression after `---` with access to locally defined variables.

## DataWeave Syntax
```
do {
  var localVar = "value"
  fun localFun() = "result"
  ---
  localFun() ++ localVar
}
```

## Notes
The `do` block creates a scope where:
- Variables and functions can be declared
- The expression after `---` is evaluated in that scope
- Variables are not visible outside the block

title: Implement DataWeave 'update' expression syntax
description:
Implement the DataWeave `update` expression for pattern-matching field updates.

## Current Behavior
```
user update {
  case age at .age -> age + 1
}
```
Error: `5:6: expected 'EOF', found update`

## Expected Behavior
Should increment the `age` field by 1 without recreating the entire object.

## DataWeave Syntax
```
myInput update {
  case field at .fieldName -> newValue
  case idx at .array[0] -> newValue  
  case attr at .@attribute -> newValue
}
```

## Notes
- This is a more complex feature than simple operators
- Supports value selectors (`.field`), index selectors (`.array[0]`), and attribute selectors (`.@attr`)
- The `~` operator in infomunge provides simple object merging but not the pattern-matching capability
- Lower priority as `~` covers basic use cases

title: Medium: Add recursion depth protection to setValueAtPath function
description:
File: internal/evaluator/builtins_core.go, lines 535-562

The setValueAtPath() function is recursive but lacks depth limit checks. This could cause stack overflow on deeply nested paths (e.g., a.b.c.d.e.f...x.y.z with 1000+ levels).

Recommendation:
1. Add depth parameter to setValueAtPath() signature
2. Check depth against MaxEvalDepth and return error if exceeded
3. Increment depth on recursive calls
4. Update callers to pass initial depth parameter

This prevents potential DoS via deeply nested path specifications, consistent with preprocessor depth limits (MaxRecursionDepth = 100).

title: Replace substring assertions with structured JSON assertions in io and cookbook features
description:
Audit follow-up from infomunge-l7sp.

Problem:
Several feature files assert complex structured outputs using broad substring checks, notably test/features/io_functions.feature and test/features/dataweave_cookbook_examples.feature.

Examples:
- io_functions read scenarios at lines 7 and 19 rely on contains Alice and 30.
- dataweave_cookbook_examples transformations (for example lines 26, 60, 162) assert only selected fragments.

Risk:
Incorrect structure, missing fields, and type regressions can pass as long as one expected substring remains.

Required changes:
- Replace contains-based assertions with exact JSON docstring assertions or stricter typed checks for key/value and shape.
- Prioritize scenarios covering read(), write(), map, groupBy, and mapObject cookbook flows.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least 10 substring-based assertions across these files are replaced by structured assertions.
- Updated scenarios fail when keys are missing or values are wrong but still textually similar.

title: Add type guards and validation helpers

title: Extract reusable bracket/depth/string-state scanner in preprocessor
description:
The pattern of initializing depth := 0, inString := false and then doing manual character-by-character bracket tracking with string escape detection is repeated 15+ times across the preprocessor package:
- transformers_operators.go: lines 58, 151, 234, 266, 376, 560 (6 instances)

The existing stringState struct is used in some places but not consistently.

Suggested approach:
- Create a unified DepthTracker or BracketScanner helper in preprocessor/utils.go or a new preprocessor/scanner_util.go

DataWeave uses '@attr' to access XML attributes. InfoMunge currently requires bracket notation like '["@attr"]' because '@' is not a valid identifier character in the Go parser.

The preprocessor should handle '@' as a selector prefix for better DataWeave compatibility.

docs/DATAWEAVE_COMPATIBILITY_TASKS.md and related migration docs still list several differences that are already implemented (array .name selection, object expression parentheses, .*, implicit $/$$, reduce initial value, nested mapObject, mapObject object returns).

title: Use return struct for findBranches instead of 5 positional values
description:
internal/preprocessor/rewriter_handlers.go:282 — findBranches() returns (int, int, int, int, bool), making call sites extremely hard to read and error-prone. Similarly, scanBranchEnd() at line 719 returns (int, int, int, bool) — 4 values with unclear semantics (position, elsePos, errPos, ok).

Suggested approach:
- Define a BranchPositions struct with named fields

The preprocessor rewrites '%' to mod() internally, but the source syntax differs. To be fully DW-compatible, infomunge should accept 'mod' as a binary keyword operator in source expressions.

title: Property no-panic test treats lambda results as nondeterministic
description:
While reproducing infomunge-tmjo, the property suite `TestEvaluate_NoPanics_Deterministic_AndTypeConsistent` now fails earlier on lambda expression values with a nondeterminism assertion:

- Repro command: `go test ./internal/testing/properties -run TestEvaluate_NoPanics_Deterministic_AndTypeConsistent -count=1`
- Example failing expr: `(left, current) -> -1.7976931348623157e+308`
- Failure: `reflect.DeepEqual` reports two evaluated lambda results as unequal due to pointer identity in lambda internals, even though behavior is deterministic.

Impact:
- Masks other property failures (including parser regressions) by failing at test start.
- Makes property checks noisy and non-actionable for function-valued expressions.

Suggested fix direction:
1. In nondeterminism assertions, treat function/lambda results as deterministic if type and callable semantics are stable (or skip deep-equality for `typeOf(expr) == "Function"`).
2. Keep no-panic and error determinism checks for all expressions.
3. Add focused regression test for deterministic handling of lambda-valued expressions.

title: Extract shared server handler code from duplicated JS and HTTP implementations

Eight functions are copy-pasted verbatim between cmd/infomunge-js/main.go and internal/cli/server.go: decodeRunRequest(), ensureEOF(), resolveOutputMimeType(), normalizeMimeType(), buildRunContext(), formatRunResult(), extractNamespaceVars(), applyXMLOutputOptions(). The struct types runInput and runRequest are also duplicated.

This is the single highest-ROI refactoring opportunity in the codebase — any bug fix in request handling must currently be applied in two places.

Suggested approach:
- Create a new package (e.g. internal/handlers or internal/server/shared) containing the shared types and functions
- Have both cmd/infomunge-js/main.go and internal/cli/server.go import from the shared package
- Verify with existing cucumber tests that behavior is unchanged

title: Lazy evaluation Phase 1: LazyValue wrapper type

- Dependencies are tracked correctly

- Computed values are cached until invalidated

High: Extract common lambda iteration pattern into helper function
description:
File: internal/evaluator/builtins_core.go (multiple locations)

The same lambda iteration pattern appears 8+ times across:
- callBuiltinFilter() (lines 782-814)
- callBuiltinMap() (lines 817-839)
- callBuiltinFlatMap() (lines 1645-1673)
- callBuiltinMapInternal() (lines 1626-1643)
- Similar patterns in other array functions

Repeating pattern:
for i, elem := range array {
    lambdaContext := copyContext(context)
    lambdaContext[lambda.ParamName(0)] = elem
    if lambda.ParamCount() > 1 {
        lambdaContext[lambda.ParamName(1)] = i
    }
    result, err := evalASTWithDepth(lambda.BodyAST, lambdaContext, depth+1)

}

Examples: mod with small divisor (test/features/utility_functions.feature:79), read XML content (test/features/io_functions.feature:43), write formatted output with indentation (test/features/io_functions.feature:367), and check if current year is leap year (test/features/date_time_functions.feature:425). title: Add lazy evaluation support

Support lazy evaluation and streaming for large data sets.

## Sub-tasks
This epic has been broken down into phases:

1. **infomunge-3q8**: Phase 1 - LazyValue wrapper type
2. **infomunge-vzr**: Phase 2 - Stream pipeline operations

title: Add multi-line string literals

title: Input name collisions silently overwrite values across CLI and /run
description:
Problem
Input variable names are not validated consistently and duplicate names silently overwrite previous values.

Evidence
- `internal/io/input.go:74-95` parses `-i name=source` and writes directly to `context[name]` without trimming/identifier validation or duplicate detection.
- `internal/handlers/run.go:80-97` trims name but still writes to `context[name]` with no duplicate-name check.
- Existing server hardening ticket (`infomunge-awpq`) calls out max input count and identifier validation, but does not track duplicate-name collision behavior or CLI parity.

Impact
- Silent data loss/ambiguity: later inputs override earlier ones with no warning.
- Inconsistent behavior between CLI and server paths (CLI currently allows empty/whitespace names that server rejects).
- Hard-to-debug script outcomes when payloads are unintentionally shadowed.

Scope
- Enforce a shared input-name validation rule across CLI and server (identifier format + non-empty after trim).
- Reject duplicate names with a clear validation error showing conflicting name.
- Add cucumber coverage for duplicate names and invalid names via both CLI and /run harness paths.

Acceptance criteria
- Duplicate input names fail fast with deterministic validation errors in both CLI and server code paths.
- Invalid names (empty, whitespace, non-identifier characters) fail consistently across both paths.
- Tests cover at least: duplicate names, empty name, and whitespace-only name.

title: Make assertion_matchers negative tests assert matcher-specific error diagnostics
description:
Audit follow-up from infomunge-l7sp.

Problem:
Negative cases in test/features/assertion_matchers.feature commonly assert only the generic phrase assertion failed (for example line 30 and many repeats).

Risk:
Matcher-specific failure quality can regress while tests continue to pass on generic error text.

Required changes:
- Upgrade negative matcher scenarios to assert matcher-specific diagnostics.
- Ensure failures mention the matcher and expected-vs-actual mismatch where available.
- Keep one broad smoke test for generic assertion failure plumbing.

Acceptance criteria:
- At least 12 negative scenarios assert matcher-specific error fragments.
- Generic assertion failed-only checks are reduced to minimal smoke coverage.

title: Test: Add cucumber tests for exponent operator edge cases
description:
Add cucumber tests for exponent operator (**) edge cases. The replaceExponentOperator function shows only 23% coverage.

Tests should cover:
- Basic exponentiation (2 ** 3)
- Negative exponents
- Fractional exponents
- Chained exponents (a ** b ** c - right associativity)
- Exponent with expressions as operands
- Exponent combined with other operators (precedence)
- Edge cases like 0 ** 0, negative bases with fractional exponents

title: DataWeave-style operators and expressions
description: Add core DataWeave operators to enable powerful data transformations. These features unlock 80% of real-world transformation use cases.

title: Add dot notation for field access
description:
Support dot notation for accessing object fields.

**Syntax:**
```
payload.name        # instead of payload["name"]
payload.user.email  # nested access
```

**Implementation:**
1. Update preprocessor to convert `.field` to `["field"]`
2. Handle nested dot chains
3. Preserve existing bracket notation

title: Add lambda expression support
description:
Support lambda/anonymous function syntax for use with map, filter, and reduce.

**Syntax:**
```
(x) -> x + 1
(item, index) -> item.name
```

**Implementation:**
1. Parse arrow function syntax in preprocessor
2. Create callable function representation in evaluator
3. Support single and multiple parameters

This is a prerequisite for map/filter/reduce operators.

title: Add map operator
description:
Support the map operator for transforming arrays.

**Syntax:**
```
items map (item) -> item.name
items map (item, index) -> { position: index, value: item }
```

**Implementation:**
1. Parse infix `map` operator in preprocessor
2. Evaluate by applying lambda to each array element
3. Support optional index parameter

title: Add filter operator
description:
Support the filter operator for selecting array elements.

**Syntax:**
```
items filter (item) -> item.active
items filter (item) -> item.age > 18
```

**Implementation:**
1. Parse infix `filter` operator in preprocessor
2. Evaluate by keeping elements where lambda returns true
3. Support optional index parameter

title: Add if/else expressions
description:
Support conditional if/else expressions (not statements).

**Syntax:**
```
if (x > 0) "positive" else "non-positive"
if (user.active) user.name else "anonymous"
```

**Implementation:**
1. Parse if/else as expression in preprocessor (convert to Go ternary-like construct or handle in evaluator)
2. Evaluate condition and return appropriate branch
3. Both branches must be present (else is required)

title: Add reduce operator
description:
Support the reduce operator for aggregating arrays.

**Syntax:**
```
nums reduce (acc, n) -> acc + n
items reduce (acc, item) -> acc ++ [item.name]
```

**Implementation:**
1. Parse infix `reduce` operator
2. Evaluate by folding array with accumulator
3. First element is initial accumulator value (or support explicit initial value)

title: Add default operator for null coalescing
description:
Support the default operator for null/missing value handling.

**Syntax:**
```
user.nickname default "anonymous"
payload.count default 0
```

**Implementation:**
1. Parse infix `default` operator
2. Return left side if not null/nil, otherwise return right side
3. Handle missing map keys gracefully

title: Add sizeOf function
description:
Support the sizeOf function for getting collection/string length.

**Syntax:**
```
sizeOf(items)        # array length
sizeOf(payload)      # object key count  
sizeOf("hello")      # string length: 5
```

**Implementation:**
1. Add sizeOf to built-in functions in evaluator
2. Handle arrays, objects, and strings
3. Return error for unsupported types

title: Implement source mapping for evaluation errors

This logic should be extracted into smaller handlers or a more robust transformation framework to improve maintainability and reduce the risk of errors during parsing.

title: Refactor: Split large evaluator_test.go into focused test files
description:
Issue: evaluator_test.go is 1270 lines with 34 test functions

Current state:
- Single file contains tests for: literals, arithmetic, comparisons, strings, arrays, objects, indexing, error handling
- Difficult to navigate and maintain
- Makes it hard to find specific test categories

Recommendations:
Split into focused test files:
- evaluator_literals_test.go - Basic literals and type coercion
- evaluator_arithmetic_test.go - Arithmetic operations
- evaluator_string_test.go - String operations
- evaluator_collections_test.go - Arrays and objects
- evaluator_indexing_test.go - Index operations
- evaluator_error_test.go - Error handling scenarios

Benefits:
- Easier navigation and maintenance
- Better code organization
- More focused test file names make intentions clearer

title: --lazy flag is wired but has no runtime effect
description:
Problem
The CLI/server wiring passes `Config.Lazy` into `runner.RunnerOptions{Lazy: ...}`, but the runner/evaluator execution path never reads `opts.Lazy`. The flag currently changes nothing.

Evidence
- `internal/cli/app.go` sets `RunnerOptions{Lazy: config.Lazy}`.
- `internal/cli/server.go` sets `RunnerOptions{Lazy: config.Lazy}`.
- `internal/runner/runner.go` defines `RunnerOptions.Lazy` but does not use it in `runFromStringWithConfig`, `evaluate`, or `evaluateWithContext`.

Impact
- Users can pass `--lazy` and believe runtime semantics/performance are changing when behavior is identical.
- Dead configuration surface increases maintenance cost and creates documentation drift.

Scope
- Either implement `RunnerOptions.Lazy` behavior end-to-end, or remove/deprecate the flag and option field.
- Add explicit test coverage that verifies mode behavior (or verifies rejection/deprecation path if removed).
- Update README/docs to reflect actual behavior.

Acceptance criteria
- A regression test fails today and passes after fix: `--lazy` must either produce measurably different execution mode semantics or return a clear unsupported/deprecated error.
- No unused lazy mode plumbing remains.
- CLI help and docs match runtime behavior.

title: Replace silent failures with explicit errors in declaration parsing
description:
internal/runner/declarations.go has silent failure patterns where malformed input is silently ignored:

- parseVarDecl() (lines 15-48): Returns nil, "", nil on malformed input instead of an explicit error. If len(parts) != 2, it silently skips the declaration.
- parseVarDeclFromLines() (lines 54-129): Same pattern — malformed declarations silently return len(declLines), nil.

Users get no feedback about why their variable declarations were ignored, making debugging difficult.

Suggested approach:
- Return descriptive errors for malformed declarations
- Include the line content and line number in error messages
- Consider a warning mechanism for soft failures (e.g., recoverable parse issues) vs hard errors (syntax that can't be interpreted)

title: Support DataWeave standard module imports in header (dw::core::* wiring)

title: Test: Add Unicode and special character edge case tests
description:
Issue: String functions lack comprehensive Unicode and special character testing

Missing test coverage:
1. Unicode strings (emoji, non-Latin scripts, combining characters)
2. Escape sequences (\n, \t, \u0000, etc.)
3. Regex with special characters  
4. CSV with quoted fields and embedded delimiters
5. XML/YAML with special entities and encodings
6. Line ending variations (LF, CRLF, CR)
7. Very long lines (1000+ characters)
8. Null bytes and binary data handling
9. Bidirectional text (RTL languages)
10. Case folding in different languages

Recommendation: Create string_edge_cases.feature with 20+ scenarios covering:
- Unicode normalization
- Regex edge cases
- Format-specific special characters
- Encoding/decoding edge cases

title: Handle single-quoted strings in structural scans
description: Structural scanners (stringState / findMatchingDelimited / scanBranchEnd / findUsingExpressionEnd / splitTopLevelArgs) only treat double-quoted strings as string literals. This can mis-parse input that uses single-quoted strings containing brackets or else/keywords, because these scans run before single-quote conversion. Update stringState (or pre-normalize) to treat single quotes as strings too, and add tests (e.g., using('a)') or if ('a)') else ...).

title: Critical: Add error handling for silent PrepareForParsing failures
description:
Files: internal/preprocessor/transformers_syntax.go and internal/evaluator/builtins_core.go

Multiple locations silently ignore errors from PrepareForParsing() using blank import:
- transformers_syntax.go lines 202, 231, 273, 396
- builtins_core.go similar locations

When preprocessing fails, the error is lost and could result in incorrect evaluation behavior. All PrepareForParsing() calls must be checked for errors and properly handled.

Example fix:
- Current: preparedExpr, _ := preprocessor.PrepareForParsing(...)
- Fixed: preparedExpr, err := preprocessor.PrepareForParsing(...); if err != nil { return ... }

title: Refactor XML reading/writing for better testability
description:
The readXML function in reader.go (50+ lines) and toXML function in writer.go (80+ lines) have complex nested logic for handling text nodes, attributes, and namespaces.

Consider:
- Extracting node type detection into helper functions
- Breaking up the traversal logic into separate functions for elements vs text nodes
- Creating a dedicated XML builder/formatter class
- Adding more focused unit tests for edge cases

title: Refactor: Centralize error message formatting
description: Issue: 240+ fmt.Sprintf calls for error messages scattered across codebase. Inconsistent wording. Create centralized error message package with templates for consistency and easier updates.

description: DataWeave allows multiple entries with the same key in an object, which is essential for XML output where multiple elements with the same name are common. Currently InfoMunge uses Go maps which overwrite duplicate keys.

description: Several files are very large and could benefit from splitting: rewriter_handlers.go (1096 lines), builtins_collection.go (1125 lines), builtins_core.go (845 lines). High cyclomatic complexity makes testing and review harder.

Split them into smaller, logically grouped files (e.g., builtins_string_transform.go, builtins_string_validation.go) to improve maintainability and navigability.

title: Support both mapObject parameter orders for DataWeave compatibility
description: DataWeave uses mapObject(value, key) but InfoMunge uses (key, value). Consider supporting both orders or making it configurable for easier migration.

title: mod() function result cannot be compared with ==
description: The mod() function returns a value that cannot be compared with == operator. Example: mod(4, 2) returns 0, but mod(4, 2) == 0 returns false. Similarly mod(5, 2) == 1 returns false. Division comparison works correctly ((4 / 2) == 2 returns true). This appears to be a type mismatch issue in the comparison.

title: Support 'match' keyword for pattern matching
description:
DataWeave 2.0 uses 'match' keyword for pattern matching. InfoMunge currently supports similar functionality but using 'case' directly (e.g., 'value case { ... }' instead of 'value match { case ... }').

For compatibility with DataWeave cookbook examples and user expectations, the 'match' keyword should be supported or an alias added.

Example failing script:
%im 0.1
output application/json
---
"hello" match {
  case is String -> "string"
  else -> "other"
}

title: __lazyReduce does not validate lambda arity
description:
Problem
- __lazyReduce accepts any lambda and does not validate param count.
- LazyReduce always binds two parameters; lambdas with fewer params lead to empty-string context keys and confusing behavior.

Impact
- Non-obvious runtime errors or incorrect results when users pass 0–1 param lambdas.

Evidence
- internal/evaluator/builtins_arrays.go:442-473 lacks param-count checks.
- internal/evaluator/lazy.go:189-194 unconditionally uses ParamName(0/1).

Proposed fix
- Mirror eager reduce validation: require 2–3 params and error otherwise.
- Add clear error messages with positional context.

Acceptance criteria
- __lazyReduce rejects lambdas with <2 params (and >3 if applicable).
- Error messages are consistent with eager reduce.
- Add a cucumber test for invalid lambda arity in lazy reduce.

title: Split evalIndex into separate functions per target type
description:
evaluator.go:555-686 — the evalIndex function is 131 lines handling 5+ distinct responsibilities in deeply nested switch statements:
- Array indexing (integer and string keys)
- String character indexing
- Object key access
- Presence selector (? suffix)
- Assert selector (! suffix)
- Metadata access
- Ordinal indexing

The ? and ! suffix logic is duplicated between array handling (lines 580-610) and object handling (lines 654-666).

Suggested approach:
- Extract evalArrayIndex(arr []interface{}, index interface{}, pos) (interface{}, error)
- Extract evalObjectIndex(obj map[string]interface{}, index interface{}, pos) (interface{}, error)
- Extract evalStringIndex(str string, index interface{}, pos) (interface{}, error)
- Extract a shared helper for presence/assert selector logic
- Keep evalIndex as a thin dispatcher
- Verify with existing evaluator tests

title: Add graceful shutdown and timeouts to HTTP server
description:
internal/cli/server.go lines 29-43: The serve() function calls server.ListenAndServe() with no timeouts, no graceful shutdown, and no signal handling. Long-running requests are never cancelled and there is no way to cleanly shut down the server.

Additionally, error handling in HTTP response writing (lines 65-67, 112-114) logs to stderr but doesn't properly handle partial writes.

title: Align object-iteration lambda semantics with DataWeave regardless parameter names
description:
Current behavior infers DataWeave order only when parameter names are exactly (value,key) or (v,k). For arbitrary names, mapObject/filterObject/pluck treat parameters as (key,value), which diverges from DataWeave.

Compatibility goal:
- DataWeave semantics should be applied independent of variable names for DataWeave-style object iteration lambdas.
- Preserve backward compatibility where possible without introducing a compatibility flag.

Implementation notes:
- Audit and update order handling in internal/evaluator/builtins_arrays_mapobject.go and internal/evaluator/builtins_collection_ops.go.
- Add deterministic disambiguation strategy where both legacy and DataWeave forms are accepted.
- Avoid name-based heuristics as the primary mechanism.

title: Simplify complex nested conditionals in parseHeader
description: internal/runner/runner.go:83-135 has deep nesting with multiple string prefix checks. Consider extracting to separate functions or using a more declarative parsing approach.

title: CLI input parameter support
description:
Implement the new CLI input parameter syntax as documented in README:

```bash
./infomunge -i payload <payload.json> "%im 1.0 output text/csv --- payload"
./infomunge -i payload <payload.json> -i input2 <input2.json> -f <infomungefile.im>
```

**New parameters:**
- `-i <name> <file>` - Named input file, parsed and injected as variable
- `-f <file>` - Read script from file instead of command line
- Inline script as final positional argument

**Requirements:**
- Multiple `-i` flags allowed for multiple named inputs
- Input files auto-detected by extension or explicit mime type
- Variables injected into script context before evaluation

title: Add -f flag for script file input
description:
Add support for `-f <file>` flag to read the infomunge script from a file.

**Usage:**
```bash
./infomunge -f script.im
```

**Implementation:**
1. Parse `-f` flag from command line
2. Read script content from specified file
3. Pass to runner for execution

This is the simplest new flag to implement as it replaces the current positional file argument.

title: Add inline script as positional argument
description:
Add support for passing the script as an inline string argument.

**Usage:**
```bash
./infomunge "%im 1.0 output application/json --- {name: \"test\"}"
```

**Implementation:**
1. If no `-f` flag, treat final positional argument as script content
2. Pass directly to runner.RunString() instead of reading from file

title: Add -i flag for named input files
description:
Add support for `-i <name> <file>` flag to provide named input data.

**Usage:**
```bash
./infomunge -i payload data.json -f script.im
./infomunge -i payload data.json -i users users.csv -f script.im
```

**Implementation:**
1. Parse `-i` flags (can appear multiple times)
2. For each input:
   - Read file content
   - Detect mime type from extension (.json, .xml, .csv, .yaml, .properties)
   - Parse content using formats.Read()
   - Add to context map with specified name
3. Pass populated context to runner

**Mime type detection:**
- .json -> application/json
- .xml -> application/xml
- .csv -> application/csv
- .yaml, .yml -> application/yaml
- .properties -> text/x-java-properties

title: Implement missing Numbers module functions (toBinary/fromBinary, radix conversions, etc.)
description: Implement missing dw::core::Numbers functions like toBinary/fromBinary and radix conversions. Add tests for each function.

title: Rewriter recursion triggered by string literals containing if("
description:
Problem
- Rewriter recursion is triggered by a raw substring check for "if (" or "if(" without excluding string literals or identifiers.

Impact
- Scripts with string literals containing "if(" can force extra rewrite passes and hit MaxRecursionDepth unexpectedly.
- Hard to diagnose since the input is semantically valid.

Evidence
- internal/preprocessor/preprocessor.go:164 checks strings.Contains(result, "if (") or "if(") to decide on recursion.

Proposed fix
- Use a scanner that skips strings/comments when detecting remaining if/else constructs.
- Alternatively, track whether handleIfElse made a rewrite pass and only recurse then.

Acceptance criteria
- String literals containing "if(" do not trigger extra rewrite passes.
- Legitimate nested if/else expressions still rewrite correctly.
- Add a test with a string literal containing "if(".

title: Improve preprocessor handling of multiline if/else
description: Handle multiline if/else blocks in function bodies without collapsing whitespace as a workaround.

title: Add XML test with XML declaration header
description:
Add a new test scenario to xml_reading.feature that tests XML parsing with a standard XML declaration:

```xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<user><name>Alice</name></user>
```

This verifies that the XML parser correctly handles the XML declaration line.

title: DW deviation: infomunge uses ** for exponentiation instead of pow()
description: DataWeave uses the pow() function for exponentiation, while infomunge uses the '**' operator (e.g., '2 ** 3'). To be fully DW-compatible, infomunge should support pow(base, exponent) as a builtin function. The ** operator can remain as infomunge-specific syntactic sugar.
close_reason: Already implemented: pow(base, exponent) builtin exists and math feature coverage passes

title: Server endpoint hardens error disclosure and input validation
description:
The server /run endpoint (cli/server.go) returns raw error messages to HTTP clients at lines 123, 129, 142, 148, 154. This can leak internal implementation details:
- File paths from module loading errors
- Internal code structure from evaluation errors
- System state from context cancellation errors

Additionally, the server has no limit on the number of inputs per request (handlers/run.go:84-104) and no character validation on input names (handlers/run.go:87-90), which could allow resource exhaustion or unexpected variable names downstream.

Recommended improvements:
1. Log full errors server-side, return generic messages for 5xx errors
2. For 4xx errors, sanitize error messages to remove internal paths
3. Add a max input count (e.g., 100 inputs per request)
4. Validate input names match identifier pattern (e.g., ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*$)
5. Return generic "Request timeout" for context cancellation instead of error details
close_reason: Hardened /run errors (sanitized 4xx, generic 5xx, generic timeout) and enforced max 100 request inputs

title: Add assignment expression support via __assign builtin
description: Implement assignment expressions to unblock while loops and enable variable mutations. The file test/features/lambda_expressions.feature contains many scenarios that only assert lambda representation (for example the step Then the output should contain a lambda function at lines 15, 38, 49, 60, 71, 82, 93, 104, 115, 126, 137, 148, 159, 170, 181, 192, 203, 214, 225, 236, 247, 258, 269, 280, 291, 303).

Parser or AST regressions in lambda bodies can pass while serialized lambda shape remains intact.

title: Refactor: Review and simplify cloneVisited usage in types.go

Issue: cloneVisited function only used once in types.go

Current state:
- Line 81: cloneVisited creates shallow copy of visited map for cycle detection
- Line 162: Only call to cloneVisited is in coerceToTypeWithVisited
- Pattern might be unnecessary complexity

Code location:
- internal/evaluator/types.go:81-90 (function definition)
- internal/evaluator/types.go:162 (single usage)

Investigation needed:
1. Is the visited map mutation causing issues that require cloning?
2. Can the recursion be restructured to avoid needing a copy?
3. Is the shallow copy sufficient, or does deep copy work better?
4. Can the pattern be simplified (e.g., pass parent reference)?

Recommendations:
1. Review the cycle detection logic in coerceToTypeWithVisited
2. Evaluate if the clone is truly necessary
3. Consider alternative approaches:
   - Pass parent visited map reference down
   - Use stack-based tracking instead of visited map
   - Restructure recursion to avoid mutation
4. Simplify or remove cloneVisited if possible

Low priority as the current implementation works, but cleanup could improve code clarity.

title: Fix determinism comparator false positives (NaN/lambda)
description:
## Problem
`internal/testing/mutation/deterministicallyEqual` treats semantically equal results as different in at least two cases:
- `NaN` values: `reflect.DeepEqual(math.NaN(), math.NaN())` is false and JSON marshalling fails for NaN, so equality returns false.
- Function/lambda values: fallback behavior differs from property tests and can drift.

This currently fails the mutation property test with a false nondeterminism signal:
- Mutated expression: `[(-4) ** 0.5][0]`
- First/second result are both `NaN`

## Evidence
- `internal/testing/mutation/mutation_test.go:199`
- `internal/testing/mutation/mutation_test.go:203`
- `internal/testing/mutation/mutation_test.go:205`
- `go test ./internal/... ./pkg/... ./cmd/...` failed in `TestMutatedCorpusExpressions_NoPanics_AndDeterministic` with `first=NaN second=NaN`.

## Impact
Property-based mutation testing emits false nondeterminism failures, reducing trust in the signal and slowing triage.

## Proposed fix
Implement a canonical deterministic comparator for test infrastructure that:
- Treats float NaN as equal to NaN for determinism checks.
- Handles lambdas/functions using semantic fields instead of pointer identity.
- Is shared by both mutation and property test suites.

## Acceptance criteria
- `TestMutatedCorpusExpressions_NoPanics_AndDeterministic` does not fail on same-NaN comparisons.
- Determinism comparator logic is not duplicated across `internal/testing/mutation` and `internal/testing/properties`.
- Add a focused test that proves NaN-vs-NaN is treated deterministic.

title: HTTP /run request body is unbounded (memory/CPU DoS risk)
description:
## Summary
The server decodes `/run` JSON bodies directly from `r.Body` without a size cap (`http.MaxBytesReader`), allowing arbitrarily large payloads.

## Impact
A client can send a very large body containing giant `script`/`inputs[*].content` strings and force excessive memory allocation and parse work, degrading or crashing the service.

## Evidence
- `internal/cli/server.go`: `payload, err := handlers.DecodeRunRequest(r.Body)`
- `internal/handlers/run.go`: `json.NewDecoder(body)` with no maximum byte limit
- No `Content-Length` enforcement or bounded reader before decode

## Expected
- Wrap body with `http.MaxBytesReader` (or equivalent limit) before decode.
- Return `413 Payload Too Large` when limit exceeded.
- Optionally enforce per-field limits (`script`, each input `content`) for defense in depth.

Deduplicate lambda-body scanning in preprocessor
description:
## Problem
Lambda-body scanning logic is duplicated with subtle divergence risk across preprocessors:
- `scanLambdaBody(...)` in `transformers_lambda.go`
- inline depth/string/group scan loop in `replaceCollectionOperator(...)` in `transformers_collection.go`

Both implement very similar bracket-depth/string-aware termination behavior.

## Evidence
- `internal/preprocessor/transformers_lambda.go:169`
- `internal/preprocessor/transformers_collection.go:103`

## Impact
Parser fixes in one scan path can regress the other path, increasing maintenance cost and chance of syntax edge-case drift.

## Proposed simplification
Extract a shared scanner utility for "find lambda/body end with depth + string awareness" and consume it in both sites.

## Acceptance criteria
- A single shared scan helper is used by both implicit-lambda rewrite and collection-operator rewrite.
- Existing behavior for nested groups, strings, and operator boundaries remains covered by tests.
- Add at least one regression test that would have failed if the two paths diverge.

Examples of vacuous patterns to look for:
- Tests where the expected output is trivially derived from the input (e.g. identity transforms)
- Tests that pass due to lenient error handling rather than correct behavior
- Scenarios where the 'Then' assertion is too weak to catch regressions (e.g. only checking for no error, not checking the actual output value)
- Tests that exercise the test harness more than the infomunge pipeline
- Duplicate scenarios that test the same code path with superficially different inputs
- Scenarios where the expression is evaluated but the result is never meaningfully validated

Deliverable: a report (or set of sub-issues) identifying specific vacuous scenarios with recommendations — tighten the assertion, remove the scenario, or replace it with a more meaningful one.

title: Add regex literal syntax support (/pattern/)
description:
The preprocessor doesn't handle DataWeave regex literal syntax (/pattern/). Currently regex functions like match, matches, scan, contains, find, splitBy, and replace work with string patterns but not with regex literals.

Example that fails:
```
%dw 2.0
var myString = "mycompany.com"
output application/json
---
{
  "contains" : myString contains(/c.m/),
  "find" : myString find(/[m|n].|m$/),
  "match" : myString match(/([a-z]*).[a-z]*/),
  "matches" : myString matches(/([a-z]*).[a-z]*/),
  "replaceWith" : myString replace /\..*m/ with ".net",
  "scan" : myString scan(/([a-z]*).(com)/),
  "splitBy" : myString splitBy(/[.\/]/)
}
```

Error: "6:24: missing ',' in composite literal (and 3 more errors)"

Implementation needed:
1. Add early preprocessing stage to convert /pattern/ literals to string literals
2. Handle escaping properly (forward slashes, backslashes)
3. Consider regex flags (e.g., /pattern/i for case-insensitive)
4. The replace operator with regex also needs support: `replace /pattern/ with "replacement"`

title: Centralize header directive parsing logic
description:
Parsing logic for header directives (var, fun, type, ns, import) is currently split between internal/runner/runner.go, internal/runner/declarations.go, and some parts of internal/evaluator. 

The runner's directiveRegistrations should be more robust and handle multiline parsing in a more unified way, rather than having specific hacks for fun and var. This would make the runner cleaner and easier to extend with new directives.

title: Support do-block separators in module files
description: Module files reject any top-level '---' today. Evaluate whether do-block '---' separators should be allowed inside module function bodies, and if so update module parsing to allow them and add cucumber coverage.

title: Extract string processing utilities
description: Extract common string replacement patterns from transformers_base.go to dedicated stringutils package. The replaceOperatorsOutsideStrings and binary operator replacement logic are repeated and could be reused. This will reduce code duplication in preprocessor package.

title: Refactor: Replace switch registry with map-based lookup
description: Issue: Large switch statements in modular_registry.go - GetBuiltinSpecial (73 cases) and GetBuiltinFunction (115+ cases). O(n) lookup. Use map for O(1) lookup and easier maintenance.

title: Unify format option dispatch for reader/writer
description:
## Problem
Read/write option dispatch for format-specific handlers is duplicated and manually synchronized:
- `ReadWithOptions` switch in `pkg/formats/reader.go`
- `FormatWithOptions` switch in `pkg/formats/writer.go`

Both contain repeated MIME alias handling and near-identical unsupported-options behavior.

## Evidence
- `pkg/formats/reader.go:21`
- `pkg/formats/writer.go:22`

## Impact
Higher maintenance overhead and increased risk of drift when adding new option-enabled formats.

## Proposed simplification
Introduce a shared option-dispatch registry for option-capable formats (with aliases), so read/write paths share common MIME normalization and capability checks.

## Acceptance criteria
- Option capability and MIME alias mapping is defined once and reused by read/write dispatch.
- Behavior for unsupported options remains unchanged (same error semantics).
- Add unit tests showing one alias pair routes identically for both read and write paths.

title: Implement timeout detection in while loops
description: The infinite loop test expects a 1-second timeout to catch the loop, but the while loop completes all 1M iterations before the timeout. Need to implement time-based checks in the loop to allow proper timeout handling. Consider using time.Sleep(0) or checking elapsed time periodically.

comments.author: david
comments.text: Key insight: The previous implementation using runtime.Gosched() and a 1M iteration limit wasn't effective because the loop was so fast (~90ms for 1M iterations) that it completed before the 1-second timeout could fire. The fix checks elapsed time every 100 iterations against a deadline, returning a timeout error when exceeded. This also required fixing break/continue to use labeled break - the original code only broke out of the switch statement, not the enclosing for loop.

title: Refactor: Extract common type assertion patterns
description: Issue: Type assertion patterns repeated across builtin functions. Common patterns like assertArg with beArray() should be used more consistently. Create generic type assertion helpers with consistent error messages.

title: Test: Add cucumber tests for math functions (floor, round, abs, pow)
description:
Add cucumber tests for these math builtin functions that lack test coverage:
- floor: Round down to nearest integer
- round: Round to nearest integer
- abs: Absolute value
- pow: Power/exponentiation

Should include edge cases like negative numbers, zero, floating point precision.

title: Test: Expand JSON/XML/YAML/CSV input format test coverage
description:
Issue: Input format tests have minimal coverage compared to core features

Current state:
- json_reading.feature: 1 scenario  
- xml_reading.feature: 7 scenarios
- yaml_reading.feature: 1 scenario
- csv_reading.feature: 4 scenarios

Compare to:
- lambda_expressions.feature: 29 scenarios
- date_time_functions.feature: 61 scenarios
- aggregation_functions.feature: 33 scenarios

Recommendation: Each format should have 15-25 core scenarios covering:
1. Simple/complex data parsing
2. Edge cases (empty, null, nested)
3. Type conversions during read
4. Error handling (malformed input, encoding issues)
5. Large payloads
6. Format-specific features (namespaces in XML, multiple docs in YAML, etc.)

Priority: Create comprehensive test suite for each format to match feature parity.

title: Implement assignment and control flow for While loops
description: Address blocking TODOs in docs/WHILE_LOOPS.md. Specifically: 1. Support assignment expressions within loops. 2. Implement break/continue control flow signals. These are required for full while loop functionality.

title: match operator times out
description: The match operator (and matches builtin function) causes an infinite loop or timeout. Example: "hello" match "h" should return true but hangs instead. This affects the regex test scenarios in string_edge_cases.feature.

title: CSV formatting silently falls back to JSON and skips non-object rows
description:
Problem
- formatCSV falls back to JSON for non-array inputs and for arrays that contain no object elements.
- Non-object items in the array are silently skipped.

Impact
- Output format becomes unpredictable (CSV vs JSON).
- Data loss when non-object elements are dropped without error.

Evidence
- pkg/formats/csv.go:74-85 fallback to JSON if result is not Array.
- pkg/formats/csv.go:91-127 skip non-object items and return JSON if headerSet is empty.

Proposed fix
- Decide a single, explicit behavior: either error on unsupported input or coerce in a well-defined way.
- If skipping non-object elements is intended, log/return warnings or document it.

Acceptance criteria
- CSV formatting behavior is explicit and documented.
- No silent data loss; errors or deterministic coercion for non-object rows.
- Add tests for mixed arrays and non-array input.

title: Add bracket/stack invariants asserts in preprocessor rewrite
description: Add assertions for stack underflow/mismatched braces and negative depth in rewriter handlers (handleCloseBrace, findBranches, single-quote handling) to catch malformed syntax early.

title: Ensure CLI command works with payload input and file
<< prepend operator causes infinite loop/hang

title: Fix ignored errors in server and evaluator

title: Critical: Remove panic from Result[T].Value()
description:
File: pkg/formats/types.go, Line 48

The Result[T].Value() method calls panic directly on error, which crashes the entire application when the method is misused. This is dangerous in library code.

Current code:
panic("called Value() on error result: " + r.err.Error())

Fix: Should return (T, error) or require users to use Unwrap()/OrElse() before calling Value(). This prevents application crashes from library misuse.

title: Inconsistent backslash escape checking across preprocessor
description:
Multiple locations use the simple pattern s[i-1] != '\\' to check for escaped quotes, but this fails for sequences like \\\" (escaped backslash before quote). The ScanState.isEscapedAt method handles this correctly by counting consecutive backslashes, but these inline checks do not:

- transformers_lambda.go:164 
- transformers_regex.go:66-67, 76-77, 417
- stringutils/scanner.go:128, 178 (SubstringUntilDepth)

Should use a shared helper that counts consecutive backslashes.

title: Support top-level object literal without braces (DataWeave style)
Cucumber coverage: core evaluator paths

Add cucumber scenarios for core evaluator paths in evaluator.go with 0% coverage. 35 functions uncovered including: subtraction operator (sub), logical OR (lor), error formatting (FormatEvalError partial at 20%, FormatParseError at 0%), offsetToLineCol, ParamNames, GetDefault, MarshalJSON, and EvaluateWithContext. Lines 1-172 of internal/runner/module_loader.go and internal/runner/module_loader_js.go are nearly identical. The duplicated code includes:

title: Rewriter iteration guard rejects long scripts and mislabels as infinite loop
description:
Problem
- The rewriter uses a single iterCount guard tied to input length. Any input longer than MaxRewriteIterations (10k) triggers an "infinite loop" error even when processing is linear.

Impact
- Large scripts fail with misleading errors.
- The error suggests a logic bug when the real issue is input size vs. guard value.

Evidence
- internal/preprocessor/preprocessor.go:72-76 increments iterCount per character and errors when iterCount > MaxRewriteIterations.

Proposed fix
- Replace the guard with a more accurate loop-detection mechanism, or make MaxRewriteIterations scale with input length.
- Update error message to reflect input-length guard, not infinite loop.

Acceptance criteria
- Scripts >10k bytes do not fail unless there is an actual rewrite loop.
- Error messages accurately describe the failure condition.
- Add a regression test with large input.

title: Module import path traversal allows loading .im files outside BaseDir
description:
## Summary
`ModuleLoader.Resolve` joins raw module spec segments directly with `filepath.Join` and does not reject `..` traversal or enforce a `BaseDir` boundary.

## Impact
Any script executed by the HTTP server can import arbitrary `.im` files from outside the repository working tree (for example `/tmp/*.im`), enabling unintended local file inclusion and code execution from attacker-controlled locations.

## Evidence
- `internal/runner/module_loader.go`: `parts := strings.Split(moduleSpec, "::")` and `relPath := filepath.Join(parts...) + ".im"`
- No `filepath.Clean` + prefix/boundary check against `BaseDir`

## Reproduction
1. Create `/tmp/evil.im`:
   `%im 0.1`
   `var x = 42`
2. Run:
   `go run ./cmd/infomunge/main.go "%im 0.1
import ..::..::..::..::..::..::tmp::evil
output application/json
---
evil.x"`
3. The script resolves and evaluates to `42`, proving module loading escaped the repository base directory.

## Expected
- Reject module specs containing traversal segments (e.g., `..`).
- Canonicalize resolved path and ensure it remains under an allowed root (prefer `modules/` only).
- Return a parse/validation error when a module escapes the boundary.

title: Make string concatenation with lambdas deterministic
description:
## Problem
String concatenation uses `fmt.Sprintf("%v", value)` for non-string operands in `add()`. For lambda/function values, `%v` includes pointer addresses, which vary across evaluations and produce nondeterministic strings.

## Evidence
- `internal/evaluator/evaluator.go:318`
- `internal/evaluator/evaluator.go:322`
- Property test failure example:
  - Expression: `payload.age + (elem) -> 0`
  - First result: `"clwbe&{... 0x...}"`
  - Second result: `"clwbe&{... 0x...}"` (different pointer)

## Impact
Runtime output can be nondeterministic when concatenating strings with lambda values. This is user-visible behavior and also destabilizes deterministic test invariants.

## Proposed fix
Use a stable string coercion function for evaluator values (especially lambda/function), instead of raw `%v`.
- For lambdas, stringify by signature/body metadata (or a stable placeholder such as `"<function>"`).
- Reuse that coercion in both `string + any` and `any + string` paths.

## Acceptance criteria
- Repeated evaluation of expressions concatenating string and lambda produce byte-identical output.
- Add cucumber coverage for a deterministic concatenation case involving lambdas.
- Existing string concatenation behavior for primitive values is preserved.

title: Refactor tests to use docstring inputs instead of read()

**Current pattern:**
```gherkin

  output application/json
  ---
  read("<user><name>Alice</name></user>", "application/xml")
  """
```

**Target pattern:**
```gherkin
Given the following XML input:
  """
  <user><name>Alice</name></user>
  """
And the following script:
  """
  %im 1.0
  output application/json
  ---
  payload
  """
```

**Benefits:**
- Multiline input data is more readable
- Avoids escaping issues in strings
- Separates data from transformation logic
- Easier to add complex test cases

## Summary
Increase in-process cucumber coverage for `internal/runner` output-formatting paths that currently execute mostly through external CLI calls.

title: Off-by-one in handleDoBlock/handleUpdateExprBlock brace content slicing
description:
In rewriter_handlers.go, handleDoBlock (line 493) and handleUpdateExprBlock (line 524) use braceEnd-1 when slicing content between braces:
  content := r.input[braceStart+1 : braceEnd-1]

But findMatchingDelimited returns braceEnd as the position of the closing brace itself (line 674: endPos = pos - 1). So the correct slice to get content between braces exclusive is:
  r.input[braceStart+1 : braceEnd]

Using braceEnd-1 drops the last character before the closing brace. Line 848 (tryRewriteConditionalObjectLiteral) correctly uses braceEnd without the -1.

This is a latent bug: it does not manifest in practice because there is usually whitespace (newline) before the closing brace, so the dropped character is insignificant whitespace that gets trimmed. But it would cause incorrect parsing for tightly-formatted blocks like do {x---y}.

Fix: Change lines 493 and 524 to use braceEnd instead of braceEnd-1.
